body_text: Hi, So we're trying to build a user facing app that will be fed DOMO data. In particular its a chatbot that will be able to query and read in DOMO data for user insights and actionable recommendations. The issue we're facing is, each of our users have particular data policies and these policies are encapsulated in a PDP that is attached to the dataset. When the user requests a view of the data we want that user to be able to only view data that is defined in these policies. The dataset api doesnt appear to restrict the view of the data per user via the parameters but rather when say the pydomo client is instantiated the views are inherited via whatever policy is attached to the client id and client secret. Is there a way to get a user of our app to only see the data the would see in the DOMO dashboards? Or do we have to reimplement the PDPs on our backend?
title: Inheriting PDP policies for a given user when querying the dataset?

body_text: Stop wasting time navigating menus, managing hundreds of identical browser tabs, copying dataset IDs from the URL, and constantly clearing your cookies. Domo Toolkit is designed for the people who live inside Domo every day—administrators managing hundreds of objects, consultants jumping between client instances, and power users building on the platform. Every feature is built to save clicks, reduce context-switching, and surface information that Domo's native UI buries. Whether you're creating, updating, troubleshooting, auditing, or cleaning, Domo Toolkit puts the tools you need one click away. Installation Disclaimer This extension is an independent, community-developed project. Domo, Inc. has no responsibility for its functionality or performance or for any consequences arising from its use. Features Context Detection Automatically detects the Domo object you're viewing - pages, cards, datasets, dataflows, app studio pages, workflows, alerts, and 100+ other object types. The extension: Identifies the object and fetches metadata from the Domo API Detects card modals and resolves parent objects for nested types (e.g. app studio pages) Detects selected code engine and form actions inside workflow editors Updates the tab title with the object's name Provides one-click access to the object's full JSON definition, with epoch timestamps annotated as human-readable dates and user IDs annotated with display names Automatic 431 Error Resolving Handles Domo's "Request Header Fields Too Large" errors with three cookie clearing modes: Auto (default) - Detects 431 errors, clears cookies (preserving your last 2 active instances), and refreshes the page automatically Preserve - One-click clearing that keeps your last 2 instances All - Clears all Domo cookies while leaving other sites and history intact One-Click Actions Copy ID - Copy the current object's ID. Long-press for related IDs like stream ID (datasets) or app ID (app studio pages). Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl+Shift+1 ( Cmd+Shift+1 on Mac). Share With Self - Grant yourself access to pages, studio apps, and custom app designs. Activity Log - View activity log records for the current object. Long-press for advanced options: view activity for all cards on the current object, all pages containing those cards, or all child pages. Clipboard Navigation - Click this button to read your clipboard, identify the Domo object only by its ID on your clipboard, and navigate directly to it. Works with any Domo object ID copied from anywhere - a card, dataset, spreadsheet, Slack message, etc. For objects that don't support navigation, detailed information is displayed in the side panel instead. Delete Current Object - Delete beast modes, appdb collections, workflows, pages/app studio pages and all their cards, and dataflows and all their outputs. Includes confirmation dialog and child page safety checks. Data Discovery Opens in the side panel for persistent exploration without losing your place. Get Cards - Lists every card on a page, app studio page, worksheet page, report builder page, dataset, or dataflow outputs. For pages, forms and queues are included and separated from cards. Get Card Pages - Shows where cards on an object live. For pages, shows all other pages not including the current page that contain cards that also exist on the current page. For datasets and dataflows, shows all pages and app studio pages containing cards that use the dataset or dataflow outputs as a source. Get Child Pages - For pages, shows all child and grandchild pages. Get DataSets - Shows datasets for an object, including inputs and outputs datasets for dataflows, dependent views for datasets, and all datasets used in cards on a page or app. Get DataSets Used in View - For dataset views and datafusions, see the underlying source datasets that feed into the view. All discovery lists support applicable actions like open all, copy ID, share with self, open lineage, open in views explorer, and remove from page. Items are grouped hierarchically or categorically with expand/collapse, counts, direct links, and IDs on hover. Card Error Tracking Card API errors are automatically captured as you browse. Click the Card Errors button to view them in the side panel with full response details. Errors are tracked per tab and cleared when you navigate away from a card. View error count at a glance, expand individual errors to see the full JSON response, and clear all errors with one click. Object-Specific Actions Lineage - Open a full-page lineage graph for datasets and dataflows. Traces upstream and downstream dependencies with dataset previews and dataflow tile operations directly in the graph. Supports dark mode. Copy Filtered URL - Copy URL with all applied filters on a card, page, or app studio page (Pfilters). Export Data - Export card data in CSV or Excel format, including applied filters (can be done from a card modal!). Export code engine package versions as JavaScript/Python files. Data Repair - Open the hidden data repair tab for any dataset. Update Owner - Change ownership of alerts and workflows with a searchable user picker and a "Set to Self" shortcut. Update DataFlow Details - Edit a dataflow's name and description without creating a new version. Update Code Engine Versions - Bulk update workflow code engine actions to the latest version in a single click, without unmapping inputs and outputs. Lock Cards - Lock all cards on a page, app studio page, dataset, worksheet, report builder report, or all dataflow outputs. Set DataSet Schedule to Manual - Set a dataset's schedule to manual. Fix Empty String Filters - Remove empty string default values from "contains" quick filters on cards, so null values display when no value is entered instead of being filtered out. Custom Favicons Customize favicons per Domo instance using regex-based rules: Instance Logo - Use the instance's own logo as the favicon Colored Domo Logo - Custom background color on the Domo logo Colored Stripes - Add a colored stripe to the top, right, bottom, or left edge Regex Patterns - Match instance subdomains with flexible patterns Priority Ordering - Drag-and-drop rule ordering Side Panel & Popup Popup - Click the extension icon for quick access Side Panel - Persistent panel alongside the page for data discovery, with collapsible actions. Opens automatically from the popup when displaying discovery results. Both show the current context (instance, object type, object ID) and update as you navigate. Settings Theme - System, light, or dark mode Default Domo Instance - Set your go-to instance for clipboard navigation from non-Domo sites Cookie Clearing Behavior - Choose between auto, preserve, or all modes Favicon Rules - Rule editor with pattern matching, effect selection, color picker, and drag-and-drop reordering Supported Object Types Pages, cards, datasets, dataflows, app studio apps (and their pages), worksheets (and their pages), workspaces, users, groups, alerts, workflows (including versions, executions, triggers, and actions), code engine packages (and versions), pro-code apps, beast modes, variables, access tokens, appdb collections, approvals, approval templates, jupyter workspaces, filesets, files, forms, governance toolkit jobs and dozens more. Privacy Only runs on .domo.com domains Uses Domo's existing authenticated session - no additional login required No data leaves the browser; no external servers are contacted Settings sync via Chrome's built-in storage Domo data is never read, stored, or sent off-device See the full Privacy Policy for details. Contributing Interested in contributing? See CONTRIBUTING for the tech stack, architecture, development setup, code conventions, and key patterns. Issues & Feedback Found a bug or have a feature request? Open an issue .
title: Work Smarter, Not Harder - Introducing the Domo Toolkit Chrome Extension

body_text: Currently, the Sage Intacct REST Connector in Domo supports only standard objects available through the Intacct REST API. However, many customers rely heavily on custom or saved reports within Sage Intacct for their business workflows. The Sage Intacct REST API documentation indicates that it is possible to access report data via API endpoints. Enabling support for custom reports within the Domo connector would significantly enhance its functionality and provide a smoother transition from the legacy connector, which previously supported this capability. Business Impact: Customers migrating from the legacy Sage Intacct connector are losing access to critical custom reports Rebuilding complex reports using standard objects and ETL processes requires additional time and effort Limits adoption of the new REST connector due to missing parity with previous functionality Requested Enhancement: Add support in the Sage Intacct REST Connector to: Retrieve custom/saved reports via available REST API endpoints Allow users to select and import custom reports similarly to the legacy connector Additional Context: This feature would greatly improve usability and reduce migration friction as the legacy connector is being deprecated. It would also align the connector more closely with the capabilities offered by the Sage Intacct API.
title: Custom Reports in Sage Intacct REST Connector

body_text: Hi everyone, I am excited to announce the release of the Datasource Swapper ! Whether you are building new datasets because you are moving to a new data provider, transitioning away from materialized datasets in favor of Cloud Amplifier, or dealing with forced changes caused by vendor API deprecations, this tool was created to help save you hours of tedious manual updates to move your existing content to your shiny new datasets. You can read more about this custom tool and get a step-by-step guide to create and run this in your instance here: https://embed.domo.com/embed/pages/8E1vl The Datasource Swapper is designed to accelerate large-scale migrations by allowing you to re-map content in bulk. Instead of opening every dataset yourself and updating each piece of content, you can provide a simple mapping dataset to this tool and let it handle the heavy lifting. Key Functionality & Features: Bulk Dataset Swapping: Automatically update the input datasource for Cards, Dataset Views, and Magic ETL Dataflows across your Domo instance. Mapping-Driven Automation: Uses DomoStats and a simple "Old ID to New ID" mapping to identify and update all dependent assets for any given dataset in one go. Proactive Schema Validation: Before committing changes, the tool checks for missing columns or data type mismatches in the target dataset, allowing you to skip problematic pairs or proceed with full visibility. Flexible Deployment: Choose the environment that fits your workflow — deploy it as an integrated Pro-Code App using CodeEngine or utilize the standalone JavaScript-based CLI tool for a local experience. This tool is perfect for Domo Instance Administrators who are tasked with maintaining instance health during structural data changes. Because it requires the ability to deploy CodeEngine packages, create custom Pro-Code apps, and modify instance-wide content, it is most effective when run by an Administrator or a user with elevated permissions and widespread access to update content. You can dive into the step-by-step implementation guide and access the code here: https://embed.domo.com/embed/pages/8E1vl Happy migrating!
title: Announcing the Datasource Swapper: Move your existing Cards, Views, and ETLs to new datasets in bulk

body_text: Ever wish you could easily delete a Beast Mode from the Beast Mode Manager? Or click a button to delete all cards on a page before deleting the page? Well now you can with bookmarklets! If you aren't familiar with bookmarklets (sometimes called favelets), they are browser bookmarks that run JavaScript code when clicked. I recently made the discovery that they also support fetch API calls, which unlocked a world of possibilities for Domo-centered scripts. I wanted to share this discovery with the community and hope you will take it to new heights with your own scripts. But, I've developed a few and added them to GitHub to get everyone started: https://github.com/brycewc/domo-bookmarklets Best part is, they don't need to be modified before use as they inherit authentication from your browser session and are built to dynamically adjust to the Domo instance you are viewing. In the repository, they are stored as beautified JavaScript. But the repository includes instructions to sync them all to your favorites bar and convert them to bookmarklets (which are minified and URL encoded). Alternatively, you can use something like the Bookmarkletify VS Code extension or an online service to convert them and add them to your bookmarks manually. If you don't have the skills to build your own, comment here or open a discussion on the GitHub repository for scripts you'd like to see and I'll build them. And if you build some cool ones yourself, I hope you'll share them by submitting a pull request to the repository.

body_text: Say I have a dataset "Current Headcount" (45 rows) shows me a current headcounts by stores, updates everyday. Someone asked if they can see the headcounts month to month? So basically a historical headcounts. - which is possible if I take a snapshot of the "Current Headcount" dataset at every month end and appending one on another → Call this "Historical Headcount" - snapshot can be created using Recursive ETL or Dataset Copy or SQL DataFlow . I am unsure which one to use. Additional question is: Can create a dataset that has both current as of today headcount & historical month end headcount on the same dataset - I think it possible by union "Current Headcount" dataset on top of "Historical Headcount" using view. - However possible issues: On the last date of the month, there will be duplicate data. How to prevent?
title: Month End Snapshot & Current as of today on the same dataset, is it possible?

body_text: Yes, I'd recommend using the Dataset Copy with Append update method. This will update the dataset every month and automatically give you a timestamp (BATCH_LAST_RUN). You could use an ETL to union these two datasets together and have a column to state "Current" or "Historical" and trigger it to run on your historical dataset update then just filter out the latest record (highest batch_id) from historical in your ETL.
title: Month End Snapshot & Current as of today on the same dataset, is it possible?

body_text: If you have start/end dates for employees (common fields from HR systems), I would suggest a different approach. Let's say I have this fake data: I could join that to the calendar data set, using the 1st of each month of interest. Filter: Join: (end date is higher than the month's start date (or if it's blank, a randomly high end date)) and start date is less than the month's start date). That gives me a new dataset with all the months where an employee was a current employee: Then I can just count Employee ID by month. My final month is the current number of employees: You could also add a summary number of the total number of current employees: You might want to play with the join in the ETL. For example, if you want mid-month hires to show up in the counts for that month (as opposed to in the next month), you might want to tweak it.
title: Month End Snapshot & Current as of today on the same dataset, is it possible?

body_text: Hi @Pari , You can replace these values using the below formula in a Magic ETL Formula tile. This will resolve the tooltip inconsistent behavior. REPLACE( Original Value , '''', '’') This replaces the standard apostrophe (') with a Unicode apostrophe (’). In some charts, the tooltip renderer encodes the standard apostrophe as ' , which causes it to appear differently in tooltips compared to axis labels. Using the Unicode apostrophe avoids this encoding and ensures consistent display across the visualization. I hope this will be helpful

body_text: I am trying to join form responses on a dataset to update the approval status of some journal entries, but don't want to create a completely new dataset. There are cards built to show statuses based on the input dataset, so the idea is that the form responses approving the entries would just update the status instead of building another dataset.
title: Can output dataset be the same as an input/existing dataset in Magic?

body_text: You can have an output dataset be the same as the input, in a recursive ETL but you cannot have the output be an existing dataset. For what you’re trying to do, it would require repointing your cards to a new dataset. If you navigate to the dataset overview, then click on the Cards Powered tile there will be an option to switch the cards to a different dataset. I'd recommend copying over any beast modes to the new dataset first to ease the transition. If this is an issue you think you’ll encounter often you may want to consider using a view as your final dataset layer and point all of your cards to the view. Then when you need to switch datasets you’d simply change the source of the view without disturbing the existing cards.
title: Can output dataset be the same as an input/existing dataset in Magic?

body_text: Looking for any tips on best functionality for rendering a AppDB Brick via Apps and specifically have it behave smoothly from an iPad via the mobile app. Curently what I'm noticing is when I rotate the screen it "resets". title: Pro Code in Apps Mobile Rendering Tips?

body_text: Hi @Sean _moore21, this is expected one. iPad rotation triggers a re-render, so your AppDB Brick reloads and loses in-session state. Try keeping state tied to controls or datasets instead of temporary variables. Avoid triggering queries on every render, cache or pre-load where possible. Simplify layouts and reduce conditional rendering tied to screen size. And since Claude’s already been your coding partner, might as well put it back to work on these tweaks 🙂

body_text: I have just finished creating and deploying my first workflow. It's doing what I need it to do. I'm struggling to figure out how to consistently get workflow completion notifications to who I need to get them. I am one of several admins. We are all in the "Domo Admin" group. I have given the group Admin access to the workflow. The only notification settings I can find for workflows are personal settings (annoying but I can tell others to set them up). But none of the settings will work. It is being started by and alert so the "you started" options won't work. And the "you own" options don't seem to work because there is no "owner". Only creator and contributor set as me and unchangeable. So next path, setting up and email task in the workflow. Well after digging through a bunch of functions I landed on the Workflow Executions function. Technically I could get everything I needed, but if the workflow fails the Email task would never get triggered. Meaning I would only get the emails on success, not failure. Pivot again. Found the DomoStats: Workflows dataset. Ok cool. I can just setup and alert for when a new row is added. I can even split things. Completion/Success just to me. Failures to the entire group. Cool. Except I only can run once a day (this is fine for normal days). I need it to update anytime the workflow runs. So add a task to run the dataset. Cool, except once again, if the workflow fails, it just stops. Meaning no trigger for failed workflow except to me. If this workflow fails I need to know asap so the tasks can be manually triggered. I'm about to leave the country for 11 days. I need other people to be able to get alerts. Is my only option to set up a rule in Outlook to forward any failures?
title: Workflow Notifications

body_text: Thank you for taking the time to share this and for outlining the challenge so clearly. We understand how important it is to have flexible notifications into workflow failures, and you’re not alone in running into this limitation. As you discovered, there currently are not options for increasing the frequency of DomoStats and the existing workflow notifications are somewhat restrictive. We recognize this is not ideal when you need ensure other are aware of potential execution failures. Your idea of forwarding notifications for failed workflows is a smart and practical workaround, and likely the best option available for your specific situation right now. That said, I want you to know this is an area we’re looking to improve within the product. Enhancing workflow notifications and flexibility is on our backlog, and we’re collaborating with our development team to better support scenarios like yours in a future update. Thanks again for your post. it helps us prioritize the right improvements.
title: Workflow Notifications

body_text: Snowflake will be discontinuing the use of username and passwords for authentication. This means that any Snowflake connectors using this type of connection will need to be migrated to either an OAuth version or a Key Pair version of the connector. The list of connectors that will need to be migrated include the following: Snowflake Snowflake Unload Snowflake Unload V2 Snowflake Managed Unload Snowflake High Bandwidth with Advanced Partitions Snowflake Partition Connector Snowflake Writeback Connectors MUST be either migrated or disabled by May 4th 2026. After this date these connectors will no longer work and will begin throwing errors if not disabled or migrated. To insure that your connectors are able to be migrated before the cutoff date, it is recommended that you submit your migration requests to support before April 1st 2026. This will help make the migration process smoother and help prevent any disruptions to your data. body_text: Currently, when triggering a publication refresh in Domo, the process must run to completion once started. There is no option to pause, cancel, or abort an in-progress refresh job. According to Domo documentation, users can initiate and monitor publication refreshes, but there is no control to stop a job once it has started. This creates challenges in real-world scenarios where: Refresh jobs can take a long time depending on the number of datasets, dashboards, and subscribers. A refresh may be triggered accidentally or at an inconvenient time. Issues are identified mid-refresh (e.g., incorrect content, missing datasets, or configuration errors). Users want to avoid unnecessary processing or system load. Proposed Enhancement Introduce the ability to: Cancel or abort an ongoing publication refresh Optionally pause and resume refresh jobs Provide clear status feedback when a job is stopped Business Impact This enhancement would: Improve operational control and flexibility Reduce unnecessary compute/resource usage Prevent propagation of incorrect or incomplete content to subscriber instances Enhance user experience when managing large or complex publications
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Ability to Cancel or Stop Publication Refresh Jobs

body_text: We are embedding Domo table cards on a client-facing website as static, read-only snapshots of data. In our use case we have a table that displays a fixed list of data in a specific order, and there is no reason for an end user to sort, filter, or copy the data. Allowing them to do so actually breaks the intentional row order we have set up. We turned off every available setting at both the card level and the dashboard level and the Sort/Filter/Copy context menu still appears whenever a user clicks a column header. This happens both within the Domo platform and in the embedded iframe on our website, so it is not an embed-specific issue. We reached out to Domo support and were told this behavior cannot be suppressed regardless of the settings selected, and were directed here to submit a feature request. Our ask is simple: if a card creator has explicitly turned off all sorting and filtering settings, the Sort/Filter/Copy context menu should not appear. There should be a way to make a table card fully static and non-interactive, particularly for embedded use cases. This feels like a bug more than a missing feature since the existing settings imply that interaction can be disabled, but the context menu appears regardless.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Allow full suppression of Sort/Filter/Copy context menu on table cards

body_text: What is happening? Microsoft is retiring the IDCFL/WS-Trust authentication method that Domo's legacy SharePoint connector ( com.domo.connector.microsoft.sharepoint.online ) uses on May 1st 2026. While Microsoft has supported this authentication method for several years after its deprecation, support is now ending. See Microsoft's announcement and schedule for more information. What is the impact on customers? Datasets powered by the legacy SharePoint connector will begin failing with authentication errors once Microsoft retires this authentication method, which is scheduled for May 1st 2026. What action do customers need to take? If customers no longer need this data: No action is required, though Domo recommends disabling dataset updates to prevent error notifications. If customers still need SharePoint data: Customers who still need their Sharepoint data will need to: Recreate their datasets using the SharePoint Online REST connector Update any downstream assets that depend on these datasets Note: The legacy connector's API cannot be directly mapped to Microsoft's REST API, so datasets cannot be automatically migrated. Why can't Domo simply update the authentication method that the connector uses? The legacy connector's underlying API doesn't support Microsoft's current authentication methods, making an update technically infeasible. Will Domo's OneDrive connectors be affected? No. Domo's OneDrive connectors use a different authentication method and are not impacted by this change.
title: Legacy Sharepoint connector retirement

body_text: Thanks for this announcement @Tasleema . Much appreciated.
title: Legacy Sharepoint connector retirement

body_text: Any help on this would be appreciated, I can't seem to get rid of this error and I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong or what I need to check. I'm duplicating an ETL we currently use for a similar dataset, but this dataset is separated by day, rather than month.

body_text: Jan 1, 23; Jan 2, 23 etc. (see column names below)
title: Failure to parse date/time

body_text: Based on the error in red, it seems your date string includes a comma after the day number and this one is using a single digit version when below day 10, this could be the reason it fails. Try updating your date format to: STR_TO_DATE(`Year Day Month (text)`,'%b %e, %y')
title: Failure to parse date/time

body_text: You need to add a comma to your date format: DATE_FORMAT(`MyDateColumn`, '%b %d, %y') For others who come across this there's a great Domo KB article on date format string you can find here: https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/36[PHONE]?language=en_US
title: Failure to parse date/time

body_text: I did try adding a comma and I'm still getting the same error.
title: Failure to parse date/time

body_text: It also seems like you have some slashes before and after your date. I would try adding a REPLACE function to remove those and then convert to date. REPLACE(fieldname,'/','')
title: Failure to parse date/time

body_text: Thanks for the suggestions, but still not having any luck
title: Failure to parse date/time

body_text: @LeonN The %d specifier in the DATE_FORMAT function is expecting a leading zero in the day, so it is expecting 'Jan 01, 23' instead of 'Jan 1, 23'. You may need to manipulate the field to include a leading zero before the day before using the DATE_FORMAT function. Alternatively you could try using the FUZZY_PARSE_DATE function instead of DATE_FORMAT.
title: Failure to parse date/time

body_text: You should be able to use %e instead of %d for the day part to account for the day not being provided in the 2 digits format, and remember to use STR_TO_DATE and not the DATE_FORMAT function, as what you have is a string you want to turn into a date and not displaying a date in a specific string format. I just tested my previous suggestion and seems to be working for me: STR_TO_DATE(`Year Day Month (text)`,'%b %e, %y') I have doubts as in the original post you mentioned having a column called Year Month Date (text) based on your ETL screenshot, but in the table screenshot you're showing the dates to be column names and a column each. What is it that you're trying to achieve? What does your ideal output look like (I doubt you want to have a separate column per each date) and what does your current input look like?
title: Failure to parse date/time

body_text: No, the ideas exchange is alive and well We have Domo heads of product that look at the ideas and takes them into consideration when developing new products. I saw multiple presentations at Domopalooza where screenshots from the ideas exchange were used as evidence that a feature was in high demand among users. Most Domo users know about the ideas exchange, and I have often heard the suggestion from Domo staff and community members to post to the idea exchange as a potential solution for an issue where they can not do something with the current Domo functionality. Yes, the ideas exchange is broken There are about 2,400 ideas in the exchange. Almost all of them are stuck in purgatory and have been for years. Based on some quick filtering of idea status, this is where I see most of the ideas: StatusType PercentofIdeas YearofOldestIdea Submitted and awaiting review from product team ~70% 2020 In Review ~12% 2019 In Backlog ~4% 2022 If it has been 6 years, the ideas is not 'awaiting review from the product team', it is awaiting sweet release from a slow and agonizing death. I can also tell there is not a strong system that compiles and puts ideas in front of the correct product people. If the product team looks at the ideas, it's because they have gone out of their way to do so, not because it is a regular part of their workstream. I would be curious what others think. Is the ideas exchange dead in the water or still bobbing along just fine? Can it be fixed? Here's where I would start: Atomize ideas . Most ideas posted are actually multiple ideas. I'm very guilty of this in the ideas I post. My Trellis Everything™ idea suggests the ability to trellis 7 different chart types. If Domo were to drop everything and begin work on that idea, I don't know if different people would be responsible for each of those chart types, but if so, then the idea should be split into each unit of work needed based on who would complete it. Maybe 2 of those 7 chart types would be very easy to trellis, so they could be prioritized while the other 5 are less realistic. Group similar ideas. There should be a way to relate/connect/merge ideas that are similar. This would be easier if the ideas were already atomized. Systems of review . While the backlog is large, the number of new ideas each week is generally in the single digits. It should be possible to assess each new idea for feasibility and give a quick update. More informative statuses . "We reviewed this, and it is unlikely to be added to our roadmap without more customer demand" "This does not fit into our current strategic vision" "We plan to roll out a similar feature in six months" "Something similar is out in Beta" Changes in status . If something has the same status for more than around 6 months, it should be reviewed again and updated. "This has been pushed to May 2027" Incentivize participation/group moderation . I don't have access to analytics, but based on scrolling through posts, I would estimate the median question on the community forum gets about 40 views and the median idea gets about 15. I don't totally understand how all the points on the forum work, but I know you get points for answering questions (even if the answer is only tangentially related to the question). But it doesn't seem like you get any points for upvoting or commenting on ideas. Maybe some of the work of my above suggestions could be farmed to the community and incentivized? Points for helpfully pairing similar ideas? Points for atomizing an idea into its constituent parts? Man the ship. There is no such thing as a healthy internet forum without human moderation; what makes Wikipedia great is its army of editors. As far as I can tell, there is essentially no one tending to the Ideas Exchange, except perhaps to remove anything blatantly offensive/spammy. The Ideas exchange is currently on autopilot and needs a sturdy captain at the helm. If it were up to me, I would say we need someone paid by Domo to actively manage the community forums. We could call him or her the Community Captain or the Community Forums Manager or Community Activity Manager (CAM) or something? Are there ways you think it should be improved?

Request for Prioritisation This is a compliance blocker , not a convenience feature. Customers in government, finance, and critical infrastructure sectors cannot use Domo with Azure Databricks at all under current constraints. Given the clear technical path, broad customer impact, and alignment with Microsoft's own security standards, we request this be fast-tracked into the upcoming roadmap and are happy to participate in any patch, beta or early access programme.

body_text: Hi Community, We recently switched to our own standalone version of DOMO after previously being a sub-instance of one of our vendors. This vendor is a core system for us, so all of their data is very important and about 95% of the data we use. All of this data is connected as "Federated". When our new instance went live, the federated data stayed connected so we didn't have to re-connect them or anything. Can anyone help me understand how these are connected? Where do they come from? If data stopped flowing right now, I'd have no idea how to troubleshoot the root cause.
title: Federated Data?

body_text: Domo has multiple ways to create "federated" data. One likely way this is now set up for you is through Virtual Datasets. The source Domo instance (your vendor) would have created a virtual dataset job in the Governance Toolkit to select which datasets should be federated to your instance. It is essentially a view and there is nothing for you to configure on your end. If data were to stop, it would be in the vendor's instance to troubleshoot. It requires an access token to function, so that could be the other potential breaking point if that token were to expire. Hope that helps.

body_text: I need to move some beast modes into Magic ETL to help solve a total/subtotal issue. In my attempts to do that I've come across an unusual issue. I have a formula that doesn't seem to want to work. Budget SFM/LB (SUM( Budget Sales Dollars ) - SUM( Budget COGS )) / SUM( Budget Pounds ) This beast mode works just fine in a card however when I move it over to the ETL the value is 0. Here's what's supposed to happen. Budget Sales Dollars = 97,853.45 Budget COGS = 70,729.39 Budget Pounds = 41,849.18 (97,853.45 - 70,729.39) / 41,849.18 = .65 Here's what I've tried: Two Group by tiles: This was supposed to be the original solution to make the move work out. I put the Budget SFM/LB into one group by tile so it could be called in by the second group by tile. This is where I noticed the issue initially Corrected the pattern in Magic ETL I tried creating a group by tile and grouping down to only the fields I need in the card and created the following formulas: SUM(Budget Sales Dollars) SUM(Budget COGs) SUM(Budget Pounds) Then I used a formula tile to create: (Budget Sales Dollars - Budget COGS) / Budget Pounds. I even tried forcing a floating decimal by casting and multiplying by 1.0; no dice Coalesce() I then tried adding a formula tile before the group by tile to coalesce each budget field; nada. Card Formatting I figured at this point maybe the data is stored in the Budget SFM/LB field and just needed to formatted correctly to display, so in analyzer I formatted the field as a number and set decimal to 6; resulted in 0.000000. I have no idea what else to try. I spent all afternoon working with AI on this too only to end up with the same results. I asked other team members to looks at it but we can't find a solution. I'm hoping I'm just overlooking something. Thank you in advance for your help
title: The Math Isn't Mathing

body_text: When you're using your single groupby (before your formula), what are the values being returned for: SUM(Budget Sales Dollars) SUM(Budget COGs) SUM(Budget Pounds) Do you have any filtering in place? Are there records making it to the group by tile?
title: The Math Isn't Mathing

body_text: This seems pretty straightforward so it makes me think you have some sort of data issue that is causing the issue. Here's how I would make sure your data is clean in Magic ETL and doing the math you want to do. You can do it in 3 tiles. Use the Alter Columns tile to force it to be a decimal. Use the Group By tile to sum up your 3 fields by whatever grain you need (I have state in my example) Use the formula tile to make sure there are no nulls. You could potentially consider replacing the IFNULL(Budget Pounds,0) with IFNULL(Budget Pounds,1) to avoid a divide by zero error. When you preview, if you get errors on your Alter Columns, then you have some non-numeric data in your data. You can use the cog next to each field to tell Domo how to handle the bad data.
title: The Math Isn't Mathing

body_text: Last week, I attended my first Domopalooza and I wanted to take a moment to share my reflections. I'd be curious to hear what everyone else took away, so I hope to hear from some of you. My biggest takeaway was how impressed I was by the product managers I got to meet and see present. They seem genuinely engaged with the user community and announced/demoed a host of features that will make my life better in Domo (as they eventually trickle out into GA). More than once, I saw screenshots of posts from this very forum as part of their presentations, showing the demand for the features they built. Also, more than once, and for different features, I heard the claim that a new feature was the "most requested" by the community. That makes me think we could use a better system for merging similar requests and creating a more reliable metric for ranking the "most requested" features. My second big takeaway was that the Domo community is, in fact, a community. I felt warmly welcomed by everyone, especially those that, like me, spend too much time on this forum. It made me realize I would benefit from putting more of myself into this community. Those two things—that Domo leaders take to heart the posts on this forum and my renewed appreciation for the members of this community—motivated this post (and maybe some more posts in the near future). Which brings me to my third takeaway from Domapalooza: bookends to the conference that made me think that Domo leaders misunderstand why people use Domo. The opening bookend was a series of breathless demonstrations of the powerful capabilities of…Claude. The demos were (it was proudly declared) prepared at 1:30 am that morning. I'm curious what was pushed off the agenda by that early-morning brainstorm. One can imagine someone had thought about something for more than a few sleepless hours that they were ready to present to the thousands of attendees at their freshest and most excited. What was the point of the Claude demos? Was the point that Domo's core features are so clumsy that you need to use a different company's robot-god-brain to extract any meaningful value from them? Was the point that none of Domo's own new features were exciting enough to compete with Anthropic, so let's play with the exciting stuff before we have to slog through all the boring Domo stuff the next couple days? They opened with Claude in an apparent vote of no-confidence of Domo. The closing bookend for me, if not the literal one, was when Domo's CEO reacted with exaggerated dismay to Domo being called a "dashboard company". What's wrong with being a dashboard company? What does a well-made Domo dashboard represent? Useful data has been connected, transformed, and analyzed, and is being put in front of the people that need to see it. Which brings me back to why (I believe) people use Domo. That process from connecting raw data to presenting it clearly has never been as easy as it is in Domo. That is Domo's competitive advantage. Anything that adds to that ease of use will build on Domo's advantage, and anything that distracts from it is a missed opportunity. The vision laid out in the general sessions started and ended with Claude and some dubious promises of using AI in Domo. Happily in contrast to that vision, when I look at the product announcements from Domo, I think most if not all are building on Domo's ease of use; you don't need to use Claude to benefit from Worksheets or the myriad enhancements in MagicETL. That mismatch between what Domo is saying they're doing and what they're actually doing gives me hope. What I do see missing is any investment in cards. What was the last new card type we got in Domo? I think it was packed bubbles back in October 2023 almost three years ago? (I'm not counting the minor updates to donuts and gauges in January 2024). Worksheets and the new App Components serve a similar function as cards, so those are welcome and helpful additions, but they don't play across the entire Domo ecosystem the way that cards do. So I'll close with my case for cards. The card is the atomic unit of analysis in Domo. They determine what can be built with the rest of Domo with the least friction. Wouldn't it be nice to expand the periodic table a bit? I'm not talking about features that can only be used in AppStudio or that you need Claude to help you create in a ProCode app, but cards that my least technical users can make from anywhere in Domo and have a better handle on their data than they did before. I have some ideas for the types of cards that I'd love to see, and my intention is to post some ideas in the coming weeks making a more specific case for those cards. I hope you upvote some of those ideas and contribute some of your own. I also hope some resources are left at Domo after they pay for all their Anthropic subscriptions to continue to develop the part of Domo that makes Domo what is is: a dashboard company.
title: Reflections from Domopalooza 2026 and my Case for Cards

body_text: Great stuff David. Thanks for sharing and writing a thoughful response. Totally agree on the community. It was AMAZING to meet all of y'all in person. I think this is an important asset to DOMO and they would be remiss to neglect, abuse, ignore, or otherwise undermine the strength of this community. I'm not saying they are - but one thing DOMO has that other's do not is us :) I agree on the sentiment regarding Claude use within DOMO. The start of the conference felt like an un-skippable ad for Claude, and I know a few others I spoke to felt this way too. Are we here for DOMO or are we here for Claude? None of what got presented needed DOMO to succeed - the "native" visualization within the Claude interface was the hero presented on the foundation of the Claude coding engine. While tremendously impressive and amazing, this had nothing to do with DOMO… Plus, and perhaps most importantly, it was never actually taught HOW to get Claude to work in DOMO. There's a lot that has to happen between having data in DOMO to having Claude actually work in your environment. I didn't receive the CEO's closing comment in the same light as you. I received it more optimistically, as if he were to say "Yes, we make dashboards, but we are so much more than just building dashboards! We also have MagicETL, and robust governance, and XYZ….." That being said, I do agree with your sentiment: a dashboard in it's most purest form is a dance of governance and clean data and optimized ETLs and smart charting and thoughtful plating and optimized UX and etc. etc. etc. But I don't think Josh James took it that way. Excited to see what everyone says,

body_text: Terrific post @DavidChurchman . Domo’s competitive advantage is making the data-to-dashboard workflow simple and accessible. Strategies that reinforce that strength will continue to add value; those that pull focus away from it risk diluting what makes Domo effective. I agree that continued investment in the foundational layer—cards, data modeling, and overall usability—is critical. Personally, I’m not looking to use Domo for building workflows or writing code. If I need that, I can use tools like Claude or Cursor directly. It’s also worth considering the added cost implications when similar capabilities exist outside the platform. It feels like some of the current direction is being influenced by executive demand to highlight how AI is being used, rather than how data is being effectively leveraged. In practice, I still see challenges with AI reliably handling even relatively simple data relationships, like joins across a few tables. That can lead to impressive demos, but inconsistent results in real-world use. With that in mind—and acknowledging that some of these may already be in development or beta—here are a few suggestions focused on strengthening the core experience: Cohort / Retention Card (simplified) • A card that shows how groups of users behave over time after they start Example: Group users by when they signed up (e.g., January, February, March), then track what percentage of each group returns in later weeks or months Signup Month Week 1 Week 2 Week 3 Jan 100% 60% 45% Feb 100% 55% 40% Funnel / Conversion Card (simplified) • A card that shows how people move through steps in a process—and where they drop off Example (website flow): Visited site → Signed up → Made a purchase What you’d see: Step 1: 10,000 users Step 2: 4,000 users (40% conversion) Step 3: 1,000 users (25% conversion from step 2) Time Comparison Card (Smart) • Automatically compares WoW, MoM, and YoY performance • Includes % change and clear visual indicators Variance / Waterfall Enhancements • More robust variance analysis (plan vs. actual with contributing drivers) • Moves beyond basic waterfall charts into clearer financial storytelling Text / Narrative Card (non-AI) • Rule-based summaries (not generative AI) Example: “Revenue increased 12% vs last month, driven by X” Parameterized Cards • A single card that can dynamically switch metrics or dimensions • Reduces the need to duplicate multiple versions of the same card Card-Level Versioning • Track changes over time • Ability to roll back when needed Cross-Dataset Cards • Blend data directly at the card level without requiring heavy ETL processes Improved Debugging Tools • Step-by-step data inspection • Clearer error tracing and troubleshooting
title: Reflections from Domopalooza 2026 and my Case for Cards

body_text: @DavidChurchman @ArborRose @MarkSnodgrass I also think that sometimes we are not good about putting things into release notes that impact cards. Sometimes it could be the small things like a setting on a donut. but sometimes other bigger things. I actually just reviewed some changes I requested to Flex Tables (had started this before this thread was a thought in your mind) as I use them a lot to show change over time for product metrics internally. Maybe like 5-6 changes to take it from sometimes useful to really awesome (sorting, some better labeling options). The engineer did mention there were a couple other new cards he was working on. And I would also call out that I think this ability to let a slicer filter set a variable is huge and game changing and I have been pushing for it for a while (https://www.domo.com/product/new-features/slicer-card-and-variable-linking, includes a video from yours truly explaining part of why I love it ). Also, there is a balance between the "exec pushing for AI" narrative (which is true) and the reality of a new world. I have been doing a lot with Claude desktop chat and our early versions of MCP and it is game changing what I can do. Now at the end of it I want the option to create some old fashioned cards too if needed or maybe a few cards and one pro code component/brick with cards around them. And that is coming soon. Still some of that atomic unit of a card but letting AI make us faster and quicker. I would also look at the new editing experience in app studio for cards. I was a hater at first. I liked my old analyzer (which yes maybe needed some refreshing). But editing in one canvas is super powerful and I am so glad we got this out to people now. https://www.domo.com/product/new-features/domo-bi-domopalooza-announcements It is a balance always in the life of a product leader. Listen to customers, solve pain points, understand what is coming new, align with business priorities. that is the life I chose I suppose!

body_text:
Terrific post @DavidChurchman.

Domo’s competitive advantage is making the data-to-dashboard workflow simple and accessible. Strategies that reinforce that strength will continue to add value; those that pull focus away from it risk diluting what makes Domo effective.

I agree that continued investment in the foundational layer—cards, data modeling, and overall usability—is critical. Personally, I’m not looking to use Domo for building workflows or writing code. If I need that, I can use tools like Claude or Cursor directly. It’s also worth considering the added cost implications when similar capabilities exist outside the platform.

It feels like some of the current direction is being influenced by executive demand to highlight how AI is being used, rather than how data is being effectively leveraged. In practice, I still see challenges with AI reliably handling even relatively simple data relationships, like joins across a few tables. That can lead to impressive demos, but inconsistent results in real-world use.

With that in mind—and acknowledging that some of these may already be in development or beta—here are a few suggestions focused on strengthening the core experience:

Cohort / Retention Card (simplified) • A card that shows how groups of users behave over time after they start

Example: Group users by when they signed up (e.g., January, February, March), then track what percentage of each group returns in later weeks or months

Funnel / Conversion Card (simplified) • A card that shows how people move through steps in a process—and where they drop off

Example (website flow): Visited site → Signed up → Made a purchase

What you’d see: Step 1: 10,000 users Step 2: 4,000 users (40% conversion) Step 3: 1,000 users (25% conversion from step 2)

Time Comparison Card (Smart) • Automatically compares WoW, MoM, and YoY performance • Includes % change and clear visual indicators

Variance / Waterfall Enhancements • More robust variance analysis (plan vs. actual with contributing drivers) • Moves beyond basic waterfall charts into clearer financial storytelling

Text / Narrative Card (non-AI) • Rule-based summaries (not generative AI)

Example: “Revenue increased 12% vs last month, driven by X”

Parameterized Cards • A single card that can dynamically switch metrics or dimensions • Reduces the need to duplicate multiple versions of the same card

Card-Level Versioning • Track changes over time • Ability to roll back when needed

Cross-Dataset Cards • Blend data directly at the card level without requiring heavy ETL processes

Improved Debugging Tools • Step-by-step data inspection • Clearer error tracing and troubleshooting

body_text:
Terrific post @DavidChurchman.

Domo’s competitive advantage is making the data-to-dashboard workflow simple and accessible. Strategies that reinforce that strength will continue to add value; those that pull focus away from it risk diluting what makes Domo effective.

I agree that continued investment in the foundational layer—cards, data modeling, and overall usability—is critical. Personally, I’m not looking to use Domo for building workflows or writing code. If I need that, I can use tools like Claude or Cursor directly. It’s also worth considering the added cost implications when similar capabilities exist outside the platform.

It feels like some of the current direction is being influenced by executive demand to highlight how AI is being used, rather than how data is being effectively leveraged. In practice, I still see challenges with AI reliably handling even relatively simple data relationships, like joins across a few tables. That can lead to impressive demos, but inconsistent results in real-world use.

With that in mind—and acknowledging that some of these may already be in development or beta—here are a few suggestions focused on strengthening the core experience:

Cohort / Retention Card (simplified) • A card that shows how groups of users behave over time after they start

Example: Group users by when they signed up (e.g., January, February, March), then track what percentage of each group returns in later weeks or months

Signup Month

Week 1

Week 2

Week 3

Jan

100%

60%

45%

Feb

100%

55%

40%

Funnel / Conversion Card (simplified) • A card that shows how people move through steps in a process—and where they drop off

Example (website flow): Visited site → Signed up → Made a purchase

What you’d see: Step 1: 10,000 users Step 2: 4,000 users (40% conversion) Step 3: 1,000 users (25% conversion from step 2)

Time Comparison Card (Smart) • Automatically compares WoW, MoM, and YoY performance • Includes % change and clear visual indicators

Variance / Waterfall Enhancements • More robust variance analysis (plan vs. actual with contributing drivers) • Moves beyond basic waterfall charts into clearer financial storytelling

Text / Narrative Card (non-AI) • Rule-based summaries (not generative AI)

Example: “Revenue increased 12% vs last month, driven by X”

Parameterized Cards • A single card that can dynamically switch metrics or dimensions • Reduces the need to duplicate multiple versions of the same card

Card-Level Versioning • Track changes over time • Ability to roll back when needed

Cross-Dataset Cards • Blend data directly at the card level without requiring heavy ETL processes

Improved Debugging Tools • Step-by-step data inspection • Clearer error tracing and troubleshooting

body_text: When sorting a table card in descending order, it would make more sense to put nulls last. Currently, if there are any nulls in the column, they show up first, making it seem like they are the highest values. For cases where a table has meaningful null values in some cells, and when the end user needs to be able to sort by multiple columns themselves (so not inside Analyzer), this is limiting. In our case, we did not want to input zeros in those null fields because they would affect average calculations. I reached out to support, and they suggested I submit the request here, since there is not a good workaround yet. Thanks!

title: Sort table card DESC nulls last

body_text: I have a dataset that has bookings and quota in it for all sellers in our company. How can I create a PDP that only filters out the quotas for each rep but still allows them to see everyone else's bookings activity?
title: How to apply PDPs that only hide a portion of data?

body_text: Hi @D-Rab , Just trying to understand. So if I was a rep, you would only want me to see my quota information, but everyone else's booking? These are two different columns right? If you could provide a screenshot or something that is always helpful.
title: How to apply PDPs that only hide a portion of data?

body_text: Appreciate the question. So i basically need to create a rule for: Rep Type (Booking or Quota) I want Reps to be able to see everyone's booking data while only being able to see their personal quota The booking/quota value is in the same column currently but can be changed if need be.
title: How to apply PDPs that only hide a portion of data?

body_text: Each individual PDP policy is subtractive, they filter the dataset, but when multiple policies apply they become additive. The combined result is the union of all rows allowed by each policy. In your case, you want two separate policies that work together: A Quota policy where Type = Quota and Rep = Managed Attribute (such as email or employee ID). This ensures each rep only sees their own quota rows. A Bookings policy where Type = Bookings. This allows the rep to see all rows classified as bookings. Together the two policies ensure that each rep sees only their own quotas plus all booking activity.
title: How to apply PDPs that only hide a portion of data?

body_text: A super useful (and increasingly popular) chart type for comparing two categories (before/after; rep/dem) is the dumbbell/connected dot plot. You can kind of do this with the horizontal High/Low chart in Domo, except in cases where the series switches which is higher/lower. (See Pinterest in the in chart above). You can also kind of do it with overlapping lollipop plots, but it's much more visually noisy (i.e., ugly). Couple of blogs showing examples of implementation: https://datavizcatalogue.com/blog/chart-snapshot-dumbbell-plot/ https://www.storytellingwithdata.com/blog/2020/12/9/what-is-a-dot-plot

body_text: We recently started testing out Cloud Amplifier on our Snowflake environment. It's great but there is one issue that is preventing us from using it. Our Snowflake database names change every month due to a data architecture decision our engineering team has implemented. This is preventing us from using CA on Snowflake because the Domo dataset is tied to the Snowflake table and database. If we change the database of the existing connection, it creates a new dataset which would then have to be updated in downstream ETLs. Yes we can create a workflow to do this, but it would be much less painful if by default we could swap out source tables and databases while maintaining the same dataset in Domo. Thanks!

body_text: I have a column with base64 character string that I want to utilize in an HTML card to show logos. The base64 character strings are extremely long (over 17k characters) and I can't get the images to render in the HTML table card. Does anyone know if this is an issue with a character limitation in a column or used in a beast mode?
title: Base64 character limitation?

body_text: Domo has a character limit of 1024 characters per column. You can try and talk with Domo to see if they can increase the limit but if you upload a string with more than 1024 characters it'll only save the first 1024. You could attempt to split your base64 into 1024 chunks but would require you to split it out and reassemble it manually - likely with a custom app.
title: Base64 character limitation?

body_text: @jpotter I think there is a command in the Java CLI that lets you adjust the character limit for a specific column. Set-dataset-column-width
title: Base64 character limitation?

body_text: Thank you both. I thought I remembered a character limit, but wanted to confirm.
title: Base64 character limitation?

body_text: We are trying to get into more operational data reporting in Domo. Other teammates are using Microsoft Excel on their shared drive in a working document to track all of their projects and work. … I saw that we have a Domo Office Add-in already installed in the spreadsheet, but it's currently used for adding Domo dashboards in the Excel document. I'm wondering if it can go the opposite direction with the same plugin, and setup a Connetor in Domo with this specific Excel Spreadsheet as the source/input? I'd love to be able to pull info directly from that spreadsheet where that team is working and not setup an extra process to get info into Domo.
title: Can we use an Excel file as the Source for Domo?

body_text: I believe the Domo office add-in is only one-way (Domo to Excel). You have a number of options for bring Excel into Domo: • Manual upload • Domo Workbench (see Admin > tools) • API calls, etc
title: Can we use an Excel file as the Source for Domo?

body_text: Yes, you can use the office add-in to update data in Domo from your Excel sheet. Here is the KB article that walks you through it: https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/000005143?language=en_US#update_datasets_in_excel Other options would be the Microsoft SharePoint Online Rest Connector. You can have the connector point at that Excel file/worksheet tab and bring that data into Domo.
title: Can we use an Excel file as the Source for Domo?

body_text: Sample Dataset: Order Sales$ SalesRep Region A 100 1 CA B 100 2 CA C 100 3 CA D 100 4 CA Context: I need to set up a PDP for a Regional Manager where he would be able to see all Sales made in Region CA regardless of the Sales Rep. So basically he would see the Total Sales for his Region = CA = $400. I set up Row PDP for him with Region = CA Problem: Only Sales Rep 1 & 3 are under this RM. I have a filter drop down for "Sales Rep" column, and ideally, he should only able to select "1" or "3" and maybe have "2" and "4" masked like "*" and "*". This is because the RM need to see the Total Sales for his Region as $400 but breakdown the Sales by Sales Rep under him only. Anyone had experience with this? Any advice would be great, thank you. P/S: In this example, there is only 1 Regional Manager, but in reality we have more than one
title: Rows Masking, is it possible?

body_text: I'm not aware of a way to do this. The approach I would take is to create an aggregate dataset at the region level, so that the Region Manager can see the totals for their region and then apply pdp to the granular dataset so that the RM can only see the details of the sales reps that are their direct reports
title: Rows Masking, is it possible?

body_text: To add to ggenovese, you could use MagicETL group-by to sum by region, and then join the totals back onto the dataset. The result could look something like this: Order Sales$ SalesRep Region TotalbyRegion A 100 1 CA 400 B * * CA 400 C 100 3 CA 400 D * * CA 400
title: Rows Masking, is it possible?

body_text: Hi, @verytiredgirl - thanks for this feedback! We're looking at how we could enhance column PDP to do the first half of what I think you're asking. Here's how this would work (please let me know if I've misunderstood you). When you create a Column PDP policy, you would have the ability to make the policy apply conditionally based on the value in some identifier column matching a user attribute. So, in your example, your policy would be effectively (I'll write this out in SQL for clarity): CASE WHEN 'RM Email Address' = userAttribute.userEmail THEN 'value' ELSE NULL END So, that would allow you to selectively mask per-row, but, it doesn't get you the second part: total sales for region CA. We've received this feedback from some other users, too; However, we're treating it as lower priority based on the limited signal we've received and the relatively greater complexity. Please do consider adding your feedback in our Ideas Exchange: https://community-forums.domo.com/main/categories/governance-security-ideas Thanks for pushing the boundaries of Domo!
title: Rows Masking, is it possible?

body_text: Adobe has announced it will retire v1.4 of its Adobe Analytics API in August 2026. When that happens, any datasets using the Adobe Analytics 1.4 connectors will no longer pull data successfully. Domo has a connector that connects to the v2.0 version of the API using the server-server OAuth mechanism. This connector is available to all customers at this time. The Connector Team has evaluated the possibility of migrating customer datasets from connectors using the 1.4 API to connectors using the 2.0 API. Unfortunately, the two API are too different from each other to allow Domo to migrate datasets. As a result, customers who still need to pull data from Adobe Analytics will need to recreate their datasets using the Adobe Analytics v2 server-server or OAuth connector. Customers are encouraged to try out the v2.0 connector ( https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/36[PHONE]?language=en_US ) and to notify Domo via a Support Case or their CSM if they see a discrepancy in functionality that impacts their reporting capabilities. The schedule for the v1.4 connector retirement is as follows: (1) Connector power ups restricted - March 31st 2026. Existing datasets will continue to run but no new datasets can be powered up with the 1.4 connector. (2) Connector is retired - July 8th 2026. Any existing dataset on the 1.4 connector will fail, and dataset settings will no longer be editable. (3) Adobe retires v1.4 API - Aug 12th 2026
title: Adobe Analytics 1.4 API retirement

body_text: I am trying to use actual values to project forward. For example, I have a table that has Month (12 rows: January 1, 2026 - December 1, 2026) and a column 'Actuals' that is filled in For January, February and March. I can join that table to an Assumptions tile that has month over Month factor for all twelve months in the year. What I want to do is either: Take 'actuals' lag 1 month and multiply that by the month over month factor and place that in a new filed 'forecast' so it would take the March actual value, multiply that by the april month over month factor and place it in a field called forecast for april. After that, it should apply the may Month over month factor to the April forecast number and place that into the may forecast slot. I can make it work in Beat mode function and have it in the table card, but i cant get it to work in ETL to place it in a table to do other things with
title: Lag to set a forecast

body_text: Magic ETL cannot perform recursive calculations (where each row depends on the previous row’s result). Instead, you must restructure the logic so each row can be calculated independently — typically using a running product or cumulative calculation based on existing data.
title: Lag to set a forecast

body_text: The first thing you need to do is convert your factors table into a compound factors table. So if your table looks like: Jan 1 2026, 1.0 Feb 1 2026, 0.8 Mar 1 2026, 0.7 Apr 1 2026, 1.2 We're going to make it look like this: Jan 1 2026, 1.0 Feb 1 2026, 0.8 Mar 1 2026, 0.56 Apr 1 2026, 0.6720 All the factors are written in terms of the cumulative factor since the start of the table. That way to get the factor between two points in the table, we just need to take the target month factor and divide it by the actual month factor: Predicting April based on February becomes 0.672/0.8 = 0.84 (which is the same as 0.7*1.2). Unfortunately, cumulative product is not a function in Magic or indeed in most SQL dialects. Cumulative SUM(), sure, but there's not PRODUCT(). But there's a trick we can use to do it with SUM() by using logarithms: SELECT *, EXP(SUM(LN(`Factor`)) OVER (ORDER BY `Month`)) AS `Cumulative Factor` FROM `Assumptions`; (Note that you can do this with three tiles instead of the SQL tile if you want: Add Formula (for the LN) → Rank & Window (for the cumulative sum) → Add Formula (for the EXP).) Now all that remains is to select the row you want to use for prediction. It sounded like you wanted the most recent row that has actual data. Pick that row using either an Order → Limit or SQL. Then inner join that row to the cumulative factors table on the month, keeping only the cumulative factor column from that side of the join and renaming it to Base Factor. Then join that result onto the cumulative factors table again , this time using CumulativeFactor.Month > Source.Month as the join expression. Now you have a table containing all the information you need for your projections: The actual value from the most recent data point and the base factor for that month, both repeated in every row, and then the cumulative factor for every month thereafter. Now you just add this formua: Actuals*(CumulativeFactor/BaseFactor) To get your predicted value for all the future months.
title: Lag to set a forecast

body_text: If there's still a piece you feel like you're missing then feel free to say—you can certainly accomplish this in Magic ETL without a beast mode if that is your goal. The SQL provided in the accepted answer will transform your month-to-month factors table into a cumulative factors table from the first month, and then it's just a matter of selecting the prediction-source row (again, assuming I understood your initial ask as using the latest row as the source for projecting the rest of the months), joining that into the cumulative factors table to get the base factor, and then joining the result of that onto the original to get the arguments you need for the final projection expression (Actual*(CumFactor/BaseFactor)). If it's a problem of clarity, I could include screenshots of the necessary tiles or just write the whole thing out in SQL (I had to make some assumptions about your table and column names, I hope they're clear enough): WITH `Cumulative Factors` AS ( SELECT `Month`, EXP(SUM(LN(`Factor`)) OVER (ORDER BY `Month`)) AS `Factor` FROM `Factors` ), `Base Factor` AS ( SELECT `m`.`Month`, `m`.`Actual` / `cf`.`Factor` AS `Factor` FROM `Main` `m` INNER JOIN `Cumulative Factors` `cf` ON `m`.`Month` = `cf`.`Month` WHERE `Actual` IS NOT NULL ORDER BY `Month` DESC LIMIT 1 ) SELECT `m`.`Month`, COALESCE(`m`.`Actual`, `bf`.`Factor` * `cf`.`Factor`) AS `Actual` FROM `Main` `m` CROSS JOIN `Base Factor` `bf` INNER JOIN `Cumulative Factors` `cf` ON `m`.`Month` = `cf`.`Month`;
title: Lag to set a forecast

body_text: Like the Title says, didn't include all the other ones but these are the top 3 that came to my mind. What are the pros/cons of picking any of those as your CDW, what does one have over the other and vice versa? Currently have my data housed in S3 because there were no other ways for me to get the data connected for scheduled reports. But interested to know if there were a way for me to get around the S3 limitation if I should have my data housed elsewhere?
title: What are the Advantages/Disadvantages of picking Snowflake vs. Databricks vs. AWS S3?

body_text: We're using Snowflake and BigQuery, but I find the Snowflake UI much more intuitive. However, one of the biggest reasons to choose Snowflake/Databricks would be to leverage the Cloud Integration features in Domo. Including a pushdown compute feature in MagicETL, which allows you to use the compute power of your CDW rather than relying only on Domo. This reduced our compute time by 86% on some transformations with massive datasets.
title: What are the Advantages/Disadvantages of picking Snowflake vs. Databricks vs. AWS S3?

body_text: Snowflake and Databricks are direct competitors to each other, while AWS S3 is a slightly different product. Snowflake and Databricks both offer cloud data warehousing, managed by them, allowing you to focus on the data and not worry about the set up of VMs, managing servers, etc. With Snowflake, you can stick to SQL to build tables, create databases, move data, and create logical structures in the same traditional format you are familiar with. You pay for what you store and pay for what you compute. Use more and pay more. But no facility overhead or infrastructure overhead. I've only ever used Snowflake, but from what I have read, Databricks is considered more technical than snowflake, where you can have a little more control of the processing and compute methods. DB is Spark based IIRC, and Snowflake is really just traditional SQL. How I understand them, a team that favors SQL writing will do better with Snowflake, and a team that favors righting python Spark jobs will do better with Databricks. AWS S3 is object storage (storing files). Not a data warehouse by itself. You can use your files in S3 to serve as a source of data that is ingested into your data warehouse, which is very common. I know that Snowflake can easily stage files from S3/GCP Cloud Storage directly into tables in your data warehouse, it's a simple process and can be automated as well. As far as Domo goes, Domo has cloud amplifier connections that connect directly to your Snowflake or Databricks instance. Connecting the two is straightforward.
title: What are the Advantages/Disadvantages of picking Snowflake vs. Databricks vs. AWS S3?

body_text: I asked this question to more than one of the company booths at Domopalooza last week. The Snowflake people basically said what @Dhuddleston mentions - users find the Snowflake UI is more intuitive. And it already has close ties with Domo and Connectors, and assets available. There are other solutions than what you mention but here's what I gather - think of these as doing different jobs—not direct replacements. I do use these myself, as I am researching the same question. S3 is just storage. It’s cheap and scalable, but it doesn’t actually analyze anything. You still need another tool on top to run reports. Snowflake is built for reporting and dashboards. It’s the easiest way to turn data into answers. Fast, reliable, and low effort for teams. The tradeoff is cost and less flexibility for advanced data work. Databricks is built for heavy data work and AI. It’s powerful, but more complex and usually needs engineers to run it. Better for building pipelines and models than for simple reporting. How to think about it If your goal is reports and business insights → pick Snowflake If your goal is data pipelines or AI → pick Databricks If your goal is just storing data cheaply → keep S3 What most companies actually do They don’t choose one. They use: S3 for storage (cheap) Snowflake for reporting (simple, fast) Databricks only if they need advanced data work
title: What are the Advantages/Disadvantages of picking Snowflake vs. Databricks vs. AWS S3?

body_text: And am I assuming correctly that by leveraging the compute power of the CDW it saves on your Domo credits. Follow-up question: Is it not really worth it to have a CDW like Snowflake/BigQuery/Databricks if you have smaller datasets (1 or 2 in comparison to say a bigger industry with multiple lanes of data coming in for instance finance, logistics, customer service, etc)
title: What are the Advantages/Disadvantages of picking Snowflake vs. Databricks vs. AWS S3?

body_text: Correct, you save on Domo credits, but it does increase your CDW usage. However, we find that the overall cost trade-off is usually in your favor. Since I don't have the full context for your follow-up question, I can say that the decision to use a CDW depends more on table sizes. For example, our product usage data contains billions of rows. Snowflake, like Domo, charges based on usage, but when dealing with hundreds of billions of rows, the CDW handles larger tables more efficiently. Overall, I recommend maximizing the use of Domo connectors until you encounter limitations like slow data loads or Magic runs. Then, evaluate which option makes the most sense.
title: What are the Advantages/Disadvantages of picking Snowflake vs. Databricks vs. AWS S3?

body_text: Hi, I’m working with a dataset that is updated monthly through a Magic ETL, where new data gets appended to the historical dataset. I now need to make a one-time correction to the existing historical data in that output dataset. However, when I try to create a new Magic ETL for this, it generates a separate dataset instead of modifying the current one. Is there a way to update or overwrite the existing dataset’s historical data without disrupting the current ETL pipeline that appends data each month?
title: How to Update Historical Data in an Append-Based Magic ETL?

body_text: There are several ways to update an existing dataset. I find it easiest to modify a record with Python via Jupyter Workspaces. I've loaded the entire dataset into a data frame, modified the record, and replaced the dataset via the data frame. But this kind of thing requires some experience with Python or knowing how to get AI to write you the code. I have tried updating a dataset using Magic ETL and eventually decided I didn't like trying that at all. Perhaps someone can give you a good upsert example.
title: How to Update Historical Data in an Append-Based Magic ETL?

body_text: Simple answer - Not easily. An alternative is to create a new dataflow with your affected dataset as the output, make the necessary changes and output it to another dataset. Once you review and test the dataset you can use the APIs to update your dataflow so the output dataset is the same ID as your input dataset and then re-run. If you need help walking you through this, send me a DM.
title: How to Update Historical Data in an Append-Based Magic ETL?
