body_text: The product team enjoyed answering questions from the audience during the final session at Domopalooza. Below you will find the answers to all questions related to Sandbox, Beast Modes, Consumption, Learn Domo and more (including those that weren't mentioned on stage). Q: Are all the new updates available to those NOT on the consumption model? Workflows, App Studio, AI… A: We are all-in on the consumption model. If you're not, please talk to your account executive. Q: What’s the future of the semantic/metadata layer in Domo? A: We are actively working toward a solution, and soliciting feedback from multiple customers in the process. We look forward to sharing more as it develops. Q: I am a developer, I use version control daily in my work. How does Domo do change management/version control for its Domo instances, ETLs, Cards, etc? A: This is supported by Sandbox, which allows you to create content in a Development environment, then migrate it to your production environment. Sandbox supports, ETL's Cards, Pages, Dataviews and connectors. Sandbox also tracks versions of content and allows for rollback in production if needed. Q: How difficult is it to onboard the Sandbox environment? Can I turn my current instance into the sandbox instance? A: Domo Sandbox enables migration of content between instances. It is easy to set up a new DEV instance or even set up a new PROD instance and use your current instance as the DEV instance. Q: My organization uses a DEV and PROD environment for its SDLC, can that be extended into Domo? A: Domo supports having separate DEV and PROD instances. Check out Sandbox and Governance Toolkit featuresSpeak with your account team to find out more. Q: Any plans to be add the ability to run SQL queries on datasets directly from PHP? A: Domo supports APIs that can be used to query datasets using a variety of languages. Q: What would you recommend to someone starting with DOMO with no developer or technical experience? What is the best approach to begin learning? A: The Domo Community Forums are a great place to start. Knowledge base articles provides great articles. We also offer Domo Free which is available to try out the platform without cost. Just jump into Domo and give it a shot. It was built for business users first. Q: Can DomoStat datasets be ran without using a credit (if you are in consumption model)? A: Currently this is something we are considering implementing. Q: Are folders or a different way to organize and manage Beast Modes a possibility??? A: As of right now the plan for the V1 of workspaces does not include Beast Modes as a feature you can organize with folders, but it is on the list of entities to add in future versions. Q: For customers on the consumption model- Any plans to rollover unused credits that customers have paid for but haven’t used? A: Credits expire at the end of the allocation time. Standard credits typically last a year and all other types are allocated (and expire) monthly. Q: What's the difference between Workspaces and pdp? A: A workspace includes more than just access to data, it also includes access to content. So adding a dashboard to a workspace will automatically share it and its cards with everyone in the workspace, and if it is removed from the workspace the dashboard and all of its cards are unshared with the people in the workspace. PDP is a level of protection on top of the sharing of content like usual. Q: How do we efficiently clean up the crazy number of beast modes that now exist in our instance? A: The Beast Mode manager provides insights into Beast Modes and their respective cards / Pages. You can also manage Beast Modes in bulk using the manager. There are also multiple Domostats available that provide insights into which are currently being used and where. Q: Besides App studio or AI what other features are you guys most excited about? A: Universal Models (Forecasting, outlier detection, PII Detection) and many different product itegrations that are focused on helping you gain valuable insights faster. Q: When do we get columnar PDP? A: Column masking limited beta in May - full rollout Summer. Q: Does DOMO offer onboarding training? A: Yes! Check out Domo University or Talk to your account team about training offerings by Domo's Education team. Q: When is Git Integration coming? This is in regard to all areas where code is involved, i.e., Jupyter, Code Engine, and other pro-code tiles across the platform. A: We don't have any plans for this just yet, but this is a great suggestion. Q: Could you demo the PowerPoint embedding? A: Talk to your account team to schedule a demo of this functionality. Q: There is so much available in Domo, what is the best way to find features that might be useful? A: In the consumption model, customers have access to the advanced Domo feature sets. In addition to discovery, Knowledge Base articles are a great way to learn about features. Have any follow-up questions? Post them in the comments below. A product team owner is closely moderating this post and will respond promptly to your questions.
title: Miscellaneous Q&A from Domopalooza

body_text: In DOMO, I have: Dataset A: Sales $ at order level, daily (millions of rows) Dataset B: Sales $ at order level daily (millions of rows) Dataset C: Sales $ by Month (100 rows) Goal: I want to compare the Sales $ between these 3 sources quickly. Option 1: Create ETL, grouping Sales $ by Month for Dataset A and B, then join those 3 datasets together. Cons: not efficient to run this ETL every 2 hours, and ETL run too slow. Option 2: Create Data Model, not possible since data model can only map datasets that come from the same source. So say Dataset A is from Snowflake, Dataset B is from Workbench will not work. Any other viable options?

body_text: Your option 1 seems to describe: Dataset A → Group By Month Dataset B → Group By Month Dataset C (already monthly) Join A + B + C Which is what I would normally try. Could you do this with Dataset Views instead — aggregating A and B to month in the view and joining them with Dataset C — so that no scheduled ETL is required?

body_text: Use Dataset Views for aggregation (but NOT joining) Step 1: Create 2 Views View A → aggregate to Month View B → aggregate to Month Step 2: Feed those views as datasets into Magic ETL. Now: Input are already small datasets. Then join and add formulas. ================ To attempt a UNION, I would try something like: Use Union in Magic ETL Step 1: Aggregate each dataset (Group By tiles) Step 2: Add a constant column: A → "A" as Source B → "B" C → "C" Step 3: Append Rows tile Now you get: Month | Source | Sales Jan | A | 100 Jan | B | 90 Jan | C | 95

body_text: Hi all, Recently there is a newly added Domo feature where the 'Merged from datasource..." beast modes will be created when cards that are using the beast modes are moved to a new DataSet. But we found that this new feature has an effect on the previous data source as well : domo will rename all the beastmodes merged previously (as "name + merged from xxxx") even if we have already adapted their name before and generated automatically another beastmode with the origin name... I understand that this feature allows the future merged cards to still render without errors, but it does make it more difficult from a governance standpoint for the previous merged cards. As far as I know, we don't have a way to avoid this behavior, so we have to archive/rename all the beastmodes affected as necessary. body_text: Hi, My company publishes a report for investors once a quarter in PDF format. It is made avaialbe on our website and the investors would like to be able to take the PDF, convert it to an excel sheet and be able to work with the data as a table instead of an image. Currently, we have about 15 tables in the report and half of them show up in table format in excel (vs in a image) Here is an image to show the difference: I am wondering, is there something in DOMO to handle this? Thanks in advance
title: How can I take a report from a PDF and make sure that the PDF extracts them as tables?

body_text: The problem appears to be in the way the PDF is created. Well structured text will come out as tables that can be recognized and extracted. Since you have a mix, it appears that some were properly exported and others were flattened to images. Using Adobe Acrobat Pro, I believe you can do an export from PDF to Excel. But it would require recognize text via OCR being turned on.
title: How can I take a report from a PDF and make sure that the PDF extracts them as tables?

body_text: EXAMPLE 1 — GOOD (Excel → Export as PDF) How to do it: File > Save As > PDF OR File > Export > Create PDF/XPS What this does: Keeps each cell as real text Preserves rows and columns Creates a structured PDF that Excel can read What happens when opened in Excel: Columns stay aligned Data lands in proper cells Little to no cleanup needed Quick test: Copy a row from the PDF and paste into Excel Result: data stays in separate columns (GOOD) EXAMPLE 2 — GOOD (Word Tables → Export as PDF) How to do it: Insert > Table (build table in Word) Then: File > Save As > PDF What this does: Word tables are exported as real table structures Rows and columns are preserved in the PDF What happens when opened in Excel: Table structure is mostly maintained Columns usually align correctly Quick test: Copy a row from the PDF and paste into Excel Result: data stays in columns (GOOD) EXAMPLE 3 — BAD (Print to PDF) How it happens: File > Print > select "Microsoft Print to PDF" What this does: Flattens the table into visual layout only Removes row/column structure Breaks Excel’s ability to detect tables What happens when opened in Excel: Data comes in as one column OR Data is misaligned / unusable Quick test: Copy a row from the PDF and paste into Excel Result: everything ends up in one column or messy (BAD)
title: How can I take a report from a PDF and make sure that the PDF extracts them as tables?

body_text: @brentsickmiller @ARosser @AsimBaig @CBrowne Apologies if you've already tried this, but have you tried to manually sync the collection using the API? I have a code engine function that does this, and I just tried it and it synced the collection to the dataset successfully. Could be worth a try? const codeengine = require("codeengine"); async function syncCollection(collectionId) { if (!collectionId) { throw new Error('Collection ID is required'); } // gets the collection const collection = await codeengine.sendRequest( "get", /api/datastores/v1/collections/${collectionId} ); if (!collection || !collection.datastoreId) { throw new Error('Invalid collection or missing datastoreId'); } try { // enables collection sync const putBody = { id: collectionId, syncEnabled: true }; await codeengine.sendRequest( "put", /api/datastores/v1/collections/${collectionId} , JSON.stringify(putBody) ); // forces collection sync await codeengine.sendRequest( "post", /api/datastores/v1/export/${collection.datastoreId} , "" ); } finally { // turns off collection sync - ensure this runs even if sync fails await codeengine.sendRequest( "put", /api/datastores/v1/collections/${collectionId} , JSON.stringify({ id: collectionId, syncEnabled: false }) ); } return { success: true, message: Successfully synchronized collection ${collectionId} }; }

body_text: @IvetteBoutilier17 I have a feeling that has to do with which metrics you are pulling into a single dataset. Not only do you need a different dataset for each time period, you have to carefully craft what data is in each dataset, basically predicting what data I'm going to need. I'll spell out the problem, and my mi-term solution. If I pull in a dataset that has (perhaps among other things): sessions page path + query string page title And then I try to pull the SUM of Sessions… I'm going to get extra numbers. Why? Because the page path + query string does not equal the page title. Sometimes users visit the page with a "/" at the end and sometimes they visit it with a search string at the end, or something else entirely. And sometimes the page title changes (we had a problem for a while where depending on how you reached the page the title might have an em-dash or an en-dash, which Google reads as two different titles. So you might get multiple rows for the same data, combining the different name/ page path combinations. In the dataset above, I would only use it to ask page-specific questions, like How many sessions did we have where users visited this page? How long did users visit this page? And I would find the most commonly used page path and use that data. So… how then, do I find the total number of sessions? I have 5 different datasets for each time period. Basic: This is where I ask how many users, how many sessions, etc) Time frame Users (I started with Total, but Google seems to be favoring Active more and more) Sessions Average Session Duration Page Views: (this is where I ask questions related to interactions with the pages) Time frame Users and sessions (again, these are only used when I have questions related to the pages themselves) Page title Page path User Engagement Views Geography : (this is where I ask questions on where users are located) Time frame Users and sessions (similar to above, these are only used when I have questions related to the geography) City Region Country Browser and Device Category: (this is where I ask questions on the tech my users are on) Time frame Users and sessions (similar to above, these are only used when I have questions related to the device) users are on) Device category Browser Custom: (this is where I ask questions about specific interactions, like buttons, scrolls, links etc.) Time frame Users and sessions (similar to above, these are only used when I have questions related to the interactions) Page path (Pages are there to show me or allow me to filter the custom events based on page) Page title Custom events, like Event Label, Link URL, etc You have probably noticed I don't have any revenue or income-generating analytics. That's because my sites are not income-generating sites, not because I left that out. Also, yes, this a whole lot of different data sets. I'm in the process of moving my data to BigQuery and going to try building out my link from there instead of storing my data in Domo. BigQuery is THE ONLY data storage that does not pull data from GA4 using the API and will actually store the data in the way that GA4 stores it. body_text: Use Case: Domo user uses Jupyter to access an API and get data. One of the fields retrieved is a boolean returning either True or False. This get added in a column in a Pandas dataframe (we'll call it TF) and is written to a Domo dataset using domojupyter.write_dataframe. The dataset is saved and accessible, and the TF column exists with a datatype of integer. However the TF column shows no values in it. It looks like an issue with the API, but it isn't. If we use the dataset as an input to an ETL , we get an error because it can't use TF. It fails on converting string to integer. You have to go into the dataset input tile and change the configuration so TF is a text data type instead. Then the ETL outputs True and False as strings for this column. So while TF data is not visible in the dataset, the value appears to be there. Reason: I think this happends because when the data is added to Pandas dataframe, it recognizes it as a boolean and sets the column dtype to bool. When domo sees a bool column, it sets it's data type to integer because for Domo, a boolean is a numeric 1 or 0 instead of True or False as in python. Domo doesn't fail the dataset write in Jupyter, and it does appear to hold True and False as string values, in a column that is an integer data type. Resolution: The python script was written to see if data is boolean and if so, an if statement converted true and false to a text value (i.e. "Yes", "No"). Alternate options would be to convert True and false to 1 and 0. You could just leave it as it is and allow a domo ETL to make the conversion, but leave the source dataset appearing blank. I didn't like this because I want to make sure I can verify values throughout all stages of transform in Domo. Future: It would be nice if Domo could recognize True and False boolean values from python/pandas when they write to domo datasets and add either allow them to be saved as text or converted to 1 or 0.
title: Pandas Boolean DType Compatibility Issue

body_text: Hello DOMO friends! I'm curious to hear from anyone out there that can share any successes or failures with trying to leverage the "Sandbox" Governance feature to control what is available internally for stakeholders to see, with most folks only looking at "Production" dashboards/cards and with some having access also to a "Development" environment of cards and dashboards. And what processes and procedures did you implement for control over things being released from DEV into PROD? We currently only have one instance (with LOTS of stuff in it) and are wanting to create a new PROD area (not sure how) without adding a second instance - but would be interested to hear also from anyone that maybe added (or had) a second instance and used one instance for DEV and one instance for PROD. And maybe also hear thoughts on the PROs/CONs of trying to make it work in just the one instance (versus two). Thanks all (in advance) for anything you can share! P.S. It seems like there could be a host of complications and limitations with trying to deploy this "Sandbox" solution (with Linked Repositories, etc. ) across all the content we want available in DOMO to our internal stakeholders. Should we rather just re-organize our existing content and leverage the DOMO "Certified Content" option to "stamp" things that are approved for public consumption in the production "section" of our single DOMO instance? body_text: Summary Please create a regular, structured Platform UX and UXR focus group / forum with customers that goes beyond functionality feedback, so Domo can validate usability, workflows, and adoption blockers earlier in betas and across new releases. Problem Platform experience issues (admin and governance flows, publishing and distribution, permissions and roles, data experiences, app building experiences, connectors onboarding, discoverability, and cross instance workflows) often surface late or through reactive escalations. Without a consistent UXR loop, it is hard to validate end to end workflows early, and adoption suffers even when the underlying feature technically works. What we are asking for A lightweight but consistent program that includes: A recurring cadence (example: monthly or per release cycle) for UXR sessions with customer participants. Early access to in progress UX flows (prototypes and designs) for validation before GA. A way to bring customer SMEs in early for topic specific areas (governance and admin, publish and subscribe, App Studio, connectors, cross instance workflows). A visible and traceable feedback loop: what was heard, what changed, what is planned. Why this matters Adoption depends on workflow clarity and usability, not just feature availability. Validating designs with real enterprise use cases reduces rework after GA and prevents “technically shipped but not adoptable” outcomes. A predictable forum allows customers to contribute constructively instead of only reacting after release.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Establish an Ongoing Platform Design Partnership Program (UXR Loop + Early Validation)

body_text: Summary Please add an option for PDP (Row Level Security) to support intersecting (AND-based) evaluation , so that when a user qualifies for multiple PDP policies, access is the least permissive overlap of allowed rows rather than the union. Problem Today, additive evaluation means users in multiple groups can unintentionally gain broader visibility through group stacking. In enterprise environments, users accumulate group memberships over time, and those changes are often managed by IAM or HR systems outside of our team. This creates avoidable governance risk and makes access harder to explain and audit. Why this matters Without intersection, we are forced to create many combined groups and bespoke policies for every permutation, which does not scale. Requested capability Add a PDP evaluation option such as: Evaluation mode: Additive (OR) or Intersecting (AND) Intersecting mode should apply when a user matches multiple PDP policies for the same dataset.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Add Intersecting (AND-Based) PDP Evaluation for Row Level Security

body_text: Domo's NetSuite Writeback connector supports the creation or most types of records. However, some record types are missing. For example, work order completions are missing but could be created if a "transform" operation on the existing "work order" object was possible in the writeback connector. It would be great if some option could be included with the existing NetSuite Object types to use a transform method, or alternatively if the list of supported objects could be expanded to include work order completions.
title: Support For Transform Options In NetSuite Writeback

body_text: To elaborate a bit more, a work order completion in NetSuite can be created very simply via POST /workOrder/{id}/!transform/workOrderCompletion (see NetSuite REST API Browser: Record API | API Reference ). This transformation only requires the item quantity and a couple of other details, everything else is automatically drawn from the parent work order. If Domo had a dedicated option for work order completions in the NetSuite writeback connector, or an additional option to "transform" under the existing work order option, it would work either way. Any other type of record which has a parent-child relationship in NetSuite can be created via an API transform, e.g., a vendor credit from a vendor bill, a cash refund from a return authorization, and so on. Having an additional "transform" option against all existing NetSuite writeback options might greatly increase the number of things which can be written back without making the Domo UI too clunky.
title: Support For Transform Options In NetSuite Writeback

body_text: Hello, we're trying to share private data with external clients without granting them access to our entire Domo tenant. What is the best way to go about this? Below are some of the notes I've gathered but please correct me if I'm wrong on anything. Thanks! Embed - Public (Can't share private data publicly) External user does NOT need a Domo Account Anyone can access the data without PDP If external user go to our tenant URL, they will NOT be able to access it Embed - Private External user DOES need a Domo Account Only SSO or manual credential users can access the data. PDP CAN be applied If external user goes to our tenant URL, they WILL be able to access it Publication Groups How is this different than Embed - Private? New Client Data Instance External user DOES need a Domo Account Only SSO or manual credential users can access the data. PDP CAN be applied If external user goes to our internal URL, they will NOT be able to access it Use "Virtual DataSets" in Governance toolkit to push the needed data from our internal instance to our client instance I've reviewed this post below but it doesn't address that external clients would be able to access the main tenant. Of course, they won't see all the data or dashboards but anything that is shared with all users would be visible to them. https://community-forums.domo.com/main/discussion/comment/103458?tab=all#Comment_103458?utm_source=community-search&utm_medium=organic-search&utm_term=external+sharing

body_text: Hi everyone, I’m running into a CORS issue while trying to call the Grok API (x.ai) from a DOMO Pro Code App. This integration was working earlier today and has been working fine for the past few weeks, but suddenly the request is failing due to a CORS error when the DOMO app tries to call the API directly from the browser. Details: The app is a DOMO Pro Code App (JavaScript). The request is made using fetch() from the DOMO app. The API endpoint is: https://api.x.ai/v1/chat/completions. The request includes an Authorization header (Bearer token). What I’ve tested so far: The same request works perfectly in Postman. The same request works from a Python Flask backend. The issue only occurs when the request is triggered from the DOMO app in the browser. The browser console shows a CORS / preflight failure. This makes it seem like the external API is not accepting the DOMO origin during the browser request. My questions: Are there known restrictions with calling external APIs directly from DOMO Pro Code Apps? Has anyone run into similar CORS issues when integrating external AI APIs with DOMO apps? Any guidance would be appreciated. Thanks!

body_text: I don't think it's a Domo restriction. It might be a CORS policy changes on the API side. That type of error occurs when an API does not want to receive browser requests. Such as those with authorization headers. You could try connecting to the API via Python or Postman to see if you get similar results. If Postman works, that indicates there is no CORS enforcement. If Python works, your server to server appears to bypass any CORS issue.

body_text: We understand the main use for column masking is to protect sensitive data but our use case further extends it to be used to generate Sample data. Currently we create copies of datasets and dashboards for our Sample data which is used for demo/training purpose which requires us to hide/mask data for all the columns. We can use text masking methods but the option for numeric fields is only to be NULL which will not show the visualizations on the dashboards/apps. If we can have masking methods like Random numbers with Seed or operations like below - scale = 0.6 + (MOD(ABS(HASH([Metric])), 8000) / 10000) jitter = 1 + ((MOD(ABS(HASH(CONCAT([Metric],[Date])), 4001) - 2000) / 100000)) Value = Value * scale * jitter Also for text fields options like Regex in a Formula Tile would be helpful. Feature Reference- https://www.domo.com/docs/s/article/36[PHONE]#column_policies Note: Column policies are data type-specific. You can use all masking methods with text-type policies. However, you can only use Nullify and Unmasked with numeric and date/time type policies.

body_text: Currently in Domo, the Transpose option available in the Megatable card works only when the number of columns in the source dataset remains constant. However, in many real-world data scenarios, the number of columns can change between refreshes, making it difficult to reliably restructure the data using the existing functionality. It would be extremely valuable to have a dynamic transpose capability within Magic ETL that can automatically convert columns into rows regardless of how many columns are present in the dataset at the time of refresh. Use Case: Some datasets contain a variable number of columns that represent similar types of data (for example, dynamically generated fields or date-based columns). When these datasets refresh, the column count may increase or decrease. A dynamic transpose function would allow these columns to be flipped into rows automatically without requiring manual updates to the ETL each time the schema changes. Requested Enhancement: Add a Dynamic Transpose (Unpivot All Columns) tile in Magic ETL that can automatically detect and transpose columns regardless of how many exist in the dataset at refresh time.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Dynamic Transpose Tile in Magic ETL for Variable Columns

body_text: Hi Domo Community, I’ve noticed a potential bug while using Domo’s new Semantic Model (Beta) feature and wanted to check if anyone else has experienced this. body_text: I'm struggling to create a dynamic market share calculation. Current calc is done via ETL and is too rigid, and frankly imprecise because the calc is at a monthly level, not the timeframe in which the dashboard may be currently filtered. I really need a Beast Mode solution. The core formula is simple: X sales / all sales The variables are where it gets messy. On the numerator side I can have: - Brand - Retailer - Product - Category The overall dataset - aka "all sales" are: - Date Range - Category - Retailer (NOTE: If Retailer or Category is filtering the numerator it would not be a definer of "all sales") Here's my ideal scenario (no retailer variable): Dashboard Loads Primary Retail Category is selected Market Share calc is [RETAIL CATEGORY SALES] / [ALL SALES] Category 1 is selected Market Share calc is[RETAIL CATEGORY>CATEGORY 1 SALES] / [ALL SALES] Brand is selected Market Share calc is [BRAND SALES] / [RETAIL CATEGORY>CATEGORY 1 SALES] Category 1 is removed Market Share calc is [BRAND SALES] / [RETAIL CATEGORY SALES] Is there a way to pull this off? If not, how can I prevent the filters from impacting the denominators? FYI there's always a date filter but it impacts both sides of the equation.
title: Filters and a formula for market share

body_text: The filters are going to affect both numerator and denominator. Your denominator will need to ignore filters. You can do most of that with FIXED. But you may not get every scenario. SUM(`Sales`) / SUM(SUM(`Sales`)) FIXED (BY `Date`,`Retail_Category`) You said ALL SALES should only depend on: Date Range Retail Category If retailer sometimes applies, you may need to add it as another variant. SUM(`Sales`) / SUM(SUM(`Sales`)) FIXED (BY `Date`,`Retail Category`,`Retailer`) Using sample dataset like this:

body_text: Noticed a few weeks ago that the constrained join feature on the join tile (one-to-many and many-to-one) in Magic ETL does not work, allowing joins that should fail to process. This is a big deal for us as we use the join constraints to ensure we don't have any cartesian joins in our data. This bug has huge implications from a data integrity and reliability standpoint. We've reported it to Domo but it's been a couple weeks now without a fix so wanted to put it on everyone's radar incase you use the feature.
title: BUG - Constrained Joins not working

body_text: Thanks for surfacing this. We're working on figuring out the issue and are hoping to have a resolution soon.
title: BUG - Constrained Joins not working

body_text: @collinT Wanted to close the loop here, if you haven't already received the communication from your CSM or the resolution to your ticket: In May 2024, we introduced a feature allowing users to specify relationship constraints on join conditions (called "Relationship Type"), including Many to Many, One to One, One to Many, and Many to One. Recently, we identified an issue where the asymmetrical join constraints (One to Many and Many to One) were mislabeled and being applied in reverse. Upon discovering this, we immediately paused enforcement of these two constraint types to prevent any unintended impact on your data workflows. As a result: If your Magic ETL DataFlows include join relationships set to One to Many or Many to One, please be aware that these constraints are currently not being enforced . Many to One and One to Many relationships configured in your DataFlows will behave as if no constraint is applied during this pause. We understand how critical data accuracy and relationship enforcement are to your operations. Our team is actively working to determine the best approach to retroactively apply these constraints where possible and ensure proper enforcement going forward. We will provide more information and a fix for this in a coming code release. In the meantime, you may wish to add steps to your DataFlow that allow you to verify that your joins are giving the expected results.
title: BUG - Constrained Joins not working

body_text: This post is to inform you about an important update concerning the Join Data tile in Domo’s Magic ETL tool, specifically related to the Relationship Type settings. In May 2024, we introduced a feature allowing users to specify relationship constraints on join conditions (called "Relationship Type"), including Many to Many, One to One, One to Many, and Many to One. Recently, we identified an issue where the asymmetrical join constraints (One to Many and Many to One) were mislabeled and being applied in reverse. Upon discovering this, we immediately paused enforcement of these two constraint types to prevent any unintended impact on your data workflows. As a result: If your Magic ETL DataFlows include join relationships set to One to Many or Many to One, please be aware that these constraints are currently not being enforced . Many to One and One to Many relationships configured in your DataFlows will behave as if no constraint is applied during this pause. We understand how critical data accuracy and relationship enforcement are to your operations. Our team is actively working to determine the best approach to retroactively apply these constraints where possible and ensure proper enforcement going forward. We will provide more information and a fix for this in a coming code release. In the meantime, you may wish to add steps to your DataFlow that allow you to verify that your joins are giving the expected results. If you have any questions or if you’d like assistance reviewing your DataFlows to understand how this might affect your specific use cases, please don’t hesitate to reach out to me. I am happy to answer questions and provide whatever assistance I can.
title: "Relationship Type" in Join Data tile in Magic ETL

body_text: Hello, I'm trying to have data sent from Domo to an end user based on the results of a form. I have gone through multiple iterations and I finally have it all working correctly. The way I ended up accomplishing this was to use a card, scheduled reports, and a Workflow. My question: Is there a way to send a csv file from Domo without having a link back to Domo to view the card? My reason for this is that ever time the form is submitted, the card overwrites itself so if someone click on the email link, it wouldn't be accurate. Of course, the csv file in the email that is sent would be accurate but if they click on the link in the future, it wont be. I have attached an image of the email I receive from the "Send Card Report to People" action from the Workflow. This doesn't have to use a card, scheduled reports, or workflows. I'm open to any suggestions. This is just how I went about building it. If there are other ways to email data from domo based on the output of a form submission, I'm all ears. Thanks! body_text: Would love if App Studio allowed for custom CSS and potentially JS code injections. This would bridge the gap between the no-code App Studio and the all-code bricks. I am imagining something similar to Squarespace's setup (but for reports instead of a website) where everything is no-code unless you specifically go to the custom CSS and code injection settings. Non-coders would not even notice the option is there, but it would be amazing for users with more specific styling and functionality needs who don't want the work or maintenance of the pro-code editor. I would love this feature since my team builds cards in the Card Analyzer because it is quick, easy, and accessible to all coding levels. Building in the pro-code editor is somewhat off-limits since it requires coding knowledge to maintain and edit, but at the same time we are limited by very simple App Studio theme settings. With this feature, the coders on the team could customize styling while still allowing everyone to work on the content of the app. I would imagine JS code injections would not affect card functionality (otherwise the pro-code editor would be more useful), just the app elements. Personally, I would prioritize custom CSS over code injections, but both would be great!

body_text: If you're using a map type that is based on provinces, then you’ll need to assign ECOM to a valid province value — otherwise you’ll have to switch to a different map type. In the example I shared, the formula substitutes Yukon because it behaves just like a regular province in the map. It’s also a good choice since it has a small population (so it’s unlikely you have physical stores there) and it appears toward the top of Canada, keeping it visually separate from major sales regions. For my own mapping project, I took a list of medical locations and pasted them into an AI chat tool to generate latitude and longitude values in CSV format. I then imported that CSV into Domo and joined it to my main dataset for long/lat mapping.
title: Custom Map for Ecom Store

body_text: Hi, @verytiredgirl - thanks for the question! I'm glad I can weigh in and hopefully address it for you and others. Our long-term strategy is to deprecate the Domo Governance connector and encourage our customers to adopt DomoStats instead. In order to do that, we obviously have to ensure DomoStats provides equivalent data that allow you to answer all the same questions you currently go to the Governance connector for. Our recent release of the PDP - Row Policy reports in DomoStats (currently in beta) is just another step in that direction. Once those reports are available GA, my recommendation to all customers is to use the DomoStats connector for PDP data. And, if you want to use the DomoStats reports in beta, if you're already using these reports and find gaps relative to the Domo Governance connector, please reach out to your Domo account team. Thanks again for the question! -Dan

body_text: I need to know if there is an easy way to create, either within Analyzer or using an ETL, that will allow me to create a financial report showing an Annualized trailing twelve pivot table (or just a table). The attached example is showing a trailing twelve months (one month per column), but I want the columns to show the amount of the current month, plus the prior 11 months. E.g. January would show the sum total of Dec-Jan, February would show Nov-Feb, etc. Any examples or screenshots would be appreciated.
title: Annualized Trailing Twelve Months Financial Reporting

body_text: You should be able to do it with a Magic ETL. Use a Group By to get one row per month. Create a sequential month index using a Rank and Window tile. Partition if needed, ordering by Month ascending. As a row number, call it something like month_rank. Add another branch duplicating it as month_rank_2. Use a join tile and join on the department and month_rank_2 being between month_rank - 11 and month_rank. Then group by current month and department, summing the amount. This would be your trailing 12 total. Jan 2025 = Feb 2024 – Jan 2025 Feb 2025 = Mar 2024 – Feb 2025 Mar 2025 = Apr 2024 – Mar 2025 Such that each month is current month plus prior 11 months.
title: Annualized Trailing Twelve Months Financial Reporting

body_text: The Challenge: Currently, the Dataset via Email connector only supports two update methods: Replace: Wipes the entire dataset and replaces it with the new file. Append: Adds the new file's rows to the bottom of the existing dataset. The Problem: Many external systems and partners send data updates via email (CSV/Excel) that contain a mix of new records and updates to existing records. If we use Replace , we lose historical data that wasn't in the latest email. If we use Append , we create massive duplication. Current Workaround (Pain Point): To handle this, we are forced to build "Landing Pad" architectures: Appending everything to a raw dataset, then building complex Magic ETL DataFlows (using Rank/Window functions) just to deduplicate the data and find the latest version of a row. This wastes storage rows and increases ETL compute time significantly. The Proposed Solution: Please add an "Upsert" option to the Dataset via Email connector settings, similar to how the Workbench or other API connectors function. Allow users to define a "Constraint Key" (or unique identifier column) in the connector configuration. When a new email arrives: If the Key matches an existing row → Update the record. If the Key does not exist → Insert the new record. Value: This would drastically simplify data pipelines for users ingesting flat files, reduce ETL overhead, and keep datasets cleaner and more efficient.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Add "Upsert" (Update based on Key) functionality to the 'Dataset via Email' Connector

body_text: Hi Domosapiens, I've struggled with this concept since I was a wee lad in the data world. All these year later, and it still doesn't make sense to me. This table has the raw data in "Charge Total Amount". The "Monthly ROI Numeraor" has the Charge Total Amount TIMES the Variable that is open input. (for reference, in the screenshot it is 30%) The cost, or the denominator, is $2,500 So, for row three: 21,600 is top line, adjusted to 30% which is 6480. Next, we take that number divided by the monthly cost (2500) to get the "Monthly ROI" column. 6480 / 2500 == 2.592, NOT .65. However, when I aggregate the "Monthly ROI" column, the math now works: I can verify 10,680 / 2500 == 4.27 I know this is a complex question, with considerations for BeastModes and aggregations and groupings, but I'm hoping to create a mental framework to make this make sense - once and for all!
title: Conceptual Understanding - Group Bys & Aggregations

body_text: The big thing when dealing with this at the card level is to be aware of what is in your sorting column as that can break up the aggregation you are trying to achieve. Also, be consistent in your summing in the beast modes. It looks like you aren't doing any aggregation in the beast mode. This will cause your Monthly ROI to evaluate at an individual level, rather than at the aggregated level. I would suggest for each beast mode, you do the SUM inside the beast mode and that should get you what you need.
title: Conceptual Understanding - Group Bys & Aggregations

body_text: You asked for a conceptual explanation, so let me see if I can try one. Let's say I have 3 days of data. I'll simplify the numbers to make things more obvious. Viewed by day: Above, you can see each day's "Monthly ROI" is 3/1 =3. 30/10 =3. 300/100 =3. When I group by month, what happens? It correctly summed 3 + 3 + 3, which is not the same as 333/111. It's doing (3/1) + (30/10) + (300/100). Basically, doing each day's math and then doing its best to roll it up into the month. If I change my BeastMode to sum(`Monthly ROI Numerator`)/sum(`Cost Amount`) per Mark's suggestion, that changes the math to (3 + 30 + 300)/(1 + 10 + 100) = 3
title: Conceptual Understanding - Group Bys & Aggregations

body_text: My understanding is that in MySQL dataflows, the Explain SQL is only available in some SQL types (like Redshift). As for performance issues….it's always useful to filter the data up front to put less stress on the SQL engine. But some things like joining on CAST values are a performance killers. ON CAST(c.id AS SIGNED) = CAST(t.entity_id AS SIGNED) This is because SQL must compute the cast for every row and prevents indexing. Even if the dataset is less than a thousand rows it has a serious impact on performance. Joins using LIKE can also take a performance hit because it is not a direct comparison and requires pattern matching.
title: My SQL Dataflow: Explain SQL

body_text: As I'm working on creating a View I'll often try to save my view but I get a very unhelpful error: "Unable to save {view name}". It's not a permissions issue and I've created the view using both SQL Editor and the UI tools. I've combed through the data types and they are correct. I'm trying to use a UNION (which doesn't seem to work at all in the SQL Editor) and can get the correct data to show, but then I can't save. Extremely frustrating that the error message is no help. It's happened to me when trying to do multiple different views. This is the first with a UNION.
title: Can't Save View

body_text: I can think of a couple possible things that might cause an issue. Use named fields. Do not use an asterisk in a SELECT statement. Try UNION ALL rather than just UNION. Union removes duplicate rows, while UNION ALL includes all rows. Make sure your fields are consistent with aliases and types. Try your view out with just a couple fields at first to see if you can identity an offending field as the issue. You may need to use CAST to make sure a field matches on data type to the other side of the union. Such as CAST(order_id AS VARCHAR) as order_id. Verify you don't have duplicate names or aliases in your select. Such as SELECT id, order_id as id. Eliminate functions and simplify queries with CTE or row number. And if all else fails, use a Magic ETL.
title: Can't Save View

body_text: Currently, Domo does not support column-level security. When sharing dashboards or apps with external users, there is no native way to hide specific columns within a dataset. Current Workaround Create a separate, trimmed dataset via ETL Remove restricted columns Build external dashboards/apps on that dataset and not on original dataset. Workaround Limitations This leads to: Dataset duplication Additional ETL pipelines to maintain Increased governance and maintenance overhead Risk of inconsistencies between internal and external datasets Requested Enhancement Introduce column-level security controls at the dashboard or app level so a single governed dataset can be reused safely while restricting specific columns for external users. This would simplify architecture, reduce operational overhead, and improve governance for partner-facing and embedded analytics use cases.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Add Column-Level Security for Domo Apps and External Users (Without Requiring Separate Datasets)

body_text: Currently, when mapping datasets to Filter Views in the Dashboard Filter View, Domo consistently prioritizes the dataset of the first card on the dashboard. If a user attempts to filter for an attribute that does not exist in the first card’s dataset—even if it does exist in the second or third card’s dataset—the filter returns no results or fails to apply correctly. The Use Case Consider a dashboard designed for order management: Card A (Top): A "Backlog Report" showing only Open Orders . Card B (Bottom): A "Shipment Report" showing Closed/Shipped Orders . If a user searches for a specific Order Number (field in both datasets) that has already been closed, the filter fails to find it because it looks at the Backlog dataset first. Because the order is no longer in the backlog, it appears as though the data doesn't exist, even though it is present in the Shipment dataset right below it. The Current (Suboptimal) Workaround The current fix is to move the Shipment report to the top of the dashboard. However, this is not ideal from a logical reporting standpoint . The Backlog report is the primary driver of the business process and belongs at the top; we shouldn't have to compromise the visual hierarchy and "story" of a dashboard just to make the filtering logic function. Proposed Solution I propose a way to manually designate a Primary Mapping Dataset for filters, or a logic update where: The filter scans all mapped datasets for the value. Users can "rank" the priority of datasets in the Filter View settings, independent of the physical card layout on the page.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Filter Views should filter on all cards with equal priority

body_text: Current behavior: An ETL execution with multiple output datasets will be labeled with "Successful" status after any one of the outputs has finished indexing. If outputs vary significantly in size, larger outputs may not finish indexing (and therefore will not have new/updated data available) for some time after the ETL execution is marked as "Successful". Expected/desired behavior: An ETL execution with multiple output datasets should be labeled with "Successful" status only after all of the outputs have finished indexing (i.e., "Successful" indicates all data processed by the ETL execution is fully available). Until that time, ETL status of "Running Indexing" would be more appropriate.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Label ETL execution "Successful" only after all outputs have been indexed

body_text: It also seems as though any cards on output datasets attempt to refresh as soon as the DataFlow/ETL is considered "Successful," even if the specific output dataset powering the card isn't done processing/indexing. This results in blank cards with "no data in filtered range" until the actual output you're using is done indexing 15-20 minutes later. Solutions might include what I mentioned above (Successful only after all outputs are indexed) or cards listening for their particular dataset to reindex rather than attempting to refresh as soon as the ETL is done.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Label ETL execution "Successful" only after all outputs have been indexed

body_text: When you publish or update an app, Domo reinitializes the app state, so in-app filter selections aren’t persisted and queues reset to their default state. One way to minimize the impact is to design queues with personalization (for example using USER() in Beast Modes or variables). This allows queues to auto-filter to the logged-in user by default, so even after an app reset users land back in their own queue.

body_text: I have a drop down filter using the Month End Date column → Added this drop down on an App → Created a filter view to pre-select the most current month '2026-02-28' However, I want this drop down filter to always have something selected (so using filter view ensure you have something pre-selected at the start). However, there is nothing stopping user from clearing the pre-selected value, they can clear it by: 1. Click on Control → Clear filter view 2. Hover over the drop down filter card, they will see a clear filter icon 3. I also have a button on this App, which I enabled 'Clear Filters' action, hence when user click on this button, it will clear all filters.
title: Drop Down Filter Card - default selection and not allow user to clear filter, is it possible?

body_text: The way Domo cards work, you can pre-select a value using a filter (you are already doing this). Users can clear this filter. There are many ways to implement behavior. You can also create beast mode to enforce a default such as CASE WHEN `Month End Date` IS NULL THEN '2026‑02‑28' ELSE `Month End Date` END Or use a dynamic filter.
title: Drop Down Filter Card - default selection and not allow user to clear filter, is it possible?

body_text: HI, How can I check our current Domo build version and verify if there are any available updates for our installed Domo tools?
title: How to find the domo version?

body_text: Domo is a cloud-based SaaS (Software as a Service) platform, and as such it doesn’t typically have a single, standalone version number that you install and manage like desktop applications. Instead, the platform is continuously updated by Domo across the cloud infrastructure with new features, improvements, and security updates rolled out over time. This means: There’s no traditional “Version 1.2 → Version 1.3 → Version 2.0” You will get the latest updates automatically as part of the service. Are you referring to a specific downloaded feature like a Powerpoint Plugin or Workbench?
title: How to find the domo version?

body_text: Hi, Thank you for the reply. Are you referring to a specific downloaded feature like a Powerpoint Plugin or Workbench?. Both
title: How to find the domo version?

body_text: I am not sure for tool plugins, I would just recommend downloading the latest version here: YOURCOMPANY.domo.com/admin/tooldownloads
title: How to find the domo version?

body_text: Hi, Thank you for the reply. Is the DOMO Workbench version the same as the actual DOMO version we use to build visualizations?.
title: How to find the domo version?

body_text: No. Workbench has it's own version. It is a client-side Windows application that you install locally. As @ColemenWilson mentioned, Domo is a SaaS production. You don't install or manage versions yourself. Updates roll out continuously. You will not see anything like "Domo version X.x".
title: How to find the domo version?

body_text: Is there any native table property or "HTML/Image" data type trick that allows for a dropdown component, or is the standard card limited strictly to data display and 'Action' links?. If I need to go the custom route, would you recommend building a Custom App using the Domo App Framework (React/Vue), or is there a way to leverage the Table-Custom App type to achieve this?. If I implement a dropdown in a Custom App, what is the current best practice for handling the writeback to the underlying Dataset? (e.g., using the Domo API or a specific connector).Whether cost is incurred if so what is the charge?. What is the alternate option to avoid app cards for any drop down requirement within a card?.
title: Implementing In-Cell Dropdown Selectors: Standard Table Card vs. Custom App (DDX)

body_text: You could make a dropdown in an html card. Which would look just like a regular table card…but alas, how would you get the selected value to pass back to the Domo filters. You could create a custom app or use a brick.
title: Implementing In-Cell Dropdown Selectors: Standard Table Card vs. Custom App (DDX)

body_text: Hi, Thank you for the reply. Could you suggest which custom app to use? If the custom app does not provide the expected solution, what alternative Domo chart type should be considered?.
title: Implementing In-Cell Dropdown Selectors: Standard Table Card vs. Custom App (DDX)

body_text: A true dropdown component is not supported in standard table cards. Those cards are intentionally limited to data display and navigation actions. If dropdown behavior is required within the card itself, a custom app (via the Domo App Framework) is an appropriate path, with writeback handled through Domo APIs. However, it’s worth stepping back to clarify the requirement. In many cases, a dropdown is not about editing data but about selecting a value to dynamically control what is shown. For that use case, native Domo features such as page filters (pfilters) or selector-style interactions are often a simpler solution and avoid the need for a custom app. A common approach in Domo is to use a dashboard page with a filter card. The filter acts like a dropdown and sits on the page with your tables or charts. When a user makes a selection, all cards on that page update based on that choice, as long as they’re using the same dataset or field. This gives you dropdown-style behavior without needing a custom app.
title: Implementing In-Cell Dropdown Selectors: Standard Table Card vs. Custom App (DDX)

body_text: In our Domo Sandbox environment, we initially deployed multiple dashboards under a single Pages repository all utilizing a shared dataset. We now plan to deploy an additional dashboard using the same dataset. We're unsure whether it's necessary to create a separate repository for each dashboard deployment. Additionally we've encountered a challenge: whenever we add a new dashboard to the shared repository we are required to reselect all previously deployed dashboards during the promotion to production. This process is cumbersome even though we're consistently using the latest version of the dataset.
title: Managing Multiple Dashboards in a Single Repository: Promotion Workflow Issue

body_text: Hi Pari! Is there a question related to your issue that the community could help answer?
title: Managing Multiple Dashboards in a Single Repository: Promotion Workflow Issue

body_text: You don’t need a separate repository for each dashboard, but using one repository for many dashboards can make promotions harder. Since everything is grouped together, Domo requires you to reselect all dashboards each time you promote anything new. If you want to avoid that extra work, it’s easier to give each dashboard its own repository so you can promote them independently without having to redo previous selections.
title: Managing Multiple Dashboards in a Single Repository: Promotion Workflow Issue

body_text: NO
title: Managing Multiple Dashboards in a Single Repository: Promotion Workflow Issue

body_text: If multiple dashboards depend on the same dataset, try : Put that dataset in its own repository (e.g., Shared_Datasets). Deploy that shared repo first. Then link the dashboards’ repositories to those datasets (they’ll reference the production copies after deployment).
title: Managing Multiple Dashboards in a Single Repository: Promotion Workflow Issue

Requested Functionality Provide a Date Range Filter with the following requirements: Two required inputs: Start Date End Date For each date: User can type a date directly into the field User can select a date from a calendar picker Calendar picker: Uses a single-month view Supports month/year navigation Filter applies at the dashboard level like other filter cards Supports DATE and DATETIME fields Supports default values and persistent selections Expected Behavior Data is filtered to values between Start Date and End Date Manual entry and calendar selection stay synchronized Validation prevents invalid ranges (e.g., End Date earlier than Start Date) Business Value Improves usability for business and executive users Reduces reliance on Beast Modes, variables, and workarounds Aligns Domo with standard UX patterns in enterprise analytics tools Lowers training and support costs Use Cases Financial and accounting period analysis Operational reporting with exact date requirements Historical trend analysis Executive dashboards requiring fast, precise filtering

body_text: The current magic ETL history page for any particular ETL shows the run successes near the top of the page, in a style that looks similar to a history of git-commits. Hovering over a square shows the number of successful runs on that date. We would like to implement some method of process control visible to all domo users and feel that this space would be a good location to start. I think that a more useful purpose of this space would be to show the run time history of that ETLs executions as a process control chart. Instead of showing green squares to indicate that date had a successful run, can this instead be a time chart that shows that last n-number of runs and (on the y-axis) show the run time for those runs? Each run can be marked via a point on a trend line, and each point can still be marked red or green for success or failure. This still allows users to see the same information of run success status, but also provides the run time as a trend over the last n-number of runs. This is helpful to identify ETLs that are starting to uptick in process time, or identify ETLs that happened to take longer than usual. Attached is an image of a Control Chart that displays the idea behind statistical process control. The x-axis would display the start times of magic ETLs and the y axis would be the execution time. Ideally, we would be able to apply control limits to these charts and set alerts on them, giving us full SPC capability within Domo!
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Add Magic ETL Runtime History to History tab

body_text: I am doing sales modeling in Domo and have a column for model (`Account Payments (cash, model)`) and a column for actuals (`Account Payments (cash, actuals, projected`). For my forecast I project the actuals to the model for the months that have not yet occurred. My issue is that my actuals are outperforming the model and I'd like to see where I'd end up if the deviation from model I've seen this YTD held through for the remainder of the year. How might I calc that in a beast mode so I only use the % deviation through the current date and then apply that to future months? The following works for the individual rows but when I attempt to sum for the subtotal/total, the card gets an error (I am plotting this on a pivot table). -- Step 1: Measures deviation from model SUM(CASE WHEN `Month` <= CURDATE() THEN `Account Payments (cash, actuals, projected)` END) / SUM(CASE WHEN `Month` <= CURDATE() THEN `Account Payments (cash, model)` END) — Step 2: Apply to the model values `Account Payments (cash, model)` * `Deviation Ratio` When I attempt to change step 2 to the following, it does not work and throws the error: -- Erroneous calulation that shows what I'm trying to do sum(`Account Payments (cash, model)` * `Deviation Ratio`)
title: Sales Modeling Correction Calculation in Pivot Table

body_text: Does this work? sum(`Account Payments (cash, model)`) *AVG( `Deviation Ratio`)
title: Sales Modeling Correction Calculation in Pivot Table

body_text: I believe David is onto the basic problem…aggregation. Something like this should work: SUM(row_value) × aggregated_metric Something like this will not: SUM(row_value × aggregated_metric) Your deviation ratio is already an aggregated calculation because it uses SUM. And Domo isn't allowing nested aggregations.
title: Sales Modeling Correction Calculation in Pivot Table

body_text: Would there be a way to adjust the deviation ratio to allow this to work as expected?
title: Sales Modeling Correction Calculation in Pivot Table

body_text: Trying taking your deviation formula, in whole, and put it into your next step. Account Payments (cash, model) * ( SUM(CASE WHEN Month <= CURDATE() THEN Account Payments (cash, actuals, projected) END) / SUM(CASE WHEN Month <= CURDATE() THEN Account Payments (cash, model) END) ) And since you don't want a divide by zero, you could do something like SUM(`Account Payments (cash, model)`) * ( SUM( CASE WHEN `Month` <= CURDATE() THEN `Account Payments (cash, actuals, projected)` END ) / NULLIF( SUM( CASE WHEN `Month` <= CURDATE() THEN `Account Payments (cash, model)` END ), 0 ) )
title: Sales Modeling Correction Calculation in Pivot Table

body_text: This looks correct for January but the values are blank for February-December. Those months should be using the adjustment from January
title: Sales Modeling Correction Calculation in Pivot Table

body_text: I have a YTD Performance card that includes the following metrics: Actual Budget Projected EOY Accruals Variance (Actual vs. Budget) On the dashboard, there is a Month slicer that allows users to select values such as Jan 2026, Dec 2025, Nov 2025, Jun 2025 , etc. Requirement The requirement is to display Year-to-Date (YTD) values from the beginning of the selected year up to the selected month based on the month filter that is having values month-year as june 2025 . Examples: If a user selects March 2026 , the card should display data from January 2026 through March 2026 . If a user selects June 2025 , the card should display data from January 2025 through June 2025 . Problem When a month (for example, June 2025 ) is selected using the Month slicer, the dataset is filtered to only that specific month , which breaks the YTD calculation. I understand that this is the expected behavior of dashboard filters in Domo. To address this, I tried using a date variable so users could select a date and then calculate YTD values using Beast Mode. However, this approach negatively impacts the user experience because: Users prefer selecting Month and Year , rather than a specific date. Variables do not support dynamically displaying or deriving Month-Year values directly from the dataset. Questions Is there a way to allow users to select Month and Year only and still use that selection within Beast Mode for YTD calculations without filtering out earlier months? Can variables be configured to dynamically display or derive Month-Year values from the dataset? Are there any recommended best-practice approaches in Domo to achieve correct YTD behavior while maintaining a clean and intuitive user experience when users select a value such as June 2025 from the filter? Any suggestions or guidance would be greatly appreciated. Thanks in advance!
title: YTD calculation breaks when using Month filter in Domo – best practice?

body_text: In Domo, YTD breaks when you use a month filter because filters remove prior months (history) before beast modes run. I'd try to use a variable - or handle it in Magic ETL using a month-year field and pre-calculating YTD by year and month.
title: YTD calculation breaks when using Month filter in Domo – best practice?

body_text: We're attempting to access our GA4 data through the BigQuery cloud connector and are running into two problems. Has anyone come across the same and solved for them? 1. If I use Domo to directly connect to a table in BigQuery, it's only one single day's data. I'd have to set up a different dataset/connection for each new day- absolutely not sustainable. Is there a different solution than to create a new view in BigQuery with all the days' data? 2. Most of the important data I need is coming all bundled up into one single. field, "event params." How are you getting around this?
title: Recommendations for connecting to GA4 data through the BigQuery cloud connector?

body_text: I don't work with BigQuery, but there are documentation pages that show example queries. https://developers.google.com/analytics/bigquery/basic-queries https://developers.google.com/analytics/bigquery/advanced-queries The documentations shows that the specifics (ie. fields) are nested as you stated. The page for basic queries and advanced (in the links above) show examples of how you can query to un-nest them. SELECT event_date, event_timestamp, user_pseudo_id, event_name, (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS page_location, (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_title') AS page_title, (SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_id') AS session_id FROM `your_project.your_dataset.events_*` {edit} The page also shows examples of date range criteria, stating it is done like this : WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201201' AND '20201202'
title: Recommendations for connecting to GA4 data through the BigQuery cloud connector?

body_text: @KristinDavis BQ supports using wildcards in their SQL, so you can create a view on the BQ side that unions all the tables together. The SQL would look something like this: SELECT PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', event_date) AS date, COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) AS total_users, COUNTIF(event_name = 'user_engagement') AS active_users, COUNTIF(event_name = 'session_start') AS sessions, COUNT(event_name) AS events FROM your_project_id.your_dataset_id.events_* GROUP BY date ORDER BY date DESC;
title: Recommendations for connecting to GA4 data through the BigQuery cloud connector?

body_text: Hi @KristinDavis, The above answers are great and give you a few options. What my team has done at DOMO is a combination of the two. We are using the native Cloud Integration to connect read/write to our BigQuery account. We are using Magic ETL and the SQL tile in conjunction with BigQuery SQL Dialect to use pushdown SQL directly to BigQuery. This query is BOTH unnesting and flatting out each field we want and using a wildcard in the FROM clause to query across all the events_ tables at once. This allows us to access 200M rows of our Raw GA4 events data directly in Domo as well as keeps all the UNNEST logic in a single place enabling version control and governance. We've found this helps with three things: Speed: this method allows my team to access the our full UNNESTed events from BQ within Domo without having to import 200M rows of data and wait for that to complete on schedule. Version Control: Keeps all our SQL logic in Domo for version control with the Dataflow instead of saved, scheduled query in BigQuery. Governance and accessibility: Keeping all the logic in Domo in a Dataflow means we can share the Cloud Integration and Edit Writes of DataFlows to other team members without giving them access to the BQ Account and instance GUI. The screenshots below shows the SQL Tile as a first input without any Input DataSet, this directly feeds an Output DataSet. Our real configuration is a little more complex as we then apply some specific aggregation and other formulas using Magic ETL to create a few different Output DataSet. As well as Cloud Integration setup screens, this is different than using Domos BQ Connector.
title: Recommendations for connecting to GA4 data through the BigQuery cloud connector?

body_text: Interestingly, we did try to make a view with multiple tables. Have you imported a view into Domo? Has it worked?
title: Recommendations for connecting to GA4 data through the BigQuery cloud connector?

body_text: This is great- thank you. It helped us move on our way
title: Recommendations for connecting to GA4 data through the BigQuery cloud connector?

body_text: For anyone who needs to know this in the future, here's who we ultimately solved for this: 1. If I use Domo to directly connect to a table in BigQuery, it's only one single day's data. I'd have to set up a different dataset/connection for each new day- absolutely not sustainable. Is there a different solution than to create a new view in BigQuery with all the days' data? We made a combined table in BigQuery and used wildcards to incorporate fields that are in some properties and not others. Note: It's a table, not a view, as it does not appear Domo can ingest table data. 2. Most of the important data I need is coming all bundled up into one single. field, "event params." How are you getting around this? We had to both unnest the fields and pivot them. For example if I have a page view where one field is Event Category (button, search, link), and another field is Event Label (the actual identifier), simply unnesting them means I get one line for Event Cagoery and one line for Event Label. I cannot then make a table that shows me the Event Labels for all events with a certain Event Category (example: show me all the search terms my users entered, so show me all the Event Labels for the events where the Event Category is Search). Therefore for our unnesting had to include a pivot.
title: Recommendations for connecting to GA4 data through the BigQuery cloud connector?

body_text: What I'm trying to achieve: Get the rows with the latest/smallest rank per user based on a given date. I created a calculated field called "Indicator" and I filter on it as "Indicator = 1". I wanted this field to indicate 1 when a transaction is the smallest rank number for a user and 0 if not. What my calculated field "Indicator" looks like: case when MIN(MIN(CASE WHEN Date <= Date 1 THEN Ranked Completion ELSE 1000 END)) FIXED(BY Marketing Cloud Visitor ID ) = Ranked Completion then 1 else 0 end Where as: Date 1 is the specified date that we want to look back from Ranked Completion is a column that ranks each transaction (the most recent transaction being 1 and second-most-recent being 2 and so on) for each user Marketing Cloud Visitor ID is unique ID of our users The warning message I get: This calculation uses both aggregated and non-aggregated columns. This may result in duplicate rows and unexpected behavior in charts. See this article for more information It still lets me save and use the field in a table but when I try to remove from the table and use it as a filter only, it shows the following error message "An invalid column was specified in your request (the column does not exist on the DataSet)." I can hide the "Indicator" column in a table so that is not a big issue but I'd love to create other visualizations such as Donut, Bar and Single Value graphs. However, I cannot make them if the "Indicator" field has to be present. Is there a way to fix my issue or an alternative line of code I can use to achieve the same goal?

body_text: FLOOR(X) Returns the largest integer value not greater than X. CEILING(X) Returns the smallest integer value not less than X. When using FLOOR or CEILING on calculating a column in Magic ETL, they will return the same value. Solution! CASE WHEN MOD(Calculation) != 0 THEN FLOOR (or CEILING) (Calculation)+1 ELSE FLOOR (or CEILING) (Calculation) END
title: Magic ETL ceiling and floor return identical values on decimal

body_text: We've noticed that if we change the update method of an existing dataset to Partition from replace, we end up with two records in the dataset for every new one (and both of them look identical, down to the field we're using for partitioning): it was quite the shock to see a dataset I expected to have 91 million rows suddenly had 182 million. The obvious takeaway is that we probably should start from scratch when using partitions, but the benefits of converting existing ETLs is too strong a siren song for me to resist. Two questions: Has anyone else noticed this? Both of us here got bit by this, so I want to know if it's a general bug, if it just affects our instance, or if we're doing it wrong and it's Working As Designed™. What would be a way around this? If I have other ETLs downstream of the dataset I don't want to delete the existing one and start from scratch unless I absolutely have to. My quick-and-probably-inefficient idea is to store the data to a secondary dataset (deduping if necessary), set the original to partition, and figure out how to use the even more beta feature to tell it to keep no partitions. Let it run once to clear out the dataset, then reimport the data from the secondary dataset and send it back to the original. Any help would be appreciated.
title: Changing dataset update method from Replace to Partition doubles data

body_text: This sounds like a bug. I'd recommend logging a ticket with Domo Support.
title: Changing dataset update method from Replace to Partition doubles data

body_text: @Chinmay_Totekar I believe the ticket was closed, with the unsatisfying conclusion that this was best for starting with new dataset, not converting existing ones. I did find two ways around it, though: For the first one, make a clone of the dataset using the Schema Management tool (Admin » Governance Toolkit » Schema Management), making sure to have it copy the data. Once done, use the same tool to clear the data out, then temporarily rewrite the ETL to set the output dataset to partitioning and bring in the cloned data and write the data out. It's kind of a pain, but it's what I've been doing for the past couple of years. Last month I decided to take the Upsert and Partitioning in Magic ETL self-paced course in Domo University. At around the 25 minute mark in the video it talks about using the CLI tool to partition the dataset for you. I haven't tested it, but it does look like it would work. You'll probably still want to make a clone of the original dataset just in case something goes wrong, but this may be your best bet.
title: Changing dataset update method from Replace to Partition doubles data

body_text: Every now and then, one or several of our ETL's or workbench jobs will become stuck in the refreshing process. So, flows or sets that otherwise take a couple minutes or couple hours to refresh will be stuck refreshing for over 20+ hours. Since email alerts only come in when jobs fail and these technically have not "failed," I often discover these situations much, much later than I'd like to. My thought was to use domostats.datasets, set it to refresh every 6 hours, and when a dataset's "last_run_date" is >= 6 hours from the current time, then send an alert. However, I found that I cannot refresh domostats.datasets more frequently than daily. My next thought was to use numeric fields that should be growing with every refresh (for example, every new registered donation id is a larger number/incremental) and set my summ num as the MAX number of [today], and so if it hasn't changed in several hours, the dataset likely has not refreshed. But, the alert option is to review the rules after each time the dataset updates (which doesn't help in this case) or review the rule hourly, which would just lead to us getting 50 false alarms a day. Just thought I'd check if anyone had any ideas.
title: Alerts for when datasets are "stuck" in refreshing process

body_text: @Jbrorby you can actually run DomoStats connectors more frequently than daily. The easiest for me personally is to set up a quick workflow that has a timer trigger (for example hourly) and a single action called "Run Connector" which is a native Domo function.
title: Alerts for when datasets are "stuck" in refreshing process

body_text: Hello. I have a Beast Mode calculation with the following general structure: CONCAT( DATE_FORMAT((CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY),'%a'), ': ', COUNT(CASE WHEN (DATE(`Opened At`) = (CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY)) THEN `Opened At` END) ) Note that there are just two calculations there. The full version has many more, but this illustrates the problem. When I run that code, I get the message "No data in filtered range". Now, the strange thing is that, if I leave only one of the calculations, like this: CONCAT(DATE_FORMAT((CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY),'%a')) or this: CONCAT(COUNT(CASE WHEN (DATE(`Opened At`) = (CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY)) THEN `Opened At` END)) it works properly. The single value is displayed properly. But putting both calculations, even without the ': ', fails. What's the deal with that? Thank you in advance.
title: Why does my Beast Mode concatenation fail when individual elements work?

body_text: You have an aggregation with a non-aggregated formula. I think it's having a problem grouping. It can do the date_format by itself but not while trying to do the count. What happens if you wrap the data format with a MIN statement?
title: Why does my Beast Mode concatenation fail when individual elements work?

body_text: Thanks for the reply. I'm a little new at this, so I might have missed something. Do you mean that this: COUNT( CASE WHEN (DATE(`Opened At`) = (CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY)) THEN `Opened At` END ) is non-aggregated? I thought that the bold part above would produce multiple values, while the italicized COUNT would aggregate. I would expect that to produce a single value, and when I test it alone, like this: CONCAT(COUNT(CASE WHEN (DATE(`Opened At`) = (CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY)) THEN `Opened At` END)) it does work, producing a single value. Is that what you're referring to?
title: Why does my Beast Mode concatenation fail when individual elements work?

body_text: Both parts are valid. This is non-aggregated: DATE_FORMAT((CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY),'%a') This is aggregated: COUNT( CASE WHEN DATE(`Opened At`) = (CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY) THEN `Opened At` END ) The CASE produces row-level values, and COUNT aggregates them into a single result. So each works on its own, but not together. An aggregation is a "grouping". Group things to count them, sub them up, find the minimum value, etc. Your formula appears to be trying to do aggregate values with non aggregates. You need to make everything an aggregate. My suggestion is that because the date value is constant anyway, just wrap it in a MIN container so Domo sees it as an aggregate: CONCAT( MIN(DATE_FORMAT((CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY),'%a')), ': ', COUNT( CASE WHEN DATE(`Opened At`) = (CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY) THEN `Opened At` END ) )
title: Why does my Beast Mode concatenation fail when individual elements work?
