It would be helpful to add definitions to the documentation so that admins can better leverage this data.\"}],\"type\":\"p\"},{\"type\":\"p\",\"children\":[{\"text\":\"\"},{\"type\":\"rich_embed_inline\",\"dataSourceType\":\"url\",\"url\":\"https:\\\/\\\/domo-support.domo.com\\\/s\\\/article\\\/36[PHONE]?language=en_US\",\"embedData\":{\"body\":\"\",\"url\":\"https:\\\/\\\/domo-support.domo.com\\\/s\\\/article\\\/36[PHONE]?language=en_US\",\"embedType\":\"link\",\"name\":\"Customer Support Community\",\"faviconUrl\":\"\\\/minasan\\\/resource\\\/partnerCommunityFiles\\\/images\\\/favicons.png\"},\"children\":[{\"text\":\"https:\\\/\\\/domo-support.domo.com\\\/s\\\/article\\\/36[PHONE]?language=en_US\"}]},{\"text\":\"\"}]}]","format":"rich2","dateInserted":"2023-03-22T20:20:12+00:00","insertUser":{"userID":17466,"name":"MichelleH","url":"https:\/\/community-forums.domo.com\/main\/profile\/MichelleH","photoUrl":"https:\/\/us.v-cdn.net\/6032830\/uploads\/userpics\/ZLTW747V6ABZ\/nA5DJFP9SALEX.png","dateLastActive":"2025-09-12T12:04:22+00:00","banned":0,"punished":0,"private":false,"label":"Coach ","labelHtml":"Coach "},"displayOptions":{"showUserLabel":false,"showCompactUserInfo":true,"showDiscussionLink":true,"showPostLink":true,"showCategoryLink":false,"renderFullContent":false,"expandByDefault":false},"url":"https:\/\/community-forums.domo.com\/main\/discussion\/57717\/documentation-on-activity-log-event-action-definitions","embedType":"quote","name":"Documentation on Activity Log Event\/Action Definitions","embedStyle":"rich_embed_card"}"> https://community-forums.domo.com/main/discussion/57717/documentation-on-activity-log-event-action-definitions VIEWED Definition: A user opened or clicked into a card, page, or app tab. Does it include scrolling past? No—scrolling past a card without clicking does not count as a "VIEWED" action. Contextual nuance: If your app has multiple tabs, a user must actively click into a tab or card for it to register as "VIEWED". EXPORTED Definition: A user exported data from a card—typically to Excel, CSV, or PDF. Does it require viewing first? Surprisingly, no. Users can export directly from a dashboard or app view without formally triggering a "VIEWED" event. Why more exports than views? This can happen if users use bulk export features or export from summary views without clicking into individual cards

body_text: Also, the email that you're using there is a user task. A user task is a very structured email that prompts the user for a response. In this case, you'd want to use the Domo Notifications package and the send email function to just send an email. To streamline this, you can just make that tool available to the agent and tell the agent to send the email. If you'd rather do that outside of the agent, you can edit the agents output to include an email body and a subject line, and then utilize those later on in your workflow. I've taken both approaches for various reasons.

body_text: I'm hoping someone can help me think of a creative solution for this. My company publishes dashboards and datasets to all of our Domo Everywhere subscriber sites. We can use the "share publication to Default group" option in the new Templates feature to share the dashboards and datasets to everyone in the instance. We want to be able to publish the dashboards to a smaller group of users but still publish the datasets to the Default group. If I share the publication to the smaller group, then separately share each dataset to the Default group, it works until we add new datasets (which is likely). At that point we'd need to go into every subscriber site to share the new dataset to the Default group since it would only be shared to the smaller group via the publication. If I share the publication to the Default group, then go in and remove the Default group from the dashboard sharing. That works fine until I have to update the publication. At that point the dashboards get re-shared to the Default group. If I create a publication with the datasets to share to the Default group, and another publication with the dashboards to share to the smaller group, they'd have two copies of all the datasets that feed the dashboards. Do you see any value in differentiating the various uses of DataSets that could all be considered "view"? For example Do you differentiate between viewing the dataset through the lens of a DataSet View or Card versus viewing the DataSet in the Data Center? Do you differentiate viewing that the DataSet exists (i.e., can see it in a list, see metadata, etc) versus viewing the actual data in the DataSet? body_text: Thanks for the thoughtful questions. My main goal with a “view-only” permission is to let users safely inspect and use datasets without any ability to modify or delete them. They should be able to explore and analyze data, and build Cards or Dataset Views, but not make any changes to the dataset itself. I’m less concerned about metadata visibility — the priority is preventing edits to dataset values or schema, and also avoiding duplicate or “rogue” datasets that could arise if users tried to extract the data elsewhere. Essentially, what’s missing today is a “Data Viewer” role: someone who can safely consume and build from data while keeping the source dataset intact. For example, this would be perfect for new or junior employees who need access to data for learning, exploration, or reporting, without risking changes to the source. That said, I do see how your questions point toward a broader permission model that could benefit all users. A simple hierarchy could look like this: View Metadata – See that a dataset exists (name, owner, columns, etc.) but not the data itself. View & Use Data – Open and inspect dataset contents, and build Cards or Dataset Views, without editing, deleting, or updating the dataset. Admin / Editor – Full control over dataset structure and content. For my use case, the “View & Use Data” level is what we need, but this hierarchy could support governance and flexibility for other organizations as well.

body_text: I think this is a great idea! If I could suggest another idea to do two view permissions (with and without sharing) in the hierarchy. It gets hard to control access to datasets when datasets automatically get shared when a dashboard/card is shared with people individually. View & Use Data without Sharing – Open and inspect dataset contents, and build Cards or Dataset Views, without editing, deleting, or updating the dataset. Admin / Editor – Full control over dataset structure and content. (only the dataset owner should be able to make changes to the data and schedule) I'm not sure exactly how this would work, since users with sharing permissions can still share it to other users individually. Another idea is to have some setting that only allows datasets/cards/dashboards/apps with groups and not individual users (except the owners).

body_text: It would be nice to have more granular control over the Domo API access. Currently, if we want to push data to Domo with the Domo API, it requires the user to have the "Manage Dataset" grant. Since this is considered an admin grant, it inherently allows access to all datasets within Domo and overrides any PDPs. In reality, if someone gains unauthorized access to those keys they could do get all datasets and use the dataset IDs to exfiltrate pretty much all the data in the instance. With the Domo activity log only updating daily, it would be too late to alert on the exported data. There are workarounds like creating a dedicated instance to push data to Domo or writing the data to another tool like SharePoint or a database, and using that connector to import into Domo. But it introduces additional steps that could cause issues. We've previously created dedicated service accounts for specific use cases when pulling data from Domo or using Domo Everywhere. This is how we limit what data those API keys have access to. However, you need more access to push data to Domo. Could there be an option to only allow API keys to only manage datasets they create, without giving access to all the other datasets?

body_text: You can't change the data type, but you can change the data label, i.e., one BeastMode that you use for the value, which is raw, and one that you use as to manually format the answer. As a simple example, if you had a variable called metric , with options 'Dollars' or 'Percent', you could create a BeastMode metric_value CASE when metric = 'Dollars' then sum(`value`) when metric = 'Percent' then sum(`value`)/avg(avg(`value`)/fixed(by group ) ) END And a separate labeling BeastMode for the tooltip/data label/hover text metric_label CASE when metric = 'Dollars' then CONCAT('$', round(`value`, 2), ) when metric = 'Percent' then CONCAT(ROUND(sum(`value`)/avg(avg(`value`)/fixed(by group ) )*100,0), '%') END Not a perfect approach; if you want nicer number formatting, you can also do that manually, which can result in some very long BeastModes. It also won't change the y-axis

body_text: create your own multi append block by code engine, go through the append to dataset code in code engine and create a copy of it and modify it for multiple rows to append and use it accordingly.

body_text:
I don't do a lot of workflows, so this a bit of theory. Upload your file (CSV, Excel, whatever). Then based on your comments, parse the file and transform the rows into delimited format using JavaScript/Python, converting them with a code block into a delimited string and store the result to a variable. JavaScript: let rows = input.rows; // assuming input.rows is the parsed array let headers = Object.keys(rows[0]); let csv = headers.join(",") + "
"; rows.forEach(row => { let line = headers.map(h => row[h]).join(","); csv += line + "
"; }); output.delimitedData = csv; Python: # Assume 'input' is a list of dictionaries, each representing a row from the parsed CSV rows = input['rows'] # Extract headers from the first row headers = list(rows[0].keys()) # Start building the CSV string csv_lines = [",".join(headers)] # Add each row as a CSV line for row in rows: line = ",".join(str(row.get(h, "")) for h in headers) csv_lines.append(line) # Join all lines into a single string output['delimitedData'] = "
".join(csv_lines) Converts structured row data into a CSV-formatted string.

Both Beast Modes work correctly on their own, but the Comparative Gauge is displaying the wrong percentage. For example, last week’s sales were $4,000 , and the 6-week average sales is $0 because this is a new campaign and there’s no data for the past six weeks. In this case, the gauge shows 4,000% , but ideally, it should show blank or null , since the denominator is zero. For reference, the "6-week Average Sales" calculation is SUM(CASE WHEN Year Scenario Rolling = 'This Year' AND Fiscal Week Index > ( Current Week Index - 8) AND Fiscal Week Index < ( Current Week Index - 1) THEN IFNULL( Amount_Sales ,0) / 6 ELSE 0 END) and the "Last Week Average Sales" calculation is sum(case when FY Order = 0 AND Fiscal Week Index = ( Current Week index - 1) then Amount_Sales end) When I use the beastmode to calculate Last week vs 6-week average, the beastmode pulls the correct value, but the comparative gauge doesn't.
title: The Comparative Gauge chart is showing the % change incorrectly

body_text: I did a quick test with a current value of 4000 and previous value of 0 does result in a comparative value of 4000 so it seems like this chart does not correctly divide by zero but treats it as 1 instead. You could add some additional logic to your current value beast mode to be zero if your previous value is zero. This will result in a value of zero displaying in the gauge.
title: The Comparative Gauge chart is showing the % change incorrectly

body_text: Currently in App Studio, when an application uses multiple datasets, the Filter component automatically sources from the first dataset in the alphabetical list. Unfortunately, there is no way to specify which dataset should power the filter. This forces us to use workarounds that are not ideal. body_text: I am barely getting started with the vast DOMO world so forgive me if this is an obvious thing. I was recently creating a dataflow and some cards from that dataflow and decided to test something out. What happened was it "broke" the card and I had to fix it by having it use the "newly renamed column" even though it was the same column. Is there anyway to avoid this when setting up the card? or is this just something that I need to be aware of when creating the dataflow and knowing how many affected cards there are down the road? thank you
title: Renaming Columns and NOT breaking cards

body_text: Column names are case-sensitive when Domo evaluates if a column is the same or not. For example, ID is different than id for Domo. You can use the Select Columns tile in Magic ETL to rename columns and keep your cards from breaking. Hope this helps.
title: Renaming Columns and NOT breaking cards

body_text: I have the same issue. I want to rename multiple columns and would like to make sure that nothing breaks. How would using Magic ETL to rename the columns keep the cards from breaking? If the card uses field 'date' now and I rename it to 'start date', the card would break, no?
title: Renaming Columns and NOT breaking cards

body_text: @genchevd That's correct, it would break the card. If you want to change the field name, I would recommend first duplicating the original column in MagicETL with the new name. Once the new field is added, change all cards using that field to the new one (the Card Fields & Beast Modes report from the Domo Governance Connector is great for identifying which card use it). Then you can safely delete the old column from the dataflow

body_text: I need to limit access to a dataset and its associated cards in Domo so that only specific individuals can view them. This restriction should apply to everyone, including admins except for a few selected admins who should have access. Is this possible using PDP or any other solution within Domo?
title: How can I restrict dataset and card access in Domo to specific users, including selected admins?

body_text: To restrict dataset and card access to specific users and selected admins—you could try using Personalized Data Permissions (PDP) combined with a custom role and sharing. PDP would allow you to filter the dataset access by user or group, and the custom role would let you limit admin privileges by removing “Manage Datasets” and “Manage Cards”. The would make sure only specific admins retain full access.
title: How can I restrict dataset and card access in Domo to specific users, including selected admins?

body_text: No. The "Admin" role cannot be restricted even with PDP. You will need to create a custom role that is "Admin Lite" that does not allow users with that role to view all data.
title: How can I restrict dataset and card access in Domo to specific users, including selected admins?

body_text: For that report the card must be on a page. If you remove your owner filter you will see all rows of data contain a Page ID - meaning that the card must be on a page to be included in the report. body_text: A system we use for event planning gives a report like I'm seeing below. Every bit of this data needs to be in a single row. Sometimes the data is given in the same cell as the data label, and others live in the following cell. Is there any way an ETL (or any other Domo solution) can help me with this? I don't have a lot of hope. Site :Site here Room Layout Comments : Comments here ID number: ID Here Start/ENd Dates and times here Schedule Date : Date and time here Sponsor: Sponsor here Booked By: Name here Contact Person : Name here Registration Start-End Date : date here Fee : fee here Contract Amount: amount here Credits: credits here Comments of Internal : Comments here Confirmation Comments: : Comments here I need this instead: Session ID and Title Site Room Layout Comments Room Layout Session Start date Session end date schedule date Sponsor booked by Contact person Registration start Registration end Fee Contract amount Credits Comments of internal Confirmation
title: Making Sense of Wildly Unstructured Data

body_text: You can create an ETL that starts by splitting each comma-separated value into columns (Split Column). That would give you each label/value in it own column but not aligned. You would have to iterate over all the columns to find the patterns. Label: Value —> Label and Value. With Label: in one column and value in the next column. Then convert your irregular columns into key-value pairs and unpivot the columns. If you give us a sample csv file with a few records, we can try to give you a direct example. If you are familiar with running Python in Domo, you can do something like this (below). Again….I don't have a data sample to try it out. import pandas as pd import re # ----------------------------- # 1. Load raw data # ----------------------------- # If CSV has one column called 'raw': df = pd.read_csv('raw_events.csv') # or pd.read_excel('raw_events.xlsx') # If multiple columns from CSV, combine them into one string per row df['raw_combined'] = df.apply(lambda row: ','.join(row.dropna().astype(str)), axis=1) # ----------------------------- # 2. Split rows by comma # ----------------------------- split_cols = df['raw_combined'].str.split(',', expand=True) # ----------------------------- # 3. Extract label/value pairs # ----------------------------- def extract_label_value(cell, next_cell=None): if pd.isna(cell): return None, None # Case 1: Label: Value in same cell match = re.match(r'\s*(.+?):\s*(.+)', cell) if match: return match.group(1).strip(), match.group(2).strip() # Case 2: Label: in one cell, value in next if next_cell is not None: match2 = re.match(r'\s*(.+?):\s*$', cell) if match2: return match2.group(1).strip(), next_cell.strip() return None, None # Iterate over all columns and extract key/value pairs records = [] for idx, row in split_cols.iterrows(): row_data = {} i = 0 while i < len(row): key, value = extract_label_value(row[i], row[i+1] if i+1 < len(row) else None) if key: row_data[key] = value # If value was in next cell, skip it if re.match(r'.+?:\s*$', row[i]): i += 1 i += 1 records.append(row_data) # ----------------------------- # 4. Create flattened DataFrame # ----------------------------- flat_df = pd.DataFrame(records) # ----------------------------- # 5. Optional: rename columns to match desired output # ----------------------------- rename_map = { 'ID number': 'Session ID and Title', 'Site': 'Site', 'Room Layout Comments': 'Room Layout Comments', 'Start/End': 'Session Start date / Session End date', 'Schedule Date': 'Schedule date', 'Sponsor': 'Sponsor', 'Booked By': 'Booked by', 'Contact Person': 'Contact person', 'Registration Start-End Date': 'Registration start / Registration end', 'Fee': 'Fee', 'Contract Amount': 'Contract amount', 'Credits': 'Credits', 'Comments of Internal': 'Comments of internal', 'Confirmation Comments': 'Confirmation' } flat_df.rename(columns=rename_map, inplace=True) # ----------------------------- # 6. Save to CSV # ----------------------------- flat_df.to_csv('flattened_events.csv', index=False) print("Flattening complete. Saved to flattened_events.csv")
title: Making Sense of Wildly Unstructured Data

It's acting like the endpoint is an internal endpoint that is not publicly accessible. import requests import csv # --------- CONFIGURATION --------- DOMO_INSTANCE = 'YOUR_INSTANCE' # e.g., 'company.domo.com' PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN = 'XXXXXX' # Must have access to datasets CSV_FILENAME = 'vault_datasets.csv' # --------------------------------- headers = { 'Authorization': f'Bearer {PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } # Step 1: Get all datasets datasets_url = f"https://{DOMO_INSTANCE}/api/data/v3/datasources" response = requests.get(datasets_url, headers=headers) response.raise_for_status() # Should now connect correctly datasets_json = response.json() datasets_list = datasets_json.get('data', datasets_json) # fallback if 'data' key missing vault_datasets = [] # Step 2: Check cryostatus for each dataset for ds in datasets_list: dataset_id = ds['id'] dataset_name = ds['name'] detail_url = f"https://{DOMO_INSTANCE}/api/data/v3/datasources/{dataset_id}?includeAllDetails=true&includePrivate=true" detail_resp = requests.get(detail_url, headers=headers) if detail_resp.status_code != 200: print(f"Warning: Could not fetch details for {dataset_name} ({dataset_id})") continue ds_detail = detail_resp.json() cryostatus = ds_detail.get('cryostatus', 'Unknown') if cryostatus == 'Vault': vault_datasets.append({ 'id': dataset_id, 'name': dataset_name, 'cryostatus': cryostatus }) # Step 3: Print results print(f"Datasets in 'Vault' (not accessed in a while):") for ds in vault_datasets: print(f"{ds['name']} (ID: {ds['id']}, Cryostatus: {ds['cryostatus']})") # Step 4: Export to CSV with open(CSV_FILENAME, mode='w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as file: writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=['id', 'name', 'cryostatus']) writer.writeheader() writer.writerows(vault_datasets) print(f"\nExported {len(vault_datasets)} vault datasets to {CSV_FILENAME}")

body_text: A recent question (Any way to view schedule for dataflows?) brought about a valuable solution that I want to share with everyone. A comment with useful information from @nathankilcrease lead me to create the following solution. In Python I created code to produce a dataset showing all dataflow information. Basically - when are my jobs scheduled to run. (Note - it also saves a csv output file. Which can be easily removed from the code.) In a Domo brick, JavaScript code filters out the scheduled entries, and produces a Gantt chart so I can visually see when my jobs are set. I've color coded daily jobs as green, weekly jobs as gold, and monthly jobs as blue. If your instance is like mine, your list will be scrollable and much longer than the sample I'm showing below. I haven't completely validated it yet, but spot checking matches so i believe its accurate. Here's the code for creating the automated dataset and the chart. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Author : Arbor Rose # Date : 10.28.25 # Description : Loops through dataflow ids and pulls the trigger settings - # saved as dataflow_trigger_settings_flattened.csv. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Revision Date : # Revision : # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # ----------------------------- # Imports and Setup # ----------------------------- import os import requests import pandas as pd import json import sys from getpass import getpass import time # ----------------------------- # Configuration # ----------------------------- DOMO_INSTANCE = "XXXXX" DOMO_DEV_TOKEN = "XXXXX" dataset_name = "Domo Scheduled Jobs" # ----------------------------- # Helper: list all dataflow IDs # ----------------------------- def list_dataflow_ids(instance, dev_token): url = f"https://{instance}.domo.com/api/dataprocessing/v1/dataflows" headers = {"x-domo-developer-token": dev_token, "Accept": "application/json"} resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers) resp.raise_for_status() batch = resp.json() ids = [df["id"] for df in batch if "id" in df] return ids # ----------------------------- # Helper: fetch dataflow preview # ----------------------------- def fetch_dataflow_preview(instance, df_id, dev_token, retries=3, backoff=1): url = f"https://{instance}.domo.com/api/dataprocessing/v2/dataflows/{df_id}" headers = {"x-domo-developer-token": dev_token, "Accept": "application/json"} params = {"validationType": "PREVIEW"} for attempt in range(1, retries+1): try: resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=20) if resp.status_code == 200: return resp.json() else: print(f"[Attempt {attempt}] HTTP {resp.status_code} for {df_id}") except requests.RequestException as e: print(f"[Attempt {attempt}] Request error for {df_id}: {e}") time.sleep(backoff * attempt) return None # ----------------------------- # Helper: extract triggerSettings # ----------------------------- def extract_trigger_settings(df_json): if not df_json: return None ts = df_json.get("triggerSettings") if ts is None: # fallback search nested def find_key(d, key="triggerSettings"): if isinstance(d, dict): for k, v in d.items(): if k == key: return v res = find_key(v, key) if res: return res elif isinstance(d, list): for item in d: res = find_key(item, key) if res: return res return None ts = find_key(df_json) return ts # ----------------------------- # Main: loop through dataflows # ----------------------------- dataflow_ids = list_dataflow_ids(DOMO_INSTANCE, DOMO_DEV_TOKEN) print(f"Found {len(dataflow_ids)} dataflow IDs.\n") sys.stdout.flush() records = [] for idx, df_id in enumerate(dataflow_ids, start=1): print(f"[{idx}/{len(dataflow_ids)}] Fetching {df_id}") sys.stdout.flush() preview = fetch_dataflow_preview(DOMO_INSTANCE, df_id, DOMO_DEV_TOKEN) if preview: name = preview.get("displayName") or preview.get("name") or " " trigger = extract_trigger_settings(preview) records.append({ "id": df_id, "name": name, "triggerSettings": json.dumps(trigger) if trigger else None }) print(f" Collected: {name}") else: print(f" Failed to fetch {df_id}") sys.stdout.flush() df = pd.DataFrame(records) print(f"\n✅ Collected triggerSettings for {len(df)} dataflows.") # ----------------------------- # Upload to Domo dataset (REST API) # ----------------------------- # Save all triggerSettings to CSV in workspace df.to_csv("dataflow_trigger_settings.csv", index=False) # print("✅ Saved CSV to dataflow_trigger_settings.csv") flattened_records = [] for _, row in df.iterrows(): df_id = row['id'] df_name = row['name'] ts_json = row['triggerSettings'] if pd.isna(ts_json): continue try: ts = json.loads(ts_json) except json.JSONDecodeError: continue triggers = ts.get("triggers", []) zoneId = ts.get("zoneId") locale = ts.get("locale") for trigger in triggers: trigger_title = trigger.get("title") trigger_id = trigger.get("triggerId") trigger_conditions = trigger.get("triggerConditions", []) events = trigger.get("triggerEvents", []) for event in events: # Capture schedule info if present schedule = event.get("schedule", {}) flattened_records.append({ "dataflow_id": df_id, "dataflow_name": df_name, "trigger_title": trigger_title, "trigger_id": trigger_id, "trigger_type": event.get("type"), "datasetId": event.get("datasetId") or event.get("id"), "triggerOnDataChanged": event.get("triggerOnDataChanged"), "schedule_second": schedule.get("second"), "schedule_minute": schedule.get("minute"), "schedule_hour": schedule.get("hour"), "schedule_dayOfMonth": schedule.get("dayOfMonth"), "schedule_month": schedule.get("month"), "schedule_dayOfWeek": schedule.get("dayOfWeek"), "schedule_year": schedule.get("year"), "zoneId": zoneId, "locale": locale }) flat_df = pd.DataFrame(flattened_records) #print(flat_df.head()) import domojupyter as domo flat_df.to_csv("dataflow_trigger_settings_flattened.csv", index=False) domo.write_dataframe(flat_df, dataset_name) #print("✅ Flattened CSV saved: dataflow_trigger_settings_flattened.csv") The brick code follows. Html: Scheduled Dataflows Gantt Chart Green represents a daily job. Gold represents a weekly job. Blue represents a monthly job. Css: body { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; margin: 20px; } h2 { text-align: center; } .gantt-wrapper { position: relative; width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; } .gantt-container { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 100%; border: 1px solid #ccc; position: relative; } .gantt-row { display: flex; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 5px; height: 24px; position: relative; } .dataflow-label { width: 300px; text-align: right; margin-right: 10px; font-size: 12px; flex-shrink: 0; } .time-bar-container { position: relative; flex: 1; height: 100%; background: #f4f4f4; border: 1px solid #ddd; box-sizing: border-box; } .time-bar { position: absolute; height: 100%; background-color: #4caf50; border-radius: 2px; box-sizing: border-box; } .time-bar.day-of-week { background-color: #f39c12; /* orange for weekly schedules */ } .time-bar.day-of-month { background-color: #3498db; /* blue for monthly schedules */ } .time-axis { height: 20px; font-size: 10px; position: relative; margin-top: 5px; margin-left: 310px; /* label width + margin */ } .time-axis div { position: absolute; top: 0; transform: translateX(-50%); text-align: center; } .gantt-grid-line { position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; width: 1px; background: #ccc; } .gantt-grid-line.major { width: 2px; background: #888; } JavaScript: const gantt = document.getElementById('gantt'); const timeAxis = document.getElementById('time-axis'); function timeToMinutes(hour, minute) { return Number(hour) * 60 + Number(minute); } const domo = window.domo; const datasets = window.datasets; domo.get(`data/v1/${datasets[0]}`).then(result => { const scheduledDataflows = result.filter(df => String(df.trigger_type).trim().toUpperCase() === "SCHEDULE" ); // Step 1: Create all rows first scheduledDataflows.forEach(df => { const row = document.createElement('div'); row.className = 'gantt-row'; const label = document.createElement('div'); label.className = 'dataflow-label'; label.textContent = df.dataflow_name; row.appendChild(label); const barContainer = document.createElement('div'); barContainer.className = 'time-bar-container'; row.appendChild(barContainer); gantt.appendChild(row); }); // Step 2: After DOM is rendered, position bars and draw grid setTimeout(() => { // ensure layout is ready const barContainers = document.querySelectorAll('.time-bar-container'); const containerWidth = barContainers[0].clientWidth; // Draw bars scheduledDataflows.forEach((df, idx) => { const barContainer = barContainers[idx]; const totalMinutes = timeToMinutes(df.schedule_hour, df.schedule_minute); const leftPx = (totalMinutes / 1440) * containerWidth; const bar = document.createElement('div'); bar.className = 'time-bar'; // Assign color class based on schedule type const dayOfWeek = String(df.schedule_dayOfWeek || '').trim().toUpperCase(); const dayOfMonth = parseInt(df.schedule_dayOfMonth, 10); const validDaysOfWeek = ["SUN","MON","TUE","WED","THU","FRI","SAT"]; if (validDaysOfWeek.includes(dayOfWeek)) { bar.classList.add('day-of-week'); } else if (!isNaN(dayOfMonth) && dayOfMonth >= 1 && dayOfMonth <= 31) { bar.classList.add('day-of-month'); } bar.style.left = leftPx + 'px'; bar.style.width = Math.max(containerWidth * 0.01, 2) + 'px'; barContainer.appendChild(bar); }); // Draw time axis & grid lines for (let h = 0; h <= 24; h += 0.5) { const leftPx = (h / 24) * containerWidth; // grid lines in each row barContainers.forEach(container => { const line = document.createElement('div'); line.className = 'gantt-grid-line'; if (h % 1 === 0) line.classList.add('major'); line.style.left = leftPx + 'px'; container.appendChild(line); }); // axis labels only for whole hours if (h % 1 === 0) { const tick = document.createElement('div'); tick.textContent = `${h}:00`; tick.style.left = leftPx + 'px'; timeAxis.appendChild(tick); } } }, 50); // short delay to ensure layout }).catch(err => console.error(err));

body_text: As the title suggests, I think it would be a really cool idea if Domo had a recycle bin. This would be a paid premium feature, and I think it would be a boon from a maintenance/emergency perspective. While sandbox is great and helpful for recovery in situations where things have been accidentally deleted, it can still be time consuming to re-deploy, fetch and restore historical data, re-establish user/groups access etc. Re-deployment also causes a change of object IDs and can affect other objects/processes. Particularly SQL based views that reference datasets by ID, any hardcoded object ID references in jupyter notebooks, external automation scripts etc. A recycle bin would allow owners of objects or admins to quickly restore a deleted item quickly. Here's how I imagine this working after the feature has been paid for. Admin > Site settings A checkbox to enable the recycle bin feature along with a dropdown allowing you to select how many days of retention before items are actually permanently deleted. The amount of days you select determines your overall cost per month (with a max of say 30 days). Grants New grants can be added to roles that let you use the recycle bin or manage the recycle bin (thus allow you to restore objects from any user). Admins would automatically have this grant. Domo UI Once enabled, a recycle bin shows up in the Domo interface. When an item is deleted, roles with the proper grants will see a categorized list of the deleted objects they own (or all items if they have the managed grant). It would also display whether or not the item is in an existing repository. If it is part of a repository, perhaps it can also show information about the repository and its current version #, etc. If the object is not part of a repository, that information would be blank with a button that would optionally allow you to add it to a new or existing repository. It would also show the objects internal ID and maybe an indicator to show that the deleted item broke the lineage of other objects along with a tooltip that lists all of objects affected. Users can right click on any item in the recycle bin to restore it immediately. The restoration would restore everything about that object as if it was never deleted in the first place. Maintaining the existing object ID, data and metadata, user group access, PDP etc. Basically, a full 1-to-1 restoration. Once restored, it no longer shows in the recycle bin. Object Types In its current state, sandbox supports a limited number of object types. The recycle bin however would support anything subject to deletion. Cards App Studio Apps Dashboards Connectors Domo Datasets Dataflows Jupyter Notebooks / Workspaces File Shares (along with any content) Pro-code Apps / AppDB Assets User / Groups Workflows / Code Engine Alerts Views Sandbox Repositories AI Projects Accounts (And other objects I haven't thought of) I realize there is a lot more to consider here as it does overlap with sandbox a bit. I also realize that restoring certain deleted objects would require any other deleted dependencies to be automatically restored as well. It's a crazy, complex idea with a lot to consider. But, if this can be made to somehow work in tandem with sandbox, I think it would be extremely useful. I imagine it would also make Domo Support's life much easier when emergencies occur. 😉

body_text: Currently, Domo supports publishing Dashboards/Pages to other instances via the standard Publish functionality. However, there is no option to publish a Report Builder View . This limitation restricts users who rely on Report Builder to create modular, reusable report views that should be shareable across Domo instances — similar to dashboards. Requested Enhancement Enable Publish support for Report Builder Views , providing functionality similar to existing Page/Dashboard publishing. Specifically: Add “Publish” or “Publish to Instance” as an available action in Report Builder. Preserve the report layout, filters, and data sources in the published copy. Allow views to be published individually or as part of a dashboard package. Ensure data permissions, PDP, and dataset lineage are maintained consistently with current Page publishing behaviour. Business Justification Reusability: Enables reusing Report Builder views across multiple environments (e.g., Dev → UAT → Prod, or internal → client instances). Efficiency: Reduces manual recreation effort for reports that already exist in other instances. Consistency: Ensures design and KPI alignment across published views. Adoption: Encourages more teams to use Report Builder as a modular reporting tool, confident their work can be shared/published like dashboards.

body_text: You can't apply HTML tags to a Pivot Table, though it would be nice. You could norm your data so above 0 (or some other value) means something and below means something else and apply a color rule to your value column. The other way to format pivot cells is by concat-ing indicators (emoji/unicode characters). For example: case when Category = 1 and sum( Orders )/sum(sum( Orders ) fixed(by week No. )) <0.05 then concat(sum( Orders ), ' ', % of total , ' 🔴') when Category = 3 and sum( Orders )/sum(sum( Orders ) fixed(by week No. )) >0.1 then concat(sum( Orders ), ' ', % of total , ' 🔵') when Category = 4 and sum( Orders )/sum(sum( Orders ) fixed(by week No. )) >0.5 then concat(sum( Orders ), ' ', % of total , ' 🔵') else concat(sum( Orders ),' ', % of total , ' ⚪') end

body_text:
Very nice. Give the man a point. Here's python code to hit that endpoint. Note - a single data flow as described in that curl. Domo instance value would be the company name that appears before ".domo.com". In my example output I am calling dataflow id 564. # Domo Dataflow schedule fetcher for Domo Jupyter Workspaces # Anonymized instance: replace YOUR_INSTANCE with your Domo instance host prefix (no .domo.com) # e.g. if your instance is henryscheinone.domo.com -> use "henryscheinone" import os import json import time import requests from getpass import getpass from typing import Optional # ----------------------------- # Configuration - fill these # ----------------------------- DOMO_INSTANCE = os.getenv("DOMO_INSTANCE", "YOUR_INSTANCE") # <-- set this or export DOMO_INSTANCE DATAFLOW_ID = "PUT_YOUR_DATAFLOW_ID_HERE" # <-- Replace with a real dataflow id (uuid-ish string) # Token: either set DOMO_DEV_TOKEN env var or leave empty to be prompted securely at runtime DOMO_DEV_TOKEN = os.getenv("DOMO_DEV_TOKEN", None) # ----------------------------- # Helper: get token securely # ----------------------------- def get_token() -> str: token = DOMO_DEV_TOKEN if token: return token.strip() token = os.getenv("DOMO_DEV_TOKEN") # re-check if token: return token.strip() # If not set, prompt securely (works in Jupyter) return getpass("Enter Domo developer token (x-domo-developer-token): ").strip() # ----------------------------- # Main function # ----------------------------- def fetch_dataflow_preview(instance: str, dataflow_id: str, dev_token: str, timeout: int = 20, retries: int = 3, backoff: float = 1.0) -> Optional[dict]: """ Fetches the dataflow preview JSON from the undocumented endpoint: GET https://{instance}.domo.com/api/dataprocessing/v2/dataflows/{dataflow_id}?validationType=PREVIEW Returns parsed JSON dict on success, or None on failure. """ base_url = f"https://{instance}.domo.com" endpoint = f"/api/dataprocessing/v2/dataflows/{dataflow_id}" params = {"validationType": "PREVIEW"} headers = { "x-domo-developer-token": dev_token, "Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": "domo-jupyter-fetcher/1.0" } url = base_url + endpoint for attempt in range(1, retries + 1): try: resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=timeout) except requests.RequestException as e: # network-level error print(f"[attempt {attempt}] Request error: {e}") if attempt < retries: time.sleep(backoff * attempt) continue return None if resp.status_code == 200: try: return resp.json() except ValueError: print("Received non-JSON response.") return None elif resp.status_code == 401: print("Unauthorized (401). Check your developer token.") return None elif resp.status_code == 404: print("Not found (404). Check instance and dataflow ID.") return None else: print(f"[attempt {attempt}] HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.text[:400]}") if attempt < retries: time.sleep(backoff * attempt) continue return None # ----------------------------- # Utility: pretty-print triggerSettings # ----------------------------- def show_trigger_settings(dataflow_json: dict): """ Extracts and prints triggerSettings (schedule info). If not present, prints available top-level keys. """ if not isinstance(dataflow_json, dict): print("No JSON data to inspect.") return # triggerSettings is expected somewhere near root (per user's cURL) ts = dataflow_json.get("triggerSettings") or dataflow_json.get("triggerSettings", None) if ts: print("triggerSettings (schedule information):
") print(json.dumps(ts, indent=2)) return # fallback: search nested keys that look like triggerSettings def find_key(d, keyname="triggerSettings"): if isinstance(d, dict): for k, v in d.items(): if k == keyname: return v res = find_key(v, keyname) if res is not None: return res elif isinstance(d, list): for item in d: res = find_key(item, keyname) if res is not None: return res return None found = find_key(dataflow_json, "triggerSettings") if found: print("Found nested triggerSettings:
") print(json.dumps(found, indent=2)) return print("No 'triggerSettings' key found in response. Top-level keys:
") print(", ".join(dataflow_json.keys())) # ----------------------------- # Usage # ----------------------------- if __name__ == "__main__": token = get_token() if not token: raise SystemExit("No developer token provided.") print(f"Requesting dataflow preview for dataflow id: {DATAFLOW_ID} on instance: {DOMO_INSTANCE}.domo.com") resp_json = fetch_dataflow_preview(DOMO_INSTANCE, DATAFLOW_ID, token) if resp_json is None: print("Failed to fetch dataflow preview.") else: # show top-level name/id and triggerSettings if available name = resp_json.get("displayName") or resp_json.get("name") or resp_json.get("id", " ") print(f"
Dataflow: {name}
") show_trigger_settings(resp_json) Output from the above code: Requesting dataflow preview for dataflow id: 564 on instance: YOURINSTANCE.domo.com Dataflow: Queue_Performance.ipynb triggerSettings (schedule information): { "triggers": [ { "title": "Trigger Title 1", "triggerEvents": [ { "id": "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", "schedule": { "second": "0", "minute": "0", "hour": "9", "dayOfMonth": "?", "month": "*", "dayOfWeek": "MON", "year": "*" }, "type": "SCHEDULE" } ], "triggerConditions": [], "triggerId": 1 } ], "zoneId": "Africa/Bamako", "locale": "en_US" } Note - my instance is set as Africa/Bamako so it centers Domo on UTC time. ;)

----------------------------- # Main: loop through dataflows # ----------------------------- dataflow_ids = list_dataflow_ids(DOMO_INSTANCE, DOMO_DEV_TOKEN) print(f"Found {len(dataflow_ids)} dataflow IDs.\n") sys.stdout.flush() records = [] for idx, df_id in enumerate(dataflow_ids, start=1): print(f"[{idx}/{len(dataflow_ids)}] Fetching {df_id}") sys.stdout.flush() preview = fetch_dataflow_preview(DOMO_INSTANCE, df_id, DOMO_DEV_TOKEN) if preview: name = preview.get("displayName") or preview.get("name") or " " trigger = extract_trigger_settings(preview) records.append({ "id": df_id, "name": name, "triggerSettings": json.dumps(trigger) if trigger else None }) print(f" Collected: {name}") else: print(f" Failed to fetch {df_id}") sys.stdout.flush() df = pd.DataFrame(records) print(f"\n✅ Collected triggerSettings for {len(df)} dataflows.") # body_text: Currently, Domo supports publishing Dashboards/Pages to other instances via the standard Publish functionality. However, there is no option to publish a Report Builder View. This limitation restricts users who rely on Report Builder to create modular, reusable report views that should be shareable across Domo instances — similar to dashboards. Requested Enhancement Enable Publish support for Report Builder Views, providing functionality similar to existing Page/Dashboard publishing. Specifically: Add “Publish” or “Publish to Instance” as an available action in Report Builder. Preserve the report layout, filters, and data sources in the published copy. Allow views to be published individually or as part of a dashboard package. Ensure data permissions, PDP, and dataset lineage are maintained consistently with current Page publishing behaviour. Business Justification Reusability: Enables reusing Report Builder views across multiple environments (e.g., Dev → UAT → Prod, or internal → client instances). Efficiency: Reduces manual recreation effort for reports that already exist in other instances. Consistency: Ensures design and KPI alignment across published views. Adoption: Encourages more teams to use Report Builder as a modular reporting tool, confident their work can be shared/published like dashboards.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Publish support for Report Builder Views

body_text: Hi Community, I’m working on a Grouped Bar Chart in Domo and facing an issue with sorting on both the X-axis and the Series (Legend) simultaneously. Here’s my setup: Category (X-axis): Product Category (Electronics, Furniture, Clothing, etc.) Value (Y-axis): Total Sales Series: Sub Category (Mobile Phones, Laptops, Sofas, etc.) Requirement: I want the X-axis to follow a specific custom order → Electronics, Furniture, Clothing I also want the Series (Sub Category) in the legend to appear in a custom-defined order (for example, Mobile Phones first, then Laptops, then Televisions, etc. ) Issue: When I apply sorting on one (for example, Product Category), the sorting on the other (Sub Category) seems to get overridden. It appears that Domo allows only one active sort order within this chart type, which causes both the X-axis and Legend sorting not to align as expected. I've tried using Custom Beast mode formulas for X-axis sorting first & Legend sorting best mode next. But it is not working as expected. Is there any way to achieve both custom X-axis and Legend order together? Any suggestions or best practices for handling multiple custom sorts in the same chart would be greatly appreciated.
title: Multi-Sorting in Grouped Bar Chart.

body_text: From what I understand, Domo’s grouped bar charts currently allow only one active sort definition, and it applies globally to the visualization, meaning if you sort the X-axis (Product Category), it overrides any Legend (Series) sort, and vice versa. I would ask AI if there is a workaround to this.
title: Multi-Sorting in Grouped Bar Chart.

body_text: It may have something to do with your custom sort logic. Are you able to share that? I was able to sort my x-axis in ascending order and my legend in descending order by putting both in the sorting section and starting with my x-axis and then my legend.
title: Multi-Sorting in Grouped Bar Chart.

body_text: My recommendations for how app studio can be improved: Allow me to double click on text boxes to edit them. Make App Studio’s navigation intuitive. The way the tabs of App Studio’s editor are embedded within each other isn’t always intuitive, making it difficult to find the things that I’m looking for. For example, naming my app is under the Configuration Tab of App Studio but the toggle of whether to show the name of my app is under the Pages and Navigation tab’s Configuration tab . Make the edit button/home button separate from the navigation tab, or add actions to buttons like printing/sharing, toggling between pre-set page filters. The Show Domo Navigation and Show Navigation Toggles, when turned off, allow me to completely softlock me inside of my app without being able to edit it or exit back to domo (until, I figured out, I can just add “/edit” to the URL). Not sure why this is an option. Maybe the edit button/home button should be separate from the navigation tab, or at least have it be an option to be. Or, there should be an option to have no pages on the navigation bar so that we can still have the share button and home button and everything on an app with only a single page. Make a button that removes only specified filters from the page or make there a way to lock page filters so that they cannot be changed. When I hit the “remove filters button” that I made, it doesn’t just remove filters like the ones the user added, but it also removes the filters for the entire page. So if I wanted users to be able to have a button to remove the filters they added without removing the page’s filters, I would have to embed the entire app with the same filter. Unfortunately, each page of my app cannot be filtered to the same date range, so that breaks a number of my cards. Make a better sorting/filing system for apps. When adding a tab to an app, tab headers (the part you click on to go through each of the tabs) should have an option to be the same size regardless of the length of the tab title and should allow wrapping text. Allow any seize tab to be printed. The Beta printing option on apps won’t print tabs that are “too long”. It also doesn’t print entire tables (if they have a scroll bar, it only shows where the table is currently scrolled to) Headers should allow me to put things next to them like text boxes do. When I want to put a button or something next to my header, I have to delete it and make it a text box before it’ll let me. Allow me to save without exiting App Studio. I have lost work before due to not wanting to exit and then receiving some sort of error which causes me to have to reload the page. Are there ways to be able to track user-activity within an app’s pages when embedded on a website? When put on our test site, the app’s URL remains the same regardless of which page you’re on, meaning we have no way of tracking which features our users use most frequently, so we have to have separate apps for each feature. This means we have like 30 apps for all the different pages that would otherwise go in 2 or 3 apps if this weren’t an issue. Make the left app studio editor bar thinner and possibly at the top of the page with a scroll bar so the app doesn’t have to squish down as much. It currently takes up a lot of space on the page. Having to toggle between app studio and the “Actual Size” is slightly frustrating. Add an X-button to the left editor. It took me embarrassingly long to figure out I could close that editor bar by clicking the tab that I’m on a second time. The first thing the editor should open to is the most-commonly used editing items. I rarely use the change theme/change color stuff, so why is it always the first thing the app opens to? Add grid lines that can be toggled on/off that show me where PDF pages will be cut off. Add an option to make all cards or all spacers or all buttons on the page the same size. Either that or make that part of the app’s theme. It’s currently hard to make everything consistent. Tabs should allow me to choose the length of my tabs first, then squeeze the size of the cards down as they’re added, only elongating if the cards can’t be squeezed down any further.When I add cards to a tab, I’ve made the mistake of perfecting the spacing and sizing on the first tab, then, when adding cards to the second tab, my spacing on the first tab is now ruined because the first card fits to the size of the ENTIRE tab and any card I add afterwards elongates the tab with no way of preventing this. Add an undo button. There’s been times where I just close out of my app without saving because it’s faster than trying to manually undo whatever mistake I’ve made. Allow me to select multiple dashboards when importing multiple dashboards to different pages. It just takes a while doing it one at a time. Allow me to select and edit a card without opening app studio. When I want to edit a card in an app, it takes me 5 clicks and 2 loading screens to be able to do so. Allow me to edit cards in the appendix. I shouldn’t have to add it to my app first to be able to edit it.

body_text: Hi, I have a Form in AppStudio with a date selector as an input. I'd like to prevent users from selecting Weekends and Company Holidays (stored in a master calendar). Is there a way to do this in AppStudio and without doing some sort of join in Magic?
title: Lock Out Dates in AppStudio Forms

body_text: Not with the Form element in App Studio. You could submit that as an idea in the https://community-forums.domo.com/main/categories/ideas You could also accomplish this using Pro Code Editor: https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/000005500?language=en_US Or you could just put in the description of your form to only select non-holiday weekdays. In the back end you could check that the date submitted was a valid date and then notify the form submitter via a workflow that they entered an invalid date and to resubmit the form. How often is this happening? If it is relatively rare, you could just have an alert for yourself to notify you anytime someone submits a response that isn't a valid workday and you could ask them to resubmit. Probably lowest effort solution if this doesn't happen often.
title: Lock Out Dates in AppStudio Forms

body_text: Another wrench in sorting series/x-axis is that if you need your series in a particular order, but the first item in your x-axis doesn't have that value, it is impossible to get the sort correct with sorting alone. For example, if I have a Likert-style question, where I need Strongly-Agree to always come after Agree which needs to come after Somewhat-Agree, but the first bar doesn't have any values for Strongly-Agree. If I am sorting, I can either compromise on where Strongly-Agree falls or what comes first on the X-Axis. Fortunately, for bar graphs (grouped or stacked), there is a workaround. You can create a BeastMode for each series and enter multiple series into the Y axis and Series options. That forces the order of the series to be correct, and then the only sort you need is for your x-axis. Here's an example of a likert stacked bar graph where I've created a series for each of the possible responses to insure the correct order:
title: Multi-Sorting in Grouped Bar Chart.

body_text: This sounds like a feature request rather than a question. Is the following (below) a correct summation? If so, maybe a forum admin could move it to Feature Request: Improve Filtering and Visibility in Execution List Summary Currently, the Execution List in Domo does not allow filtering or searching by recipient (e.g., email address or person). This makes it very difficult to investigate issues with automated processes that send emails or require responses. Use Case We run an automated process that sends weekly emails requesting form responses. We have 300+ recipients at a time. When investigating user-reported issues (such as someone receiving a reminder despite having completed the form), we cannot: Search/filter executions by recipient or variable (e.g., email). See at a glance who received an email without drilling into each execution. Problem A recipient received reminder emails despite evidence they had already completed the form. The form was no longer in the queue, but we could not determine which execution sent the email because the Execution List has no filtering options. Troubleshooting requires manually opening each execution, which is inefficient and impractical at scale. Requested Enhancement Please add the following capabilities to the Execution List: Filtering/searching by recipient (person or email address). Filtering by variable values (e.g., user ID, form name, workflow inputs). Quick visibility into recipients of each execution without needing to click into each one.

body_text: @ArborRose I have a solution in the meantime using the APIs. Call the first to get a list of execution (instance ) ids for a specific workflow and version. GET: https://{company_instance}.domo.com/api/workflow/v2/executions?modelId={model_id}&triggerTypes=ALERT,API,APP_STUDIO,CUSTOM_APP,MANUAL,TIMER,WORKFLOW&modelVersion={model_version}&status={status}" Then loop through the ids retrieved about to get the variables included in the workflow capturing for when the 'id' key IN (user_id, user_name, user_email): GET https://{comapny_instance}.domo.com/api/workflow/v1/instances/transactions?instanceId={instance_id}" You can loop this through each status option ['COMPLETE','IN_PROGRESS','FAILED','CANCELLED'] Works a charm.

body_text:
Please consider the implementation of a NUMBER_FORMAT function in Beast Mode in the same vein that we have DATE_FORMAT and TIME_FORMAT. This would take a number, and based on parameters, format the number (add thousand separator commas, percent sign, currency sign). Numerous discussions have been had in the forums about how to use Beast Mode to add commas, dollar signs, percent signs in summary numbers, or in table cards. As much as I love @GrantSmith a 67 line beast mode to add thousands separator commas feels like a workaround of a solution to a relatively common problem. In addition, I have had to write even more cumbersome Beast Mode statements to satisfy requests when working with the Variables Product when for example, one metric is a currency and the other is a percentage. Greetings! This is another post highlighting a beast mode from my Domo IDEAs conference session. This one covers how to format numbers a number when concatenating with a string.

Problem:

When concatenating a string with a number the resulting value is a string and unable to utilize Domo's built in formatting.

Solution:

Check the length of the number using the LENGTH function and then get the appropriate segments of the number using SUBSTRING and then combining them all together using CONCAT

-- Author: -- Created: -- Last Modified: -- Description: -- Checks the length of a number to determine how to insert thousands separators (,) using SUBSTRING to get 3 digit pieces of the number. CONCAT('Total Amount: ', CASE WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 12 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 4, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 7, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 10, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 11 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 2), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 3, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 6, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 9, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 10 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 1), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 2, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 5, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 7, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 9 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 4, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 7, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 8 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 2), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 3, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 6, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 7 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 1), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 2, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 5, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 6 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 3), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 4, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 5 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 2), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 3, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) = 4 THEN CONCAT( SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 1, 1), ',', SUBSTRING(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0), 2, 3) ) WHEN LENGTH(ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0)) <= 3 THEN ROUND(SUM(`random_number`), 0) WHEN SUM(`random_number`) IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 'ERROR' END ) Note:

These beast modes only go to 100 Billion (12 digits). Any number higher would need to expand using the same logic for higher lengths.

body_text: How is everyone structuring their queries for transactions from NetSuite to Domo? I'm using SuiteAnalytics Connect and struggling a bit with the best way to ensure data is complete for an income statement and balance sheet. Specifically, what date range should I select? I'm joining transactions, transactionLine, and transactionAccountingLine (plus a few other tables) to get all transactions down to the line level. Obviously I can't just do a full replace each time. I could do a partitioned/recursive ETL … but If I select a rolling window by transaction date, i.e. WHERE trandate >= (SYSDATE - 7) then I risk missing updates/deletions to older transactions. Next idea was to do the same, instead using transaction.lastModifiedDate … but then I don't have any handling for deleted transactions. Likewise for upsert … no handling for deletions. Maybe there is some method using accountingPeriod.closed and accountingPeriod.closedOnDate ? Perhaps WHERE closed = 'F' OR closedOnDate >= (SYSDATE - 7) ? But then I'm pulling a heck of a lot of rows with each sync. Hoping for some best practices from the community! Thanks
title: NetSuite General Ledger Best Practices

body_text: I have a few issues with creating apps in domo, some of which are bugs and some of which are general gripes with the user experience. All of these have been sent to Domo Support but they encouraged that I post it to Domo's community forums as well. To start, the bugs: The first time I hit save after creating an app, after hitting save, the page saves but does not exit out like normal. When creating a new app, if I want to use a custom theme from another app that I’ve created, I have to reupload the theme each time from my computer. For some reason it doesn’t save to Domo. When I try to import a new page from a dashboard or app, it makes me save the page I’m currently on, even if no changes have been made, and then I have to hit the import button a second time rather than it opening itself the first time. When hitting a button that opens another page of the app in a separate tab, it works just fine on Domo, but when embedded in a website, the buttons cease to work. Now, the gripes: When adding a Header to the page, I have to delete the word “Title” each time rather than it highlighting/deleting for me. I don’t like that I can’t double click on text boxes to edit them. The way the tabs of App Studio are embedded within each other isn’t always intuitive, making it difficult to find the things that I’m looking for. For example, naming my app is under the Configuration Tab of App Studio but the toggle of whether to show the name of my app is under the Pages and Navigation tab’s Configuration tab . The Show Domo Navigation and Show Navigation Toggles, when turned off, allow me to completely softlock me inside of my app without being able to edit it or exit back to domo (until, I found out, I can just add “/edit” to the URL). Not sure why this is an option. Maybe the edit button/home button should be separate from the navigation tab, or at least have it be an option to be. When scrolling on my app in Domo, the menu sticks to either the top or the side of the screen just fine. But when embedding my app in a website, however, the menu loses its “stickiness” and instead when I scroll to the bottom, I have to scroll back up to select another page of the app. Not sure if this is something domo support can help with or not. Maybe having the menu have its own scroll bar separate from the rest? Not sure. In Domo and when the app is embedded on a site, when I hit the “remove filters button” that I made, it doesn’t just remove filters like the ones the user added, but it also removes the filters for the entire page. So if I wanted users to be able to have a button to remove the filters they added without removing the page’s filters, I would have to embed the entire app with the same filter. Unfortunately, each page of my app cannot be filtered to the same date range, so that breaks a number of my cards. If there was a way to make a button that removes only specified filters from the page, that would be great. Or if there was a way to lock page filters so that they cannot be changed, that would help. I have been converting a lot of our dashboards into apps, which will continue to get more difficult to manage without some sort of filing or sorting system. When adding tabs to an app, tabs should have an option to be the same size regardless of the length of the tab title and should allow wrapping text. The bugs are currently being addressed by Domo Support, but hopefully the rest of my feedback reaches the right people. I was told to post in the "Feedback" section of Domo Forums, which I can't seem to find, so if there's a better place I should post this please let me know.
title: App Studio Bugs and Gripes

body_text: On November 15, 2025 , Facebook will implement important breaking changes to all versions of their API: 1. The 'impressions' metric will be replaced by a new metric called 'views'. This is not just a rename – 'views' is a completely new metric. 2. The 'page fans' metric will be fully retired and no longer available. For more details, please visit Facebook’s official announcement: [Facebook Developers Blog] --- What Changes Will Domo Make? In response to these API updates, Domo will implement changes on November 3, 2025 affecting both the Facebook and Facebook Advanced connectors: 1. Deprecation of the following reports: - Page Fans - Page Fans by City - Page Fans by Country Datasets configured to use these reports will start to throw errors. Unfortunately, there are no direct replacements for these reports. 2. Removal of the following metrics from the 'Page Impressions Details (PageMetricsOverview)' and 'Page Post Lifetime Metrics' reports: - page_fans - Page_fans_locale - Page_fans_city - Page_fans_country - Page_fan_adds - Page_fan_adds_unique - Page_fan_removes - page_fan_removes_unique - page_impressions - page_impressions_paid - page_impressions_viral - page_impressions_nonviral - post_impressions - post_impressions_paid - post_impressions_fan - post_impressions_organic - post_impressions_viral - post_impressions_nonviral Additionally, the Facebook and Facebook Advanced connectors will no longer request these metrics for existing datasets. Some of these metrics have alternative options available. Please see the mapping below. --- What Do Customers Need to Do? - Customers should disable any datasets configured to pull Page Fans, Page Fans by City, or Page Fans by Country reports at their convenience. - Datasets using the Page Impressions Details (PageMetricsOverview) and Page Post Lifetime Metrics reports will be automatically updated to stop requesting deprecated metrics. - We recommend customers update their datasets ahead of time to include any available alternative metrics, and also update any dashboards or assets that rely on the deprecated metrics. --- How Will Customers Be Notified? Owners of datasets using the affected reports will receive email notifications. --- Alternative Metrics Please refer to the list below for alternative metrics that can be used where applicable: Deprecated Metric Alternative Metric page_fans page_follows Page_fans_locale no alternative Page_fans_city page_follows_city Page_fans_country page_follows_country Page_fan_adds no alternative Page_fan_adds_unique no alternative Page_fan_removes no alternative page_fan_removes_unique no alternative page_impressions page_media_view page_impressions_paid page_media_view with is_from_ads breakdown page_impressions_viral no alternative page_impressions_nonviral no alternative post_impressions post_media_view post_impressions_paid post_media_view with is_from_ads breakdown post_impressions_fan post_media_view with is_from_followers breakdown post_impressions_organic post_media_view with is_from_ads breakdown post_impressions_viral no alternative post_impressions_nonviral no alternative ---

body_text: Is anyone else getting this error recently? I've had 2 Magic ETLs suddenly stop working without any real cause with this same error message. It's too vague to diagnose and the preview runs perfectly, so I'm stuck. Screenshot 2025-10-07 at 11.39.38 AM.png
title: Dataflow "Not Runnable" Error

body_text: A " Not Runnable " error in Magic ETL usually indicates that the ETL cannot execute due to issues with its structure, dependencies, or configuration. Here are common causes: Disconnected or Missing Inputs If a dataset used as input for the ETL is deleted, renamed, or inaccessible, the ETL cannot run. Invalid or Broken Transformations Any transformation (like Filter, Join, Group By, or Formula) that has invalid configuration can prevent execution. Examples: • Using a column that no longer exists. • Syntax errors in a formula tile. Circular Dependencies If the ETL’s output is somehow being used as an input in a way that creates a loop, Domo will mark it as “Not Runnable.” Missing Output Dataset If the output dataset of the ETL is deleted or its connection is broken, the ETL cannot run. Unsupported Operations Certain transformations may not be compatible with the dataset type (e.g., trying to perform a join on incompatible types). Permissions or Access Issues If you don’t have read/write permissions on the input or output datasets, Domo will prevent execution.
title: Dataflow "Not Runnable" Error

body_text: The preview is running perfectly, which would indicate no structural or configuration issues. I am the owner of each input dataset. Also, it already ran successfully 40 times up until today, and I did not change anything.
title: Dataflow "Not Runnable" Error

body_text: The preview only samples data. Such as the first thousand rows. The full ETL may hit limits or collisions the preview does not catch. New rows of data might contain a field that was previously clean and now has NULL or unexpected values. Check critical fields like dates, Ids, and numbers. Check case sensitivity (where applicable) & types such as number to string. Make sure the schema hasn't changed Could be a Domo platform glitch due to a recent update. Especially if multiple ETLs are failing. If you suspect that, open a help ticket with Domo Support. This is where the new disable tile(s) feature would be handy. You could disable sections and verify the rest runs up to a point to trace down the issue. My guess is there is a data anomaly in new rows. Null values or

body_text: Our organization considers non-interactive, service-to-service authentication a critical capability for integrating Domo with external systems like Databricks and other enterprise platforms. At present, Domo’s OAuth implementation only supports interactive (user-based) authentication, which requires individual user credentials. This creates several challenges: Integrations are tied to a single user account. Automated data pipelines and system-to-system processes are difficult to maintain. There are potential security and operational risks if a user account changes or is deactivated. Request: We request that Domo add support for non-interactive OAuth authentication (service principal or equivalent) that allows secure, automated, and user-independent authentication between systems. Value / Impact: Enables secure, fully automated integrations without relying on personal user accounts. Reduces operational and security risks tied to user-based tokens. Improves scalability and reliability of enterprise workflows and scheduled jobs. Aligns with industry-standard best practices for cloud platform authentication. This capability would be a significant enhancement for enterprise customers and greatly simplify integration management across systems.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Support for Non-Interactive Service-to-Service Authentication (OAuth / Service Principal)

body_text: The idea behind this would be to render the iframe of the page with a variable value already set by the src url, like passing a pfilter, so when the page loads, it is loaded with the variable with the passed value.
title: Is there a way to set variables to an embedded page like passing pfilters?

body_text: In my experience with embedded Domo content, variables and other elements are fairly black-boxed and difficult to interact with. In developing with Domo bricks over the last year, using the Domo native library, it's set up so developers only have read permissions for a Domo environment such as an app or dashboard. You can read events and read content, but can't write to the environment it's in. From an iframe, you might be able to pick up events, but I don't think you can set variables based on the pfilter. My suggestion would be to use page filters for apps and dashboards. Alternatively, if you want an app to act differently, you might consider developing a Domo brick for your card with a variable control inside. You can make it default to different variable values based on the url the brick is in using the "window.location.href" variable.
title: Is there a way to set variables to an embedded page like passing pfilters?

body_text: Hi, In my Magic ETL dataflow, I tried to use a Python scripting tile to dynamically pivot monthly forecast data and generate new columns for a rolling 18 month window. However, when the new month starts, the Python tile correctly adds the new columns for the tail end of the rolling 18th month window, but the Python output schema still includes the previous month's column (e.g., "2025 Sep Fcst"). This means the dataset retains outdated columns and I have to manually update the Python schema if I want only the current rolling window. I cannot find an option in the Python tile or anywhere in Magic ETL to allow dynamic schema changes or automatically update the output schema to match only the current columns generated by the Python script. I need a way for the output schema of the Python tile to adapt each run—removing old month columns and adding new ones—so subsequent tiles always get the correct set of forecast columns without manual maintenance or intervention. Is there a best practice or a supported way in Domo Magic ETL to make the Python tile’s output schema update dynamically as column names change month-to-month, so the flow remains fully automated? Thanks in advance!
title: Python Tile Dynamic Update of Pivoted Columns

body_text: Based on your comments, I would expect to leverage the Domo API . But I wouldn't expect the Python tile to handle anything like that. In Domo Magic ETL, the Python scripting tile must declare a static output schema. Domo enforces that so downstream tiles and datasets know the column structure ahead of time. Even if your Python code dynamically creates or drops columns, Domo “freezes” the schema based on what was present when you first saved the tile. Have you tried keeping a fixed schema and pivot the output later? Or — run it outside Domo (e.g., in a scheduled script or a Domo Jupyter Workspace).
title: Python Tile Dynamic Update of Pivoted Columns

body_text: That makes sense based on the behavior of magic ETL tiles and the example above. Yes, I am now executing this example in a Domo Jupyter Workspace and it seems to have solved the problem. Thank you for your input!

body_text: I’m trying to automate updates across multiple Domo Everywhere subscriber sites (like setting host URLs, adding roles, etc.) using Workflows. Each subscriber has its own Domo Access Token account. If I manually select the account in my Code Engine step (as an input of type Account), everything works great and I can effect all the changes on that single site. Given the number of sites I have though, that's a big pain, and I'm hoping to find a way to loop through a list of URLs and access token accounts to do this all programatically. I tried using /domo/accounts/v1 and ce.getAccount() to dynamically bind to an account object by ID or name, but Code Engine seems to only work when the account is preselected. I either get “No account found” or an HTML auth redirect. Has anyone figured out a way to bind accounts dynamically inside Code Engine or Workflows, so you can loop through subscribers without manually selecting each account? Or figured out another way to easily manage making changes to dozens or hundreds of subscriber sites?
title: Code engine to loop through subscriber sites and take actions?

body_text: In Code Engine and Workflows, the account input type would be statically bound to the compiled execution. So the credentials would be to one account. I don't think you can dynamically switch at runtime. This isn’t a bug; it’s a security boundary in the Code Engine runtime. If there's a way, I'd love to see it.
title: Code engine to loop through subscriber sites and take actions?

body_text: In the Domo sandbox environment we initially deployed dashboards under a single Pages repository using a shared dataset. Now we plan to deploy an additional dashboard utilizing the same dataset. We're unsure whether it's necessary to create a separate repository for each dashboard deployment. Additionally we've encountered a challenge: whenever we add new dashboards to the common repository we're required to reselect all previously deployed dashboards for production which is becoming cumbersome.
title: Deployment Challenges with Shared Repository in Domo Sandbox

body_text: I believe a repository is essentially a deployment package that tells which content to move between environments. If a single repository is shared for multiple dashboards, the entire repository is the deployable thing. Any time you add or remove, you'd have to reselect all the contents. If multiple dashboards depend on the same dataset, try : Put that dataset in its own repository (e.g., Shared_Datasets ). Deploy that shared repo first. Then link the dashboards’ repositories to those datasets (they’ll reference the production copies after deployment).
title: Deployment Challenges with Shared Repository in Domo Sandbox

body_text: Proposed Enhancement: Add a new tile type or function in Magic ETL, for example: 1. Alert Tile Triggers when a specified condition is true (e.g., when a dataset contains rows, when a metric exceeds a threshold, etc.) Can optionally write an alert message to the activity log or push to Domo notifications. 2. Email Tile Sends an email to designated users or groups. Can use dynamic fields from the ETL (e.g., dataset name, counts, timestamps). Supports optional HTML/text templates. 3. Webhook Tile (optional) Allows Magic ETL to send a simple webhook payload to external systems (Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, ServiceNow, etc.) without requiring a separate Domo Workflow. Example Use Cases: Notify admins if any dataset has not updated within its expected frequency. Send automated data quality reports when a validation check fails. Alert analysts when a data feed stops due to expired Workbench credentials. Push summary status messages after ETL jobs complete successfully or with warnings. Benefits: Reduces dependency on manual alert setup via Domo cards. Enables true end-to-end automation within ETL pipelines. Simplifies operational monitoring (no need for external scripts or workflows). Improves real-time awareness of data issues. Example UI Concept: A new Magic ETL tile named “ Send Alert / Email ” with configuration options such as: Trigger Condition: (Boolean expression or row count condition) Recipients: (User list, group, or dynamic field) Subject / Message Body: (Free text with variable substitution) Delivery Options: Email, Domo Notification, Webhook Impact: This feature would make Magic ETL a more complete data automation platform , aligning it with modern ETL tools that support in-flow alerting. body_text: We generate Public Share links for our dashboards. We have any issue where the link displays all unfiltered data, before the filtered data appears.
