body_text: It could be that the link briefly shows unfiltered data before applying filters, which would indicate a timing or permissions issue where Domo is fetching data before fully enforcing the permissions/filters for that user. If a user generating the link has broader dataset permission than other people, the initial data fetch may include everything they can see, and only after the dashboard applies filters does it narrow down. But users with restrictive permissions shouldn't see the unfiltered data because the fetch itself would be limited from the get go. That's a guess, btw.

body_text: I am attempting to write a where clause in the Netsuite Analytics connector to reduce the number of rows I am pulling on each run. body_text: Try WHERE TH.TRANDATE >= TO_DATE('2024-01-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD') I don't think Netsuite knows the SQL version YEAR().
title: NETSUITE ANALYTICS CONNECT

body_text: @ArborRose unfortunately that doesn't work. I have tried the following and all receive an error message TH.TRANDATE >= TO_DATE('2024-01-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD') EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TH.TRANDATE) >= 2024 TO_CHAR(TH.TRANDATE, 'YYYY') >= '2024' I have submitted a ticket to Domo support but I believe this is most likely just a limitation of the connector and isn't supported.
title: NETSUITE ANALYTICS CONNECT

body_text: Based on review of multiple support sites, the following apparently are NetSuite supported. Function NetSuite Support Notes _1 ----------- ------------------ ------- ADD_MONTHS(date, integer) Yes Returns the date plus the specified number of months. LAST_DAY(date) Yes Returns the date of the last day of the month for the given date. NEXT_DAY(date, char) Yes Returns the date of the first specified weekday (char) that is later than the input date. ROUND(date, fmt) Yes Returns date rounded to the unit specified by the format model (fmt). TRUNC(date, fmt) Yes Returns date with the time portion truncated, or rounded down to the unit specified by the format model (fmt). TO_DATE(char, fmt) Yes Converts a character string to a DATE value. CURRENT_DATE Yes Returns the current date in the session time zone (datatype DATE). CURRENT_TIMESTAMP Yes Returns the current date and time in the session time zone. MONTHS_BETWEEN(date1, date2) Yes Returns the number of months between two dates (supported but not in your original list). SYSDATE Yes Returns the current date and time based on the server time zone (commonly used).
title: NETSUITE ANALYTICS CONNECT

body_text: To answer my own question, your where clause date needs to match the format of the date setting in your Netsuite instance. Ours happens to be mmm d, yyyy so TH.TRANDATE >= 'JAN 1, 2024' produces the expected result

body_text: I have a form that allows users to select multiple inputs. I need to separate these comma-separated values before the data is useful. I haven't found a Domo-native way to extract these so I'm currently using Magic for this. I am open to alternatives if I have missed something. Only 5-10% of entries are comma-separated, most are single inputs. I would like the ETL to run only when a new entry containing a comma is submitted. I tried using a Dataset View that filters to comma-separated value only, but the ETL runs every time the View runs even if no new data is in the View. Is there a wat to limit when the ETL runs based on a View or based on a conditional like: IF Invoice like '%,%' run ETL ELSE do not run ETL
title: Limit Condition Under Which Magic Runs with Dataset Views as Input

body_text: Domo ETLs executions are trigger based, not condition. It won't trigger on a condition specifically. You would have to simulate a dataset change or something to get the flow to run. Such as having an ETL filter rows where INVOICE LIKE '%,%'. If not rows match the dataset won't change. If rows do match, the flow would trigger when it sees the dataset change. Or you could try using a workflow to watch for dataset conditions. When its met, trigger your ETL or alert.
title: Limit Condition Under Which Magic Runs with Dataset Views as Input

body_text: I have survey results collected twice a year. I am filter the data by dates for my dashboard. However, even though there are results that exists after Oct 1, 2025, the Magic ETL is not filtering them and is giving me blank results. Filter 1 and Filter 2 between date ranges where as filter three has > Oct 1, 2025.
title: Date Filtering not giving results

body_text: Things to check/test: 1. The timezone settings in your instance. 2. When you run your preview in Magic ETL, it limits how many rows from the data are running in the preview. It defaults to 10k rows and if your dataset is larger than 10k rows, the October 2025 values may not be getting processed when running the preview. You can bump this up 5 million rows when running previews. If your data is greater than 5m rows, you will just need to save and run the dataflow and see if the rows appear. 3. Datatype. Is the created field datetime? 4. Triple check that there are indeed values in the input dataset >= October 1 @ 07:33am 5. If none of those solve it, you could also try doing a Formula Rule in the filter instead of a Filter Rule: DATE( __created__ ) >= '2025-10-01'
title: Date Filtering not giving results

As far as I know, Domo does not support exploding the output - where each selection in your multi-select becomes its own row automatically. I believe there have been requests asking for this feature (turning multi-select selections into separate rows. Description: I’d like to propose the addition of two key features for Domo App Studio Forms that would significantly enhance its functionality and usability. These omissions currently present challenges in how we collect and manage data through forms, and addressing them would improve the overall user experience.

1. Page Filter Integration with Form Submissions There is currently no known mechanism to automatically capture and save page filters when forms are submitted. This missing functionality makes it difficult to understand the specific context (e.g., region, date, category) a user had applied during form submission.

Use Case: Often, form submissions need to be tied to specific filter values, such as regions or timeframes. Having these filters saved with the form responses would provide vital context and allow for better analysis and application of the input data.

Proposed Solution: Introduce the ability to save page filter values as part of form submissions, ensuring that users’ inputs are tied to the specific data context in which they are working.

2. Table Section for Multi-Row Entries Currently, there is no built-in table section that allows users to populate a form with data from a dataset and manipulate multiple rows at once. Users are forced to input data row by row, which is highly inefficient for bulk entry tasks. This functionality is available in the existing version of forms and is one of the most used features, making its absence in App Studio a significant limitation.

Use Case: For processes that require users to edit or input data for multiple rows at a time (e.g., updating multiple records or entries in bulk), a table section that pulls from a dataset would allow users to efficiently manage larger sets of data without repetitive, single-row entry.

Proposed Solution: Reintroduce or enhance App Studio forms with a table section that allows users to populate forms with rows of data from a dataset and manipulate them in bulk. This would greatly improve productivity for tasks requiring bulk data input.

Thank you for considering these ideas. I’m happy to provide additional context if needed.

body_text: Okay, another thought is Mark's approach to splitting and pivoting is pretty computationally inefficient because of the huge join, which is probably why it takes 45 seconds. (It's also very clever within the restrictions of MagicETL, so no shade on Mark). If you could get that time down, you could still use the data in its current form. I would guess under 10 seconds would be annoying but usable. First thought: is there a maximum number of items a user will reasonably select? Mark joined his on up to 31 splits, but if you know that there will never be more than 5 (for example), than you can save a lot of time. Is there a way to split/pivot only the most recent form(s) instead of all of them every time? Like, do it more recursively. Maybe, bring in the old already pivoted data, bring in the form data, but filter for only forms submitted after the already pivoted data. Pivot/filter that new data and append it to the old data. I wonder how much time you could save doing that.
title: App Studio Form Output for Multi-select

body_text: I checked and the max number of selections so far has been 80. I did add a pre-processing step in the morning that handles all old entries. This allows my main ETL to only need to import form entries from today. ETL time has dropped from 40-45 seconds to 18-20. This is better, but still not as performant as using Views. Using Views has the added benefit of Syncing differently and allowing users to maintain their filters.

body_text: Cutting time in less than half isn't too bad! Another thought is I wonder if you could use a Python or R scripting tile to split and pivot the data more efficiently than joining every new entry with 80 rows. (Makes the ETL cost twice as many credits, so depending on your credit budget, might not be worth it). I know R's tidyr library has the perfect function for this situation: separate_longer_delim(). Unfortunately, Domo's R environment is too outdated to use it in MagicETL, but it wouldn't be that hard to code using older R functions or in Python.

body_text: I don’t see anything in your steps that would make a link clickable. Which is obviously the question…how do we? Let’s take a quick step back and review how links work in HTML. A basic anchor tag looks like this: Visit Domo Community Forums HTML is a markup language that uses tags wrapped in < > to define elements. The tag starts an anchor (a link), and ends it. The href attribute defines the destination of the link—short for “hypertext reference.” The text between the tags is what the user sees and clicks: Visit Domo Community Forums When you see a Domo reference like this: https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/36[PHONE]?language=en_US …it usually means you need to embed that anchor tag inside your text. Often this is done with a CONCAT statement in Domo, for example: CONCAT(' ','Link Text',' ') That creates HTML output like this, where target="_blank" ensures the link opens in a new tab: Link Text In your post, you’re describing links but not actually constructing them. The documentation is assuming some familiarity with HTML—what you need to do is embed anchor tags directly in the workflow’s text.
title: How to Include Clickable URLs in Domo Workflow Forms

body_text: I have a dataset with quite a few datetime fields all in UTC. It's powering programmatically embedded apps that are being viewed by users in different time zones. body_text: Yes, its possible. Time zones shift by hours, centralized on UTC (Universal Time). Depending upon the local time zone, you shift so many hours. In Dallas, I am 5 hours off UTC time…depending upon daylight savings. Meaning when it's 1 PM in Dallas, it is 6 PM UTC. DATE_ADD(`utc_datetime`, INTERVAL `user_offset_hours` HOUR) Detect the user’s local time zone in your embedding layer (JavaScript can do this). Then pass that into Domo as a parameter or filter variable.

body_text: I believe the solution to this is to append your data. For example if you had two groups, one that could see revenue and one that couldn't, you would just append your data to itself once, and zero out the revenue values in the appended data. You would also have an additional column that would distinguish which is which and then create your PDP on that additional column. This would keep everything as one dataset as you could just do the append at the very end of your ETL. Hope that makes sense.
title: PDP on Columns?

body_text: @MarkSnodgrass welp, I am confused. I wanted to know if I can do PDP on a single column. It sounded like you said I cannot? But, the 2nd to last sentence you said I would "...create your PDP on that additional column" ?
title: PDP on Columns?

body_text: @Canioagain sorry I wasn't clear. You are applying PDP based on values in column, which will hide that entire row. I was suggesting creating a column called "ShowRevenue", for example and it would contain values Yes and No. In your ETL, duplicate the data, but in one set of the duplicate zero out the revenue column and make the ShowRevenue column No. In the other set of the data that has the revenue values, set ShowRevenue to Yes. Then, create a PDP policy that has the people that can see revenue in one group base the policy off of ShowRevenue = Yes and then another policy for those that can't see revenue and base it off of ShowRevenue = No. If you haven't looked at this example, this may help. Although, they didn't duplicate the data, the filtering on values concept is the same. https://domohelp.domo.com/hc/en-us/articles/36[PHONE]-Creating-and-Deleting-PDP-Policies#5. Hope this helps.
title: PDP on Columns?

body_text: Hey @Data_Devon congrats again on the MajorDomo cert! How I would approach this is to add a 3rd table or some logic to your data. The 3rd table would be an allocation table to would maintain split allocation, effective dates, etc… You could then join this table to have fields that would tell you: 1. If there is a split for this Provider 2. If the appointment falls within the split effective period 3. What the split allocation is You could alternatively accomplish this through logic in a formula tile in your ETL, but this may be a pain to maintain. The benefit of the Allocation table is that it could be maintained by a sales ops or other operations person at your company AND you'd have a detailed source of truth and history of allocations. Your data might end up looking something like this: Appointment Provider Galley Split? Split Allocation Eval Mitch John FALSE 1 Eval Justin John FALSE 1 Eval Kristin Tanner TRUE 0.5 Eval Kristin Tanner TRUE 0.5 Eval Kristin Brent TRUE 0.5 Eval Kristin Brent TRUE 0.5

body_text: Workaround CLI wasn't working for me (IT issues). I needed this so I could update some partial blank columns of old records due to new calculations added in. This is what I did: 1 - updated the original Magic ETL to have a one-for-one input to output (existing dataset inputs) without changing the output tiles but still including the calcs needed 2 - changed ETL outputs to Replace since all records are in the input now 3 - ran updated ETL 4 - reverted to previous version of ETL that pulls in the "new records" dataset and Upserts them to the output dataset This would also work if there was a flaw in calculated columns that needed to be fixed. Just make sure the calc fix gets on the newest version so you don't have to do it again. I plan on documenting this process in detail for my company. This won't be a common thing but is super important to ensure complete and accurate data. The data team is small (90% just me) and the data volume is millions of records much of which is new each day needing to flow through to the users. A Domo tool that allows selection of output data set would better allow corrections to the data external to the main data flow.

body_text: Idea: I’d love to see a feature in Domo that allows us to rename dataset columns once, and have those changes automatically reflected everywhere that column is referenced (cards, drill paths, ETLs, beast modes, etc.). Problem Today: When we want to rename a column (for example, changing “Parent Account” to “Parent Customer”), we have to update every single reference across cards, filters, beast modes, drill paths, ETLs, and report filters. This is extremely time-consuming and risks breaking existing reports. Additionally, many datasets have duplicate or near-duplicate fields (e.g., “Parent Account,” “Parent Client,” “Parent Customer”) that would ideally be consolidated into one consistent name. Without a global rename, cleaning this up creates disruption. Why It Matters: Saves significant time and manual rework. Reduces risk of broken cards, drill paths, and ETLs. Encourages standardization of naming conventions across the org. Makes it easier for users to navigate and understand datasets. Proposed Solution: A “global column rename” or “replace all references” feature: Admins can rename a field once at the dataset level. All dependent cards, filters, beast modes, drill paths, ETLs, and report filters automatically update with the new name. Optionally, Domo could provide a preview/impact analysis showing which items will be updated. This would provide massive efficiency gains and improve data governance for all Domo users.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Global Column Rename

Increased Complexity: It forces the creation of extra dataflows for what should be a simple filtering step, cluttering the data pipeline. Higher Costs: It inflates data storage and processing costs within the Domo platform. Delayed Insights: The time taken to import and then process large, unfiltered datasets delays the availability of fresh data for decision-making. For example, if a Google Sheet contains 100,000 records but a user only needs the last two days' worth of data, they are forced to import all 100,000 rows and then build an ETL to filter them. body_text: I have a VERY large dataset that I've uploaded to Domo. I initially did a REPLACE to load the whole dataset. I then changed the workbench job to APPEND and use an 'update date' in the table to run HOURLY while checking back the past couple days for any new/missed data. Due to some bugs on our side, sometimes very old data needs to be corrected, so I have to do a REPLACE again, which can take hours. Is there any way to establish a regular REPLACE job, perhaps monthly, which will run automatically without messing up the hourly APPEND job on that same dataset?
title: How to periodically REPLACE in addition to APPEND jobs?

body_text: You'd need two separate jobs, one for hourly append and one for monthly replace updating the same dataset. There is some risk involved with this as it can cause them both to run at the same time and get unexpected results. What you can do is limit the hourly job to run in between certain hours and then once a month or whatever you schedule the replace job to be within the append job downtime.
title: How to periodically REPLACE in addition to APPEND jobs?

body_text: @JunkDoom have a close look at Partitioning. Many Domo connectors are starting to support partition schemes based on Date. If your data is not partitioned by Date you can use the CLI to create your own partition tags as you upload data. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A9g2rc2Fy_w&t=3s the in-Domo ETL version of "Partitioning" can be recreated with Recursive Dataflows. https://domohelp.domo.com/hc/en-us/articles/36[PHONE]-Creating-a-Recursive-Snapshot-DataFlow-in-Magic-ETL There is a beta (or is it GA @GrantSmith ) for Magic ETL + Partitions. You want to be careful mixing Partition with Replace. Replace will Replace your entire dataset WITHOUT partition_tags. meaning that if you tried to mix Replace with Append+Partition you would duplicate data.
title: How to periodically REPLACE in addition to APPEND jobs?

body_text: @GrantSmith Thanks! After some trial and error and confusing schema warnings, here's what's working for me so far: -Create a new REPLACE job, and RUN it. -Change the job to APPEND, which will then allow you to pick an UPSERT key in the "schema" tab. (may need to uncheck "Protect" on that column. -Change the query to look back X days on a date field -Create a separate REPLACE job without any date range in the query -In the "Overview" tab, under "Domo Details" under "Dataset Name", click the "Browse" button to pick the proper dataset for this to load into. If you TYPE the name, it will create a separate dataset with the SAME EXACT NAME. (yuck!) -Schedule your new replace and append jobs as appropriate.

You’re noticing that when you open a form in a pop up via a button, the filter value from your dashboard’s dropdown isn’t being passed into the form’s dropdown as it is when the form is embedded directly on the dashboard. body_text: You can use Domo forms to collect submissions and write those submissions to a Domo dataset. Then using a card, display the submitted data in a dashboard. For example, if the status is set to "approved", trigger an alert or update another dataset, etc. Inline edits would require bricks or writeback apps. A card won't support inline editing out of the box.

body_text: Our Finance team relies heavily on the New Domo Office Excel Add-In when using the Dataset Import function to pull large datasets from Domo. The add-in works well for basic imports, but there are critical gaps that limit efficiency and accuracy for financial workflows: No indication of how many rows will be imported once filters are applied. A row count preview would help users estimate load times and confirm dataset scope before committing to the import. The preview pane only displays the first 100 rows. Finance and audit teams often need to scan deeper to validate filters, check for outliers, or confirm ordering logic. Even the ability to page through (e.g., “next 100” or “next 1,000”) would address this gap. Filters appear to be limited to single-condition logic. Users need to build filters with both AND and OR operators, consistent with Analyzer/DataSet views. Example: (Department = Finance OR Department = Accounting) AND Period >= 202501. Importing large datasets has no early warning about row size or performance impact. A lightweight estimate such as “~250k rows / ~30MB” would help teams refine filters before pulling into Excel. Summary of Request: Enhance the New Office Add-In (Dataset Import function) with: Row count visibility after filter application Ability to preview more than 100 rows Full AND/OR filter logic Import size/performance awareness These improvements would make the New Office Add-In’s Dataset Import function far more robust for Finance and other teams working with high-volume data, while reducing trial-and-error and improving trust in the results.

body_text: The Problem My company publishes datasets to all subscribers on Domo Everywhere. Customers often need to manipulate these datasets (filtering, renaming, adding columns), which works fine in Dataset Views. They also frequently need to join datasets. While Views can handle joins for materialized datasets, joins on the datasets we publish to subscribers fail. The functionality appears available, but Domo confirmed it does not work for non-materialized datasets. This creates two major issues: User Experience – Customers see functionality that looks enabled but does not work. Credit Usage Impact – Every join must be done in MagicETL, costing us a credit each time it runs. Since we refresh datasets three times per day, subscriber ETLs update just as often, compounding costs quickly. This is not just an annoyance for my instance. Any Domo customer publishing datasets to subscribers will run into the same problem. Enabling joins in Views for non-materialized datasets would eliminate wasted credits and prevent users from having to go to the more complex MagicETL interface for simple joins. Issues specific to my setup that add urgency We publish Views (e.g., View A = join of Datasets 1+2; View B = join of Datasets 3+4). Customers then join View A and View B in MagicETL, which runs every time underlying datasets update. With three refreshes per day, a single ETL can consume 12 credits daily . Even with workarounds (setting update frequency to run only after all sources update), it still costs 6 credits per day . Customers rarely grasp this nuance, and I have no way to enforce optimal settings. The new Data Refresh Permissions don’t solve the problem - I can't add a limitation on time (e.g. when datasets update … the ETL and hasn't refreshed within the last hour) because then the update will only run when the very first of the underlying datasets updates. Bottom Line Customers need the ability to join published datasets directly in Views. Without it, we and others waste credits and frustrate users with misleading functionality.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Enable Joins in Views on published datasets

body_text: Hello, Currently I've created a number of tables cards in my dashboards that my users like to export into excel, the issue is that the formatting of the exported file isn't great and my users aren't happy with how limited the export is. Is there a way I can create export options through the dashboards or Apps that format the data akin to exporting data as reports with a reporting program like crystal? Is there any code examples that have been created to help with the exporting of data to format it to be more like a report, like adding dynamic tiles / dates? Thanks, any help would be great.
title: Exporting data into formatted report?

body_text: Not really. Not in the way you are looking for. Domo’s native export options (Excel, CSV, PDF) are limited. You cannot control formatting, add dynamic headers/dates, or create multi-section, report-style layouts purely through Domo dashboards. Exported Excel files will be basic tables without merged cells, advanced formatting, or dynamic tiles. You could try building a dashboard specifically for reporting. Arrange multiple cards in a clean layout and export to PDF. Or you can use the Domo API to generate reports externally. Pull the dataset using the API using Python or some other method. Within your code, create bold headers, dynamic dates, conditional formatting, etc. This is the only way to replicate a Crystal Report-style report.
title: Exporting data into formatted report?

body_text: So is there no way via app creation to export the table via a button which points to some work flow / some other means to export the table with top level code into an excel format?
title: Exporting data into formatted report?

body_text: As I mentioned, you could try to build out something that calls the Domo API. Maybe someone has code out there. In a brick or procode, I'd try something like: Download Dataset to Excel With some kind of JavaScript or other code that looks something like this: import * as XLSX from "xlsx"; document.getElementById("exportBtn").addEventListener("click", async () => { const datasetId = "YOUR_DATASET_ID"; // replace with your dataset ID const token = "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"; // secure this properly! try { // Fetch dataset data as CSV (works well for Excel conversion) const resp = await fetch(`https://api.domo.com/v1/datasets/${datasetId}/data?includeHeader=true`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: "text/csv" } }); const csvText = await resp.text(); // Convert CSV → Excel sheet const workbook = XLSX.utils.book_new(); const worksheet = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json( XLSX.read(csvText, { type: "string" }).Sheets.Sheet1, { header: 1 } ); XLSX.utils.book_append_sheet(workbook, XLSX.utils.aoa_to_sheet(worksheet), "Data"); // Trigger download XLSX.writeFile(workbook, "dataset_export.xlsx"); } catch (err) { console.error("Export failed:", err); alert("There was an error exporting the dataset."); } }); But I'm sure its more complicated than this. You have security issues, user access to the dataset, etc.
title: Exporting data into formatted report?

body_text: You can get pretty close to your report's format with just a default pivot table and a BeastMode: Here's what it looks like exported to Excel: Note that the header color was maintained. body_text: So, I have a page in an app that only uses blank bricks, because the built-in Domo components didn't have the functionality we needed for a visualization. This page is used as a drill-in for another page in the same app. My question is, is there a way to pass filters to that page when navigating to it? The navigation is done using a hyperlink in a brick on another page, so simply applying the filters on that page and navigating via a button (persisting filters) isn't going to work. I found a post from a couple of years ago about using pFilters, but when trying to apply them in the url of the page, the brick simply…bricks. It refuses to connect to ANY data and throws an error in the console. Any help y'all can provide would be amazing, thank you!
title: Is there a way to pass app filters to bricks?

body_text: Sure. You can do almost anything with a brick. Let's start with a basic brick to display a sample data file Here are the code parts: HTML: JavaScript: var domo = window.domo; var datasets = window.datasets; // get the data domo.get(`data/v1/${datasets[0]}`).then(function(result){ var tableHTML = " "; // Extract headers and make them bold var headers = Object.keys(result[0]); headers.forEach(function(header) { tableHTML += " " + header + " "; }); tableHTML += " "; // Loop through each row and populate table result.forEach(function(row) { tableHTML += " "; headers.forEach(function(header) { tableHTML += " " + row[header] + " "; }); tableHTML += " "; }); tableHTML += " "; // Link to html document.getElementById("result").innerHTML = tableHTML; }); CSS: table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; } th, td { border: 1px solid black; padding: 8px; text-align: left; } th { background-color: #4CABC5; color: white; font-weight: bold; } td:nth-child(3) { border-left: 3px solid black; border-right: 3px solid black; background-color: #A3D4E1; } Product,Sales Product A,1200 Product B,950 Product C,870 Product D,1500 Product E,400 Product F,200 Product G,1750 Product H,300 Product I,100 Product J,600 Display without filtering: Now we modify the code to accept filtering from the URL var domo = window.domo; var datasets = window.datasets; // Get pfilters from URL var filters = getPfiltersFromUrl(); function getPfiltersFromUrl() { var params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search); if (params.has("pfilters")) { try { return JSON.parse(params.get("pfilters")); } catch (e) { console.error("Invalid pfilters JSON in URL:", e); } } return []; } // Fetch dataset0 domo.get(`data/v1/${datasets[0]}`).then(function(result){ var filteredData = result; // Apply filters manually filters.forEach(function(f) { var col = f.column; var operand = f.operand; var values = f.values; if (operand === "IN") { filteredData = filteredData.filter(function(row){ return values.includes(row[col]); }); } // You could add other operands (GT, LT, etc.) here if needed }); // Build table var tableHTML = " "; var headers = Object.keys(filteredData[0] || {}); headers.forEach(function(header) { tableHTML += " " + header + " "; }); tableHTML += " "; filteredData.forEach(function(row){ tableHTML += " "; headers.forEach(function(header){ tableHTML += " " + row[header] + " "; }); tableHTML += " "; }); tableHTML += " "; document.getElementById("result").innerHTML = tableHTML; }); Which displays this when filtered to Product D. The URL encoded pfilter: [{"column":"Product","operand":"IN","values":["Product D"]}] Encoded: https://yourinstance.domo.com/page/[PHONE]?pfilters=%5B%7B%22column%22%3A%22Product%22%2C%22operand%22%3A%22IN%22%2C%22values%22%3A%5B%22Product%20D%22%5D%7D%5D
title: Is there a way to pass app filters to bricks?

body_text: Hi everyone, I’m trying to replicate a view like this in Domo: I have three columns in my dataset: Date Airline Name Revenue What I’d like to build is a table that shows: Current month’s revenue Previous month’s revenue and % change (MoM) Same month last year’s revenue and % change (YoY) Will I have to manipulate Pivot Table chart or could I potentially download a chart that would make this layout possible?
title: Building a “Current Month vs Previous Month vs Last Year” comparison card (or dashboard) in Domo?

body_text: You can do date comparisons on a normal table chart….or a pivot chart but its not necessary. Look back at past forum questions and you see references with formulas such as CY, PY, P2Y (current year, previous year, previous 2 years). It works for comparing years, or months depending upon the formula. Example, if you want current year to date use something like this: sum( case when YEAR(`date`) = YEAR(CURRENT_DATE()) and `date` <= CURRENT_DATE() then `amount` else 0 end ) Previous year to date would be something like: SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(`date`) = YEAR(CURDATE()) - 1 AND `date` < DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) THEN `amount` ELSE 0 END) and so on. For change/difference or % of change do use your CY, PY, and P2Y. If you need months versus years, do the same type formulas but instead of YEAR(date) and interval 1 year, use Month(date) and interval 1 month. Note - in most cases for current year, you probably only have data up to current date, so you may not need that second line. But on past years you do need it.
title: Building a “Current Month vs Previous Month vs Last Year” comparison card (or dashboard) in Domo?

body_text: Hi All I'm sure this has been asked a few times but I couldn't find a specific answer that helped with my challenge I have a PIVOT Table which contains all of my financial data rows consisting of Costs and Revenues I want to calculate a share of revenue for each cost whilst having a filter on my card to remove the Revenue line however when I filter out revenue all the shares drop to 0 I've not used FIXED functions to level before so could use some help and guidance on how to show share of revenue % on my table and filter out the revenue row Thanks Dan
title: FIXED Function with filter on card

body_text: The fixed function in Beast Mode lets you compute a value across a fixed level of aggregation, ignoring filters on specific rows. Using a beast mode to represent Total Revenue (fixed) FIXED (SUM(CASE WHEN `Type` = 'Revenue' THEN `Amount` ELSE 0 END)) and use that in another formula for % Share CASE WHEN `Type` = 'Cost' THEN `Amount` / FIXED (SUM(CASE WHEN `Type` = 'Revenue' THEN `Amount` ELSE 0 END)) ELSE NULL END Filter out Type = 'Revenue' and the table should show cost rows. Cost Category Amount % of Revenue Labor 50,000 10.0% Software 25,000 5.0% Btw, I don't have any sample data created to confirm this works.
title: FIXED Function with filter on card

body_text: @_DanielB_ FIXED functions have the ability to aggregate while ignoring certain fields when filtered using FILTER NONE, FILTER DENY, and FILTER ALLOW, which you can read about here: https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/440[PHONE]?language=en_US In your specific case, if you wanted the denominator of your calculation to ignore all filters, you could set it up like this: sum(`Revenue`) / sum(sum(`Revenue`)) FIXED (FILTER NONE)

body_text: Assuming Salesforce Advance connector uses these API: What is the difference between REST API and BULK API? Use cases?
title: Salesforce Advance Connector - Browse Object Tile vs Browse in Bulk Tile

body_text: The REST API would be optimized for real-time, small queries. You request a dataset and SalesForce returns the results immediately. Probably has request limits and daily quotes. Use case would be for syncing a single object like pull all accounts or leads daily. For dashboards that don't require a bunch of historial data. i.e. "Give me today's updates." The Bulk API would be optmized for large scale data extractions. It would create a job, process the request asynchronously, and return the data in chunks. This would handle big datasets (millions) more efficiently than the REST API. You won't get the data instantly because it runs the job to fetch the results. The use case would be for getting history for many years. Like event logs.
title: Salesforce Advance Connector - Browse Object Tile vs Browse in Bulk Tile

body_text: My answer is still the same. You are trying to use a state map, but your logic happens at the county level. • Counties need to be flagged first (fail vs not fail). • Then you roll those up at the state to count failing counties. • Then you display that count on the state map. Step 1 : County level fail flag to get a Boolean - true or false. This is the formula that marks each country as failed or not failed. Use this only when your data is grouped by county. CASE WHEN (SUM(fail_events) / SUM(total_events)) > 0.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END Step 2 : Aggregate to the state level (count the failing counties) You need to roll up those counties into a count per state. The following formula says - for each state, count how many distinct counties crossed the 50% fail threshold. This is the value you'll use for the state map. COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (SUM(fail_events) / SUM(total_events)) > 0.5 THEN county END) Step 3 : Configure the map card Raw data: state county fail_events total_events California Los Angeles 120 200 California San Diego 80 100 California Orange 20 60 California Fresno 40 120 Texas Travis 30 40 Texas Dallas 50 150 Texas Harris 300 400 New York Kings 10 50 New York Queens 70 90 Applied formula: state county fail_events total_events fail_flag California Los Angeles 120 200 1 California San Diego 80 100 1 California Orange 20 60 0 California Fresno 40 120 0 Texas Travis 30 40 1 Texas Dallas 50 150 0 Texas Harris 300 400 1 New York Kings 10 50 0 New York Queens 70 90 1 Aggregated to state level: state failing_counties California 2 Texas 2 New York 1 Drop this on a state map and you will have California shaded with a value of 2. Texas with a value of 2. And New York with a value of 1.

body_text: Hi all, I need to calculate the time between two Timestamp fields in Analyzer: Hotel Arrival Date Hotel Departure Date Goal A numeric duration in hours (decimal) A readable HH:MM string for tables Optional: integer minutes Example Arrival = 2025-08-28 22:10:00 Departure = 2025-08-30 00:20:00 Expected: Hours ≈ 26.17 , HH:MM 26:10 , Minutes 1570 What failed This did not validate in Beast Mode: A) TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, Hotel Arrival Date , Hotel Departure Date ) / 60 B) CASE WHEN Hotel Arrival Date IS NULL OR Hotel Departure Date IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN Hotel Departure Date < Hotel Arrival Date THEN 0 ELSE ROUND( (UNIX_TIMESTAMP( Hotel Departure Date ) - UNIX_TIMESTAMP( Hotel Arrival Date )) / 3600, 2 ) END C) CASE WHEN Hotel Arrival Date IS NULL OR Hotel Departure Date IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN Hotel Departure Date < Hotel Arrival Date THEN '0:00' ELSE CONCAT( FLOOR((UNIX_TIMESTAMP( Hotel Departure Date ) - UNIX_TIMESTAMP( Hotel Arrival Date )) / 3600), ':', LPAD( FLOOR( MOD((UNIX_TIMESTAMP( Hotel Departure Date ) - UNIX_TIMESTAMP( Hotel Arrival Date )), 3600) / 60 ), 2, '0' ) ) END
title: Beast Mode: build “hotel stay duration” from Timestamps

body_text: Using the UNIX_TIMESTAMP function is the way to go to get the time difference. I would start out by just doing the simple subtraction between the two dates using the UNIX_TIMESTAMP around both of them and making sure it validates. Then, start adding in your additional logic for the CASE statement and make sure it validates. I would also refer you to this post on formatting the results. https://community-forums.domo.com/main/discussion/52682/domo-ideas-conference-beast-modes-time-difference-formatting#latest
title: Beast Mode: build “hotel stay duration” from Timestamps

body_text: Exporting a page/dashboard as PDF or PowerPoint is a great feature to help utilise DOMO content outside of the DOMO platform, however when images are used on a dashboard there are some limitations. If the image is uploaded directly, or using links where the image is hosted in DOMO, the images are exported fine. However, we have discovered with a recent use case that if an image is linked from a location that requires user authentication, it is not included in the export. The case has a dashboard that has been set up for multiple areas, and because the different areas report on the same KPI's/measures, filters and PDP are used rather than create 8 different dashboards. Images are required to be updated on a regular basis, the image is then displayed on the dashboard by linking in a HTML table, utilising the same PDP/Filters to determine which area's image to display. First attempt was to upload the images directly into DOMO, however the latest image is required, and automating the revisionId of the image has not yet been figured out. As the images are not able to be hosted on a site that makes them available to the public, the image libraries on our internal SharePoint were created. The link for the files is obtained through the SharePoint connector and combined into a table which then displays on the dashboard. As mentioned above, the issue comes when trying to export the dashboard. Whilst the authentication seems to pass through allowing people to view the dashboard, the export function does not utilise this and the image section of the dashboard shows as a broken image. The export function needs to be able to export everything that the user performing the export can see on the dashboard.

body_text: One of the big drawbacks to Apps currently is not being able to download the whole sheet or even a single card as a PDF. I was wondering if anyone here has some ideas or knows if its even possible to make a pro code brick that would allow us to accomplish this? This is one of the last hurdles we're having for widespread adoption of these new reports we've made so any suggestions would be great!
title: Any ideas for a Pro-code Brick that would allow PDF downloads for embedded apps?

body_text: Similar questions like yours have been asked previously in the forum. The base problem appears to be capturing the state of filters. We can manually export via the UI, but there's no export to pdf action available. And Domo does not expose the API endpoint as far as I know. A possibility may exist if you try to create a brick that can snapshot the screen. But I think the best you would get is the ability to capture what you create on the brick's canvas, not the native Domo dashboard or cards themselves. For example, I created a brick that maps locations and hurricane movement. I could add something to grab that canvas and export it. Capturing a brick might be done using html2canvas or dom-to-image libraries to get a png or jpg. You could then try to hand it off to a pdf library.
title: Any ideas for a Pro-code Brick that would allow PDF downloads for embedded apps?

body_text: We need to surface asset-level performance (headlines/descriptions) from Google Ads inside Domo for better marketing optimization. Right now, the Google Ads connectors in Domo expose the ad_group_ad_asset_view table, but they only return impressions for RSA assets (headlines/descriptions). This matches what we see when testing the API through Domo, but not what the Google Ads API itself supports via GAQL. What we tested in the Google Ads API (GAQL) RSA asset performance (with clicks/cost/conversions, no conversion action segment): SELECT campaign.id, ad_group.id, ad_group_ad.ad.id AS ad_id, ad_group_ad_asset_view.asset AS asset_id, ad_group_ad_asset_view.field_type, metrics.impressions, metrics.clicks, metrics.conversions, metrics.all_conversions, metrics.cost_micros, segments.date FROM ad_group_ad_asset_view RSA asset × conversion action (with conversion splits): SELECT campaign.id, ad_group.id, ad_group_ad.ad.id, ad_group_ad_asset_view.asset, ad_group_ad_asset_view.field_type, metrics.conversions, metrics.all_conversions, segments.conversion_action, segments.conversion_action_name, segments.date FROM ad_group_ad_asset_view PMax assets (conversions available at asset level): SELECT campaign.id, asset_group.id, asset_group_asset.asset AS asset_id, asset_group_asset.field_type, metrics.conversions, segments.date FROM asset_group_asset Smart Campaign assets (combinations, metrics available but only for extensions like SITELINK, STRUCTURED_SNIPPET): SELECT campaign.id, ad_group.id, ad_group_ad.ad.id, ad_group_ad_asset_combination_view.enabled, ad_group_ad_asset_combination_view.served_assets, metrics.impressions, metrics.clicks, metrics.conversions, metrics.all_conversions, segments.date FROM ad_group_ad_asset_combination_view Current limitations in Domo RSA (ad_group_ad_asset_view): Connector only returns impressions , even though the API supports other metrics (clicks, cost, conversions, etc.). PMax (asset_group_asset): No metrics surfaced in the connector, though API supports conversions. Smart (ad_group_ad_asset_combination_view): Limited exposure; metrics not accessible for analysis in Domo. Business need Our marketing team wants to evaluate which headlines & descriptions drive MQLs, Opportunities, and Customers . Conversion actions we track: HubSpot – Marketing Qualified Lead HubSpot – Opportunity HubSpot – Customer Without asset-level metrics in Domo, we can only see impressions. This prevents us from optimizing creative effectively. Request Please update the Google Ads connector to align with the Google Ads API by exposing: For RSA : metrics (clicks, conversions, cost, etc.) at ad_group_ad_asset_view (with and without conversion_action segments). For PMax : conversions at asset_group_asset . For Smart : full metrics (not only for extensions, but also for headline, description) from ad_group_ad_asset_combination_view . This enhancement will allow marketing teams to optimize creative performance more effectively and tie asset performance back to key conversion actions. The priority is more on the RSA - ad_group_ad_asset_view table. Please ensure support for segments.date starting from June 5, 2025, when Google Ads began exposing full asset metrics in the association report. Thanks!
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Enhancement Request: Google Ads Connector – Asset-Level Metrics

body_text: I have a number of cards embedded into a Confluence page along with 2 selectors. Unfortunately on the confluence page the selectors arent working but in the DOMO card settings I have allow filter changes and chart picket enabled. Should the selectors work back to DOMO to change the contents of other cards?
title: Selector filters not working in confluence

body_text: When you embed Domo cards into a Confluence page, the interactive features like selectors (filters) often do not work the same way as they do within the Domo platform. Even if "Allow filter changes" and "Chart Picker" are enabled in Domo, embedded cards typically do not support cross-card filtering or selector-driven interactivity outside of Domo itself. In most cases, embedded cards act as static views, and selectors on the page will not affect other embedded cards. This is a common limitation discussed in the Domo Community. If you need interactive filtering across multiple cards, users generally need to access the cards directly within Domo.
title: Selector filters not working in confluence

body_text: Setting up these two config settings in Databricks Cloud Amplifier: Data Freshness & Data Caching. Are there links to any Domo documentation that defines these settings? How do they function? What's the difference? Is there a difference? I did a cursory look and didn't find anything too helpful for our team.
title: DataBricks - Data Freshness & Data Caching.

body_text: https://domo-support.domo.com/s/article/44[PHONE]?language=en_US https://www.domo.com/blog/how-to-optimize-data-warehouse-strategy-with-cloud-amplifier These are the only documentation links I can find. Feature Purpose & Behavior Data Freshness Checks whether underlying data in the warehouse has changed—triggers reload, alerts, or on-demand refresh. Data Caching (TTL) Temporarily stores previous query results to avoid unnecessary compute; automatically expires after time or data change. Freshness checks evaluate whether data changed; caching stores query results and helps reduce compute cost and latency. They work in tandem but serve different roles. According to the blog, Cloud Amplifier issues freshness-check queries (like querying information_schema) periodically—by default every 15 minutes—to determine if source data in your cloud warehouse (e.g., Databricks) has changed. It uses these to: • Decide whether to trigger ETL flows in Domo. • Trigger dataset alerts. • Determine if on-demand queries should hit the warehouse again or can be served from cache.
title: DataBricks - Data Freshness & Data Caching.

body_text: The easiest thing would be to use a Slicer filter instead of a Radio filter, which gives options to select multiple or select all. body_text: I figured out a way to do it but not sure if this is the best option. Step 1: Add a dummy column which has a constant value. In my case, I added a column called "Site" and entered a constant value (say "Amazon"). Step 2: Using the "Rank and Window" tile, I created a Row ID column using the "ROW_NUMBER" function. See screenshot below. I used the Site field created in the previous step to order the rows. This basically keeps the table rows in the same order as the input file and just adds a row number to it. Step 3: I created another field "Adjusted Row Number" to group a pair of rows with a same row number. I used the MOD function to achieve this. So in my case rows 1 and 2 in my table will have a value 1 for Adjusted Row Number. Rows 3 and 4 will have a value 3 for Adjusted Row Number and so on…. Step 4: I then used the "Adjusted Row Number" field as the Row identifier in my pivot function and did the pivot. Hope this helps.
title: Pivot Data

body_text: Here's a slightly different method using the Lag function in Rank and Window that avoids pivoting altogether. End result here in 3 steps: Create Row_Number, Product_Odd, and Sales fields via a formulas node as follows. This will have the end result of containing the product value in odd-numbered rows. We're also applying the same approach on Sales (forced to numeric via Value*1 , appearing in even-numbered rows), but we'll only worry about applying a lagged offset for a Products column in the next step. Use the Rank and Window Lag function to "repeat" the Product_Odds field value one row down into a new Product field, which will now correctly correspond to the Sales value within the same row. This step is why we were forced to add a row number in step 1, as Rank and Window requires something to order on and this dataset otherwise has no inherent ordering. Finally, filter the data to only rows where Sales isn't null. All that remains is some column cleanup. Hope this helps!
title: Pivot Data

body_text: I think the main issue here is that there is no relationship established within your data other than row order. Without a column in your data that tells you that rows 1 & 2 relate to other, as do columns 3 & 4, etc, there is no "clean" way to resolve the problem. In this event, pairing rows as you've done in your answer, or applying lag/lead on either of the product/sales field as I've done in mine, are really just different ways of doing the same thing, each of which critically relies on native row order. In the event your data comes into that ETL step out of the order, you'll have chaos. You may want to re-visit your initial data structure, if possible, to mitigate that risk.

body_text: I have a few hundred pivot table cards that are using one value (call it Old Revenue). Our data now has a new column (call it New Revenue) that we want to use to replace the Old Revenue value on all of the pivot tables. Is there any way to do this in bulk, or do I have to replace it on every card, one by one? For the record, I'm using 8-9 different data sets and views, but the Old Revenue column name is standardized across all of them. Same goes for the New Revenue column name.
title: Is there a way to bulk-swap values in Pivot table cards?

body_text: Before anyone asks — I cannot deprecate the Old Revenue column — I still need that column to be able to show users the progression from Old to New.
title: Is there a way to bulk-swap values in Pivot table cards?

body_text: In Domo, there isn’t a direct out-of-the-box bulk edit feature to replace a specific value or column used in multiple existing cards across different datasets or views all at once. However, here are some practical approaches you can consider: 1. Use a Data Pipeline or ETL Approach If possible, modify the underlying datasets or views so that the “Old Revenue” column is replaced or aliased by “New Revenue” at the data preparation layer (for example, in Magic ETL or a SQL transform). With this approach, the cards referencing “Old Revenue” will automatically reflect the updated values without needing to update each card individually, as long as the column name remains the same. 2. Duplicate and Update Datasets with Column Aliasing You can create a new dataset or view that renames “New Revenue” to “Old Revenue” (matching the column name expected by the cards). Then, you can switch the cards to use the new dataset. This method reduces card-level changes, though it does require managing the new dataset. 3. Card-by-Card Update If modifying the datasets isn’t feasible (e.g., due to dataset structure or dependencies), you would need to manually update each pivot table card to replace “Old Revenue” with “New Revenue.” To speed up this process, you could group cards by dataset and open multiple cards in different browser tabs for editing. 4. Use the Domo API for Automation (Advanced) If you have access to development resources, Domo’s REST API allows you to automate card updates programmatically. This would involve: 1. Listing all pivot table cards, 2. Retrieving each card’s configuration, 3. Updating the JSON configuration to replace “Old Revenue” with “New Revenue,” and 4. Pushing the updated configuration back to Domo. This is the only true bulk update method, but it requires programming knowledge and careful testing. Summary: -There is no built-in bulk replace for card fields. -Updating at the data prep level is the most efficient non-API solution. -Otherwise, manual edits or API-based automation are needed.
title: Is there a way to bulk-swap values in Pivot table cards?

body_text: I have a table card that filters names based on a selected campaign name in a slicer card in my dashboard. Currently the table card displays all the names until a campaign name is selected. How can I get the table card to be blank until a campaign name is selected? Thanks for the help in advance.

body_text: You could put something in beast mode to filter the view. On the table card, add a filter like this and set it to 1. The card will only show rows if the campaign has an applied filter. Otherwise, it will be blank. CASE WHEN LENGTH(`Campaign Name`) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
title: Card Display - Table Card Filtering

body_text: Thanks for the reply Arbor.This did not solve my issue. It wanted to do a count instead of showing the names. I did try something like… Case When Length('campaign_name') > 0 then 'campaign_name Else '' End Still shows all the campaign names. I'm wondering if it is an issue with my datatable. (Everything is joined together. See screen shot.) Thanks in advance.
title: Card Display - Table Card Filtering

body_text: I don't think you implemented it the way I intended. I should have added - Then, on the table card itself , add this field as a filter and set it to only include 1 . You could do something like the following, but you will probably get a bunch of blank lines where they are null. Thus, I still believe my first suggestion is better. CASE WHEN campaign_name IN (SELECTED_CAMPAIGN()) THEN company_name ELSE NULL END {where selected_campaign() is the campaign field used in your slicer}

body_text: Domo assumes the default state is “show everything until filtered,” because the philosophy is dashboards should always display some data for readability. So you want is to flip that default, i.e. “show nothing until a slicer is picked” , which Domo doesn’t currently allow for the reasons your rep gave (design principle: always show data). Then the only other trick I can think of would be to create an ETL that adds a dummy row in Magic ETL that only appears when a slicer isn’t applied. Your table can then show a “No Campaign Selected” message instead of data.
title: Card Display - Table Card Filtering

body_text: I have a workflow where if one side of a parallel logic flow ends then I need the whole workflow to stop processing rather still having the other side of the parallel flow continuing to run. The 'End' control doesn't stop the workflow, I need a control that will terminate the whole workflow. The scenario revolves around our Finance team has a task that acknowledges an external party has paid an invoice - one side of the parallel logic, and we need to send out a reminder email every 20 days (up to 4 times) to the account manager to chase up the payment if it hasn't been made - the other side of the parallel logic. Once the payment is made then workflow is complete and we no longer need to send out reminders - hence I need to then terminate the workflow.
title: Ending a workflow when in parallel logic

body_text: @JohnXClifton - the best way to handle this is not with a parallel gateway, but rather a non-interrupting timer on the user task. If you go to the user task, in the config pane on the right you'll see a timers tab. Create a recurring timer, that is non-interrupting (interrupting timer voids the user task, non-interrupting does not) that time cycles whatever number of times you want it to. This will create a new pathway off of the user task. You can put your reminders there. Once the user task is completed, it moves on the timers are no longer a thing. LMK if that doesn't make sense.
title: Ending a workflow when in parallel logic

body_text: Thanks Dan. I've tested that option and it works as per my requirements, so that's another problem solved!
title: Ending a workflow when in parallel logic

body_text: Hello Team, Calling DOMO experts! We need help on building applications and workflows in DOMO.Use case: Inside DOMO we have cards with filters on data. We want to send these filters as SQL query or JSON payload to snowflake.Please reach out if anyone has worked on similar use case. Regards, Ritesh
title: Building application with DOMO

body_text: You could build an app using JavaScript and the Domo SDK to read page or card filters with the filtersChanged event. Format the filters as SQL or JSON. Then call Snowflake. You can find code examples of filtersChanged on the web and in Domo Community Forum posts. Another way may be to use a workflow to take the inputs and pass them to a Snowflake connector. Or use Domo's API to extract the filters. Via the API you should be able to read the card definition and save filters. domo.onFiltersChanged(function(filters) { console.log("Filters updated:", filters); // Example filter object: // [ // { column: "Region", operator: "EQUALS", values: ["West"] }, // { column: "Date", operator: "GREATER_THAN", values: ["2024-01-01"] } // ] // Convert to SQL WHERE clause let whereClauses = filters.map(f => { if (f.operator === "EQUALS") return `${f.column} = '${f.values[0]}'`; if (f.operator === "GREATER_THAN") return `${f.column} > '${f.values[0]}'`; return ""; }); let sql = `SELECT * FROM MY_TABLE WHERE ${whereClauses.join(" AND ")}`; console.log(sql); // Optionally send this SQL to your backend/workflow });
title: Building application with DOMO

body_text: I am creating a table chart type and I can pull in a column for ID's and they show properly. When I pull in a quick filter and select the range of numbers to be displayed, it shows them in standard deviation. How can I fix this so I am able to add a quick filter for all order id's? Data type is a FLOAT so it pulls in as a measure in analyzer. Shows properly on table but not the quick filter. Any suggestions?
title: Range filter showing as standard deviation.

body_text: Domo is treating it as a measure instead of a dimension because it is stored as a float. That's why your quick filter is showing standard deviation (measure aggregation). Use Magic ETL to add a step to convert your Order ID from a float to a string or text. Something like CONCAT(ROUND(OrderID, 0), '') If you need to keep your original as a float, just use the formula to add another field. That should make the ids function as a list instead of a numeric range.
title: Range filter showing as standard deviation.

body_text: Thanks! Will try that out.
title: Range filter showing as standard deviation.

body_text: Problem Statement When using Domo to display % distributions over time (e.g., offer volume % by category), the platform recalculates percentages per time slice . This makes a value like 25% appear at different vertical positions in different periods if the total changes. The result is misleading visuals and makes trend analysis and cross-period comparisons less accurate. Scenario: Offer Volume % by Calculator Name Month Total Offers Category A Offers Actual % for A Jan 100 25 25% Feb 10,000 2500 25% Mar 300 75 25% Apr 50,000 12,500 25% Expectation: In a line or bar chart, all four months for Category A should be plotted at the same horizontal Y-axis level (25%) since we are trying to look at the % distribution trend. Reality in Domo’s Current Behaviour: Because each month’s % is recalculated independently for its bar or stack, the visual position for 25% shifts up or down depending on each month’s internal scaling. This makes it look like Category A is growing or shrinking when in fact it’s completely stable. Benefits Clarity : Consistent, comparable percentages across periods. Efficiency : No need for Beast Modes or ETL pre-processing. Accessibility : Business users can achieve accurate visuals without technical help. Flexibility : Works for any chart type, not just stacked bars. Desired Output Screenshot 2025-08-11 155432.png Current Output Screenshot 2025-08-11 155342.png Case Reference: 05908705
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Consistent Percentage Scaling Option for All Charts in Domo

body_text: I have a source that drops a csv file into my S3 bucket daily. I import data into Domo using the AWS S3 connector. The source periodically changes the header names which is super annoying. But now I have rows where there is no data. For example, new files starting 7/1 has a column for "Line Name" but previously, that column was just called "Line". Now data that was in the "Line" column are gone. Any suggestions for how to handle this so that if the source changes the header again, I would retain past data?
title: Header in csv files (via S3 connector) keep changing

body_text: I'd be talking to the vendor or source person generating the file and ask them to standardize their output. Sounds like someone who doesn't have much experience. body_text: One of the pain points we have with using the Virtual Datasets tool in Governance Toolkit is that jobs are not editable, and if the federation fails, you have to recreate the job. So the first thing we need is for jobs to be editable. The second thing we need is for jobs to be able compare the name of the dataset in the federating instance with the name of the dataset in the receiving instance so that if the name of the dataset changes in the federating instance, the toolkit will update the name in the receiving instance to match. This would be configurable on a dataset-by-dataset basis and we should be able to set the default to either checked or not checked. The third thing we need is a setting that will make it so that the Virtual Datasets tool will not let you federate a dataset that has already been federated to the receiving instance and still exists in that instance. Currently, because the default behavior is to allow you to federate the same dataset as many times as you want to, there is no easy way to check to make sure it hasn't already been federated before federating it again. Especially since someone can change the name of the dataset in either instance, people may think the dataset they need hasn't been federated and request that it be federated. Which means we have to resort to joining the federation logs to other datasets in order to determine whether the dataset has already been federated or not, and if so, point them to the right place. The fourth thing is we need to be able to un-federate a dataset using the Virtual Datasets tool. Domo Publish has the ability to un-publish and delete the content from the subscriber instance, so the Virtual Datasets tool needs to be able to do that too.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Virtual Datasets in Governance Toolkit Enhancements

body_text: Hi folks, I have a field that contains JSON-encoded text representing client-defined fields in our application. The data in here is custom user profile fields defined differently by each of thousands of clients. For example, one client will have an object that looks like: {"gender": "whatever", "suffix": null, "facebook": null, "linkedin": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/whoever/"} And a different client will have an object that looks like: {"job_title": "Analyst", "company_name": "Acme Bank", "why_join": "I joined to network, learn, and advocate for our industry."} So the key thing to understand here is that the fields encoded in the JSON differ per client. All clients get the same set of dashboards, drawn from the same datasets, filtered to their own data in a Domo app that we embed on the clients' sites (so our external application embeds the Domo app and includes a filter to a client ID when we call it). Our goal: we'd like to allow clients to filter the dashboards by these custom fields. We could flatten them using an ETL, but we would be adding thousands of columns to a dataset, meaning thousands of filters visible to clients on the dataset. It would be hard for clients to find their own fields and they would see the names of other clients' custom fields. And aside from those already-unacceptable issues, I don't know how well Domo would handle that many filters on a dashboard. One solution, if there's a way to do it, would be to flatten the JSON objects in an ETL (creating a dataset with thousands of columns) and then filter columnwise by client in the embedded version of the app. I don't know if there's a way for an external app to filter columnwise when embedding a Domo app. Another solution I could imagine would be an app that somehow builds the columns dynamically from the JSON object based on the data that it finds after we filter. So first, we have our embedded app which only displays the client's data in their view of the dashboards. Then our app uses some kind of magic to build out columns in the underlying dataset from only the pre-filtered data, so we end up with columns for only the client's custom user profile fields. We don't want to build out separate dashboards per client or separate datasets per client. Clients aren't logging into Domo in our solution, so the beta columnwise PDP feature isn't an option. If anyone has any ideas for our situation here, they would be much appreciated! All the best, Andy
title: Filtering a dashboard based on a JSON object with a large number of encoded fields

body_text: You definitely don't want to flatten that JSON into thousands of columns - it just won’t scale, and it creates all sorts of usability and performance issues. Instead, I’d look at converting the JSON into a key-value pair structure, and include client/user identifiers. That way, you end up with two datasets: one for your core metrics (tied to client and user), and one for the custom fields. You can then join them in a Domo ETL on client_id and user_id. So something like: client_id,user_id,key,value 123,1,gender,whatever 123,1,suffix,null 123,1,linkedin,url_path 456,2,job_title,Analyst 456,2,company,Acme Bank This avoids the explosion of columns and keeps things flexible as different clients have different fields. Since your users aren't logging into Domo directly, you'd likely handle filtering outside the dashboards - maybe in your embedded app - by querying just the custom fields for that client and letting them choose what they want to filter by. Then you’d pass those filters into the embedded dashboard via the Domo embed SDK or URL params. It’ll take some custom wiring on your side, but this keeps it scalable and avoids maintaining separate dashboards or datasets per client.
title: Filtering a dashboard based on a JSON object with a large number of encoded fields

body_text: The current method of creating tags within Domo is quite straightforward and simple, and probably for many smaller organisations the ability for anyone to create a new tag would be quite useful. The lack of control over the different variations of tags in larger organisations though can result in things becoming messy. Especially when the Tag is too long for the display (similar to the issue identified here Improve Readability for Long Column Headers in Color Rules Dialog) , users are unable to see the one they are after if the beginning of the tag is the same for multiple. For example, when tagging something as "Technical Data Steward: " then a particular area, can make it difficult to identify the correct tag. The only way is select the one you think it is, then save it. If it's wrong, you would need to return into the dialog and pick another. Ideally these issues would be fixed in 2 ways: 1. Increase the width of the Tag Dialog popup - Additional space could be added by having the Tag list and the Tags on this Dataset above/below each other rather than side-by-side 2. Add a control into the Admin settings that would prevent the creation of new tags unless they have a certain grant or role (possibly selectable under the setting), preventing users from creating multiple versions of what should be the same tag. This would leave the ability for all users to create new tags in instances for those organisations that would like to keep that option.
tags: Submitted and awaiting review from product team
title: Control of Dataset Tags within the instance

body_text: Hi everyone 👋, I'm currently working on a custom Domo app and trying to fetch data from a dataset using ryuu.js with a GET request like this: domo.get('/data/v1/dataset/YOUR_DATASET_ID?limit=20') .then(data => { console.log('Fetched data:', data); // Use the data in your app }) .catch(error => { console.error('Error fetching dataset:', error); }); From what I understand: There's no need to manually set headers or authorization tokens — Domo handles that automatically. I’ve replaced YOUR_DATASET_ID with the actual ID from my dataset ID. However, the issue I'm facing is that this request still seems to be pointing to localhost instead of Domo’s environment, and I can’t figure out why and i'm use ReactJS. 😕 Has anyone encountered this issue before? Any ideas on what I might be missing or misconfigured? Any help would be greatly appreciated! Thanks, Priyank
title: Get Dataset information using ryuu.js lib

body_text: Your GET request is pointing at localhost instead of Domo's backend API because of where it is running. You are running your app locally so it points at local development environment. In production, when the app is hosted, it will probably route the API request domo.get() as you expect. Check to see if there is a ryuu CLI to preview locally. Otherwise, you may need to deploy the app to see it properly.
title: Get Dataset information using ryuu.js lib

body_text: I'm not looking to solve your entire problem, but this may help you with the blank brick display example. Go to AppStore and search Blank Brick. Create as a new dashboard. Edit the brick and enter the following in the Javascript section: var domo = window.domo; var datasets = window.datasets; // Target end-of-month dates from the image const targetDates = [ "31-Jan-25", "28-Feb-25", "31-Mar-25", "30-Apr-25", "31-May-25", "30-Jun-25", "31-Jul-25" ]; // Diff headers (vs 31-Jul-25) const diffHeaders = [ "31-Jan-25 vs. 31-Jul-25", "28-Feb-25 vs. 31-Jul-25", "31-Mar-25 vs. 31-Jul-25", "30-Apr-25 vs. 31-Jul-25", "31-May-25 vs. 31-Jul-25", "30-Jun-25 vs. 31-Jul-25" ]; // Fetch data from Domo domo.get(`/data/v1/${datasets[0]}`).then(function(data) { // Build country -> date -> headcount map const map = {}; data.forEach(row => { const date = row.Date; const country = row.Country; const headcount = Number(row.Headcount); if (!targetDates.includes(date)) return; if (!map[country]) map[country] = {}; map[country][date] = headcount; }); // Start building HTML let html = " "; // Header row 1 html += ` Country Headcount Headcount Difference `; // Header row 2 html += " "; targetDates.forEach(d => html += ` ${d} `); diffHeaders.forEach(d => html += ` ${d} `); html += " "; // Data rows Object.keys(map).forEach(country => { const row = map[country]; let htmlRow = ` ${country} `; // Headcounts for target dates const values = targetDates.map(d => row[d] ?? 0); values.forEach(v => htmlRow += ` ${v} `); // Differences vs. 31-Jul-25 const july = values[6]; for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { const diff = july - values[i]; const cls = diff > 0 ? "diff-positive" : diff < 0 ? "diff-negative" : ""; htmlRow += ` ${diff} `; } htmlRow += " "; html += htmlRow; }); html += " "; // Render to page document.getElementById("result").innerHTML = html; }); In the html section: And in the css section: table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 12px; text-align: center; } th, td { border: 1px solid #ccc; padding: 6px; } th { background-color: #000; color: #fff; } th[colspan="7"] { background-color: #333; } th[colspan="6"] { background-color: #0075a2; } th:first-child, td:first-child { background-color: #c4f0c5; font-weight: bold; color: #000; } .diff-positive { color: green; } .diff-negative { color: red; } Set the dataset below to your dataset. It will load as dataset0.
title: Customized Pivot Table Card

body_text: Updated Javascript: var domo = window.domo; var datasets = window.datasets; domo.get(`/data/v1/${datasets[0]}`).then(function(data) { // Group by Country and Date const byCountry = {}; const allDates = new Set(); data.forEach(row => { const date = row.Date.trim(); const country = row.Country.trim(); const headcount = Number(row.Headcount); if (!byCountry[country]) byCountry[country] = {}; byCountry[country][date] = headcount; allDates.add(date); }); // Sort dates descending (latest first) const sortedDates = Array.from(allDates).sort((a, b) => new Date(b) - new Date(a)); // Get latest 7 unique month-end dates const targetDates = sortedDates.slice(0, 7).reverse(); // oldest to newest const latestDate = targetDates[targetDates.length - 1]; // current/latest // Build table let html = " "; // Headers html += ` Country Headcount Headcount Difference ${targetDates.map(d => ` ${d} `).join("")} ${targetDates.slice(0, 6).map(d => ` ${d} vs. ${latestDate} `).join("")} `; // Body Object.keys(byCountry).forEach(country => { let row = ` ${country} `; const hc = targetDates.map(d => byCountry[country][d] ?? 0); hc.forEach(val => row += ` ${val} `); const current = hc[6]; // latest headcount for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { const diff = current - hc[i]; const cls = diff > 0 ? body_text: We are receiving a cross origin access error while embeding domo as an iframe into our portal. As a work around If we disable the xframe options check then it is working as expected How can we fix this ?
title: Receiving unable to connect unless we disable Xframe options check

body_text: Because your website and domo are coming from different domains by default you'll get the CORS error which is a standard security check to make sure you're not attempting to access a website from a completely different website. This is to avoid click-jacking attacks. There isn't a way to avoid this except for turning off the xframe options like you're doing.
title: Receiving unable to connect unless we disable Xframe options check

body_text: Where did you turn off xframe options??

body_text: Hi all! I'm looking for help to create an ETL from which I can create a pivot table to track when people are in town through our organization to have a guest census by month. I've attached test data. The values in the test data are personID, ActualArrivalDate, DepartDate, and Housing. I'd like the result to look like this, tracking personID by month. A personID would be listed for every month between the person's arrival date and depart date. If there is not a depart date for the personID, the ID would continue to be a result each month beyond the arrival date in the table: Test Data Guest Census.xlsx Thank you for any help!
title: Track length of visit on pivot table

body_text: To track guests month-by-month in Magic ETL, you could start by loading your guest data and adding a constant field like DefaultEndDate (e.g., 2026-02-29) using an Add Constants tile or formula tile. Then use a Formula tile to create a new field called FinalDepartDate with the formula: CASE WHEN DepartDate IS NULL THEN DefaultEndDate ELSE DepartDate END This fills in missing departure dates for ongoing guests. Next, join your guest data to a calendar dataset that has one row per month (e.g., the first of each month). Use a join tile with this condition: Date >= ActualArrivalDate AND Date <= FinalDepartDate This generates one row per guest per month they were present. Use another Formula tile to extract the month in YYYY-MM format, and then group by Housing and Month, counting distinct Person IDs. The final dataset should show monthly guest counts by housing type, ready for use in a pivot table.
title: Track length of visit on pivot table

body_text: Thank you so much for your help! Overall, this solution helped me achieve my goal. One issue I found with this is that when I selected the calendar dataset with the first day of each month and then joined it with the statement Date >= ActualArrivalDate AND Date <= FinalDepartDate it captured all people who arrived before that date and still in town, but those that arrived after the date on a later day of the month were not included in the month's count. I therefore did not limit the calendar dataset and joined, creating many rows for each guest. I then used a beast mode to the count the distinct number of guests per month in the pivot table card, which appears to be accurate. Is there a better way to do this? Thank you again - this was so helpful!
title: Track length of visit on pivot table

body_text: Instead of joining only on the first of each month, use a calendar that has one row per day . Join using: `Date` BETWEEN `ActualArrivalDate` AND `FinalDepartDate` Then extract the month DATE_FORMAT(`Date`, 'YYYY-MM') And group by month and housing with count on distinct person ID.
title: Track length of visit on pivot table

title: Automatically Default Date Filter to Month Start – Max Available Date

body_text: The problem with doing a filter for month to date is that you can only do that for the current month. If you need the max date from the data, I'm afraid you probably have to create an ETL using a rank tile or max(date) formula and append that max date back to the dataset. You could then use a formula such as CASE WHEN `date_field` >= DATE_FORMAT(`max_date_value`, '%Y-%m-01') AND `date_field` <= `max_date_value` THEN 'In Range' ELSE 'Out of Range' END to know what is within scope.
title: Automatically Default Date Filter to Month Start – Max Available Date
